sections.title: Rolling 12-month board

items.evidence: Ran: node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/layout.test.js → '# pass 93 / # fail 0'. Rows '1.1 — twelve month columns, always, in one model' (tests/tier1/layout.test.js:41, asserts MONTHS_VISIBLE===12, cols.length===12, keys 2026-01…2026-12) and '1.1/1.3 — rolling mode starts at TODAY's month, ignoring startMonth' (:186). items.text: When I open the app, I see the current month plus the next 11 as vertical day columns on one screen, so the whole planning horizon is visible without any clicks.

items.clause: headers in the reference format (e.g., `August '26`)

defence.reason: The finding stands and the auditor's citations are accurate. The on-screen column header is built from `col.label`, which layout.js constructs as the first three letters of the month name plus a typographic apostrophe and two-digit year ("Aug ’26"); the full name ("August 2026") exists only as `fullLabel` and reaches the user solely as the hover `title` of the header, the scratchpad aria-label, and the print page banner. No CSS pseudo-element or transform adds the full name back (`.col-head::after` is only the today-dot; print.css:90 restyles the head but does not change its text), so the printed column heads read "Aug ’26" as well. I searched docs/v2 (AUDIT, V2-FINAL, FINDINGS, STATUS, E*-VERIFICATION, adr/), tests/COVERAGE.md and the git log for any design decision adopting the 3-letter form and found none; the abbreviation is unchanged since the v1 baseline commit 66126e9 and item 1.A is not mentioned by any prior audit ledger. The second clause (short months leave their bottom rows empty, as a contiguous void tail) holds and is pinned at tier 1 and tier 2. Shell choice is irrelevant: this is web-layer rendering identical in both shells. Sharpening: (a) the abbreviation is pinned three times at tier 1 and once at tier 2 as *intended* behaviour, so this is a spec-vs-implementation conflict, not an accident — resolving it needs either a catalogue erratum (accept "Aug ’26") or a code+test change in layout.js:847, tests/tier1/layout.test.js:129-138, tests/tier1/repeats-find-i18n.test.js:1044-1060 and the regex at tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js:309; (b) note the catalogue's own 10.4 wording already uses "Aug '26" for the same month, and the catalogue's example uses a straight apostrophe where the app uses ’ — both point toward the catalogue example being loose, but the catalogue says the specs govern, so PARTIAL is the correct carry until the PO rules.
defence.evidence: Header text: src/js/layout.js:847 `label: \`${MN[mo.m - 1].slice(0, 3)} ’${String(mo.y).slice(2)}\`` and :848 `fullLabel: \`${MN[mo.m - 1]} ${mo.y}\``; MN is MONTH_DE/MONTH_EN (layout.js:542). Rendering: src/js/board.js:628-632 `buildHead` appends a span with `col.label` and sets `head.title = col.fullLabel`; patchColumn (:643-645) rebuilds via the same function. fullLabel's only other consumers: board.js:702 and :1269 (scratchpad label/aria-label) and src/js/print.js:85 (print page banner "Januar 2026 – Dezember 2026"), not the column head. CSS: src/css/app.css:218-230 `.col-head` has `overflow:hidden`, `::after` is the today-dot only; src/css/print.css:90-94 restyles the head in @media print without touching its text — printed heads are also "Aug ’26". Tests pinning the abbreviation as intended: tests/tier1/layout.test.js:129 row 'column labels: short in the head, full for the tooltip' asserts label 'Jan ’26'/'Mär ’26' and fullLabel 'Januar 2026'; tests/tier1/repeats-find-i18n.test.js:1044 row 'German column heads are the first three letters, umlaut included' asserts the full 12-array including 'Aug ’26'; :1053 row 'English column heads use the English three-letter forms'; tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js:294 row '1.1/1.2 · twelve columns, each headed by its own month, in order' asserts head.textContent === m.cols[i].label (:302), head.title === fullLabel (:303) and regex /^[A-Za-zÄÖÜäöü]{3} ’\d\d$/ (:309) — passed in the real WKWebView run at HEAD. Second clause verified: tests/tier1/layout.test.js:67 row '1.6 — every column is exactly 31 rows; short months pad at the BOTTOM' (asserts firstVoid === c.len and tail all void; Feb len 28); tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js:319 row '1.2 · 372 day rows: one per calendar day, the rest padded as .void'. Ran: `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/layout.test.js` → "ok 3 - 1.6 — every column is exactly 31 rows; short months pad at the BOTTOM", "ok 8 - column labels: short in the head, full for the tooltip", "# pass 93 / # fail 0". No design decision found: `grep -rn -i "abbreviat|slice(0, 3)|three-letter|reference format" docs src tests` returns only the code, the tests above and catalogue lines 18/23/119; `git log -S"slice(0, 3)} ’" -- src/js/layout.js` → only 66126e9 "v1 baseline — LangzeitPlaner 1.0 as handed over"; docs/v2/adr/* and AUDIT/V2-FINAL/FINDINGS/STATUS/E*-VERIFICATION carry no 1.A entry. Catalogue self-reference: docs/v2/UX-AUDIT-CATALOGUE.md:119 (10.4) itself writes "Aug '26 and Aug '27".

defence.reason: The finding stands. The on-screen month header is the 3-letter abbreviated form ('Aug ’26'), not the catalogue's reference format ('August ’26'); the full month name exists only as the hover title. No alternate render path (print, toolbar) shows the full name in a column header, and both test tiers pin the abbreviated form. The second clause (short months leave bottom rows empty) is verified PASS at tier 1 (run) and tier 2 (assertion read). Sharpening: the abbreviation is unchanged since the v1 baseline commit 66126e9, so it is inherited v1 behaviour rather than a v2 regression; DESIGN-DECISIONS.md carries no entry justifying it; the v1 spec §5 the catalogue cites is not in the repo, so the catalogue wording is the only auditable reference. Shell-independent (pure web layer). Verdict remains PARTIAL: clause 2 holds, clause 1 fails as worded — resolvable either by a catalogue erratum accepting 'Mon ’YY' or by changing layout.js:847 plus the pinned assertions.

items.evidence: src/css/app.css:209-211 `.board-wrap { flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-x:auto; overflow-y:auto; }` — the scroller allows vertical scroll; no code scales row height to the viewport (grep for ResizeObserver/'resize' in src/js hits only legend.js and interact.js). src/js/settings.js:305-320 computes need = 31×rowH + 26 + 62 against .board-wrap.clientHeight and shows the warning 'the scratchpad and roughly the last N day rows of every month fall below the fold and have to be scrolled to'. Chrome: src/css/app.css:89 titlebar 28 px, :111 toolbar 40 px → default rows (22 px, src/js/store.js:321) need a window ≥ 839 px; src-tauri/tauri.conf.json sets minHeight 640 (board-wrap 571 px → ~9 rows below the fold). tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js:436-447 row '1.4 · month headers are sticky…' itself branches on `wrap.scrollHeight > wrap.clientHeight + 20` and scrolls vertically when true. Fit mechanisms present: src/js/layout.js:381-383 rowCapacity, :731-740 capacity slice → overflow '+n', popover (src/js/popover.js).
items.note: The fit mechanisms (row density, truncation, +n popovers) exist and are what keep 31 rows on screen at the default 1440×900 window (61 px spare). But 'never' does not hold: the shipped Tauri window can be resized to 640 px and a 13" 1440×900 display with menu bar and Dock cannot host an 839 px window, so at default density the last 1–2 rows scroll on exactly the machine 1.4 names. The product admits this in its own settings copy. Not listed in docs/v2/AUDIT.md's residual ledger (no hit for 'vertical'/'overflow-y'). A tier-2 row asserting `.board-wrap` never scrolls vertically at the Tauri minimum window height does not exist and would go red today.
items.clause: The board never scrolls vertically

defence.reason: The finding stands; I could not refute it. The clause "The board never scrolls vertically" does not hold in the shipped Tauri build. (1) The scroller is explicitly a vertical scroller: src/css/app.css:210 `.board-wrap { flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-x:auto; overflow-y:auto; }` inside `.app { height:100vh }` (app.css:86). (2) Board height is fixed by settings, never by the viewport: layout.js:551 `rowH = max(dp.minRowHeight, s.rowHeight || dp.rowHeight)` → board.js:281 `setVar('--row-h', model.rowH)` → board.js:601 `rows.style.height = 'calc(var(--row-h) * 31)'`; a grep of src/js for ResizeObserver/'resize'/innerHeight/clientHeight hits only legend.js (legend width), popover.js (close/clamp) and interact.js (bar-edge drag kind 'resize'), plus settings.js:307 which only *measures* to warn. (3) Geometry: at the default 22 px row (store.js:321) the board content needs 31×22 + 26 (--head-h) + 14 (.pad margin-top, app.css:787) + 62 (--pad-h) = 784 px; chrome above it is 28 (titlebar, app.css:89) + 40 (toolbar, :111) + 1 px border = 69 px → a window of ≥ 853 px. tauri.conf.json:19 permits minHeight 640 (board-wrap 571 px → 213 px short ≈ 9.7 day rows below the fold), and the Swift reference shell has the same floor (main.swift:2052 `minSize 900×640`), so the two shells agree and there is no shell-mismatch escape. (4) The product itself admits it scrolls: settings.js:308-314 computes `need = 31*rowNow + 26 + 62` against `.board-wrap.clientHeight` and renders "…fall below the fold and have to be scrolled to". (5) Tier 2 pins the admission, not the promise: tests/tier2/density-808.dom.js row '§8 · the vertical cost is measured against this window and said out loud' asserts the warning appears *exactly when* need > have and is non-vacuous (some configurations warn) — i.e. the passing suite proves configurations where content exceeds the scroller; tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js:433-443 row '1.4 · month headers are sticky…' branches on `wrap.scrollHeight > wrap.clientHeight + 20` and sets `wrap.scrollTop = 60` when true. No tier-2 row asserts overflowY !== 'auto' or scrollHeight ≤ clientHeight at any window height. Docs: E9-VERIFICATION.md:398-402 already calls the vertical cost "honest and the pane says it"; AUDIT.md's residual ledger has no entry for it. Sharpening: the auditor's "61 px spare at 1440×900" omits the pad's 14 px margin-top — real spare is 47 px, and the same omission sits in settings.js:308 (the warning under-states the shortfall by 14 px; density-808 §8 encodes the identical formula so it does not catch it). Direction of the finding is unchanged. Second clause (fit via row density, truncation, +n popovers) genuinely holds: layout.js:381-383 rowCapacity, :731-740 capacity slice → overflow '+n', popover.js. So PARTIAL, failing clause "never scrolls vertically".

defence.reason: The auditor's PARTIAL is confirmed on the clause "The board never scrolls vertically"; the second clause ("vertical fit is achieved by row density, truncation, and popovers") holds. I looked for a fit-to-viewport mechanism, a Tauri-shell window constraint, and a tier-2 row that asserts the absence of vertical scroll, and found none. (1) The scroller is explicitly allowed to scroll vertically: src/css/app.css:209-211 `.board-wrap { flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-x:auto; overflow-y:auto; }`. (2) Row height is never derived from the viewport. src/js/layout.js:551 `const rowH = Math.max(dp.minRowHeight, s.rowHeight || dp.rowHeight)` clamps only to the density preset's floor (kompakt 18, komfort 26; layout.js:82-99), and src/js/board.js:281 writes that value straight to `--row-h`. The only ResizeObserver/'resize' listeners in src/js are legend.js:398-403 (legend width), popover.js:110/176 (close popover) and interact.js:356/481 (bar resize drag) — none touch row height. (3) The shipped Tauri shell permits a window in which the board must scroll: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:16-19 width 1440, height 900, minWidth 900, minHeight 640; src-tauri/src/lib.rs has no window-size code at all. shell-macos/main.swift:2052 sets the same 900x640 minimum, so the shells agree. With `* { box-sizing: border-box }` (app.css:65), titlebar 28 px (app.css:89) and toolbar 40 px (app.css:111), a 640 px window leaves board-wrap 572 px; the board needs 31·rowH + 26 + 62 (app.css:40-46 tokens; settings.js:308) = 770 px at the default 22 px (store.js:321), 646 px even at the Kompakt floor of 18 px. So at minimum height the last ~9 rows (default) or ~5 rows (smallest permitted density) plus the scratchpad are below the fold and reachable only by vertical scroll. Default 1440x900 fits with 61 px spare. (4) The product itself states the overflow: src/js/settings.js:305-315 measures `.board-wrap.clientHeight` against `need` and shows "…fall below the fold and have to be scrolled to". (5) The tier-2 suite pins that warning, not the absence of scroll: tests/tier2/density-808.dom.js §8 row 'the vertical cost is measured against this window and said out loud' asserts the biconditional warned === (need > have), with its own comment (lines 725-747) acknowledging that the harness cannot change the WKWebView height. tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js:436-447 row '1.4 · month headers are sticky…' branches on `wrap.scrollHeight > wrap.clientHeight + 20` and, when true, sets `wrap.scrollTop = 60` and asserts the header stays pinned — i.e. it tests behaviour UNDER vertical scroll. No row asserts overflowY none/hidden or scrollHeight <= clientHeight. (6) Not in any residual ledger: no hit for vertical/overflow-y/below the fold in docs/v2/AUDIT.md, STATUS.md, FINDINGS.md, MOM-TEST.md; tests/COVERAGE.md:40 maps only 1.4 (horizontal). The v1 F1 note the catalogue cites is not present in the repo (only quoted in settings.js:296-297 and density-808.dom.js:731), so the catalogue wording governs. defence.reason: The auditor's PARTIAL is correct and, if anything, understated. Two of the three clauses hold with verified evidence: (a) "clicking expands a popover with the full stack" — tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js row '2.4 · clicking the +n chip opens the popover with the FULL stack' asserts every one of 4 note texts is listed after a real click on .d-more (chip text '+2'), and src/js/interact.js:416-420 routes the click to openDayPopover; (b) "narrow columns never silently hide entries" — layout.js:740-745 computes hidden = queue.slice(noteSlots) and overflow = hidden.length + laneOverflow[d], so every folded note AND every folded bar is counted into the chip; tier-1 'capacity reaches the model…' asserts overflow === 4 - cap for rowHeight 18/20/22/26/32 and tier-2 asserts chip text `+${5-cap}` for 18/22/32. The rule is rowCapacity(rowH, metric) = clamp(floor((rowH-1)/lineH),1,3) (src/js/layout.js:381-383), and the shown count is noteSlots = capacity - holidayLines (layout.js:734-740). This deviates from "first two" in two concrete situations: (1) the auditor's slider case — Kompakt rowHeight 18–21 px gives capacity 1 (tier-1 layout.test.js:287 pins [18,1],[20,1]; tier-2 row loops rowHeight 18 → shown.length === 1, chip '+4'); the product even tells the user so in the settings hint (settings.js:277-279: "unter 21 px trägt jeder Tag nur eine Zeile"); (2) NOT in the auditor's evidence — at the SHIPPED default (Kompakt 22 px, capacity 2) a day that is a shown public holiday gets holidayLines = 1 (layout.js:737: `if (capacity >= 2 || notesHere.length === 0) holidayLines = 1`), so a crowded holiday shows the holiday name on line 1 plus ONE note plus "+n". tests/tier1/layout.test.js row 'a shown holiday DOES cost a note slot at capacity 2' (line 973-983) asserts d.notes.length === 1 and d.overflow === 2 for three notes on 2026-01-01 at rowHeight 22, and it passes at HEAD (ran: node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/layout.test.js → "ok 3 - a shown holiday DOES cost a note slot at capacity 2", 93 pass / 0 fail). Clause 2 ("clicking expands a popover with the full stack") and clause 3 ("narrow columns never silently hide entries") HOLD: every hidden note and every undrawn bar is counted into one +n badge (layout.js:744-746, board.js:911-912) and the chip opens the full stack (interact.js:417-421 → openDayPopover; tier-2 row asserts all 4 texts present). Clause 1 ("shows the first two notes") holds at every shipped default — Kompakt 22 px, the whole Komfort range 26–32 px, A4 paper 20 px and A3 paper 29 px all compute capacity 2 (I ran rowCapacity over every slider value and both paper metrics: kompakt 22..32 → 2, komfort 26..32 → 2, a4 → 2, a3 → 2) — but it is not literally true in two reachable states, so PARTIAL is right. (a) The auditor's slider caveat is real but the range is wrong: Kompakt 18, 19, 20 AND 21 px all give capacity 1 (floor((21-1)/10.5)=1), so the low-density range showing ONE note plus +n is 18–21, not 18–20; the settings hint at settings.js:278 says "unter 21 px", which itself misses 21 (COVERAGE.md discrepancy 3 records the same missing-21 defect in the design table). (b) A second, stronger deviation the auditor did not record occurs AT THE SHIPPED DEFAULT: when the Feiertage layer shows a holiday on a crowded day, the holiday keeps line 1 and the row shows ONE note plus +n (layout.js:737-740 noteSlots = capacity - holidayLines; tier-1 row "a shown holiday DOES cost a note slot at capacity 2" asserts notes.length 1, overflow 2 at rowHeight 22 — passes). Nothing is dropped (the note is counted in +n and listed in the popover), so clause 3 survives, but "first two notes" does not describe that row. Minor note, not a defect: on a family board the two shown notes are ordered mine-before-theirs (layout.js:498-501 orderForCapacity), so they are not necessarily the first two in store order; the catalogue's "first two" does not define its order, so I do not count this against the clause. Both shells share this JS; nothing here is shell-level, so Tauri vs Swift does not affect the verdict.

items.note: Edit, delete and per-note category (colour dot, name on hover) all hold. The failing clause: the popover row uses the same nowrap/ellipsis rule as the board, in a fixed 214 px card; after padding, dot, gaps and the three .act buttons roughly 150 px of 10 px type remain (~30 characters), so an 80-character note is visibly clipped inside the popover too. Confidence medium because the pixel budget is computed from the CSS, not measured in a browser; the tier-2 rows assert DOM textContent, not visible width.

defence.reason: The finding stands and is sharpened from a CSS-derived estimate to a browser measurement. Three of the four clauses hold in the shipped code: in-place edit (popover.js:412-414 click on .txt → startEdit; :636-660 input with maxLength 80, Enter/blur commit, empty commit deletes, Escape abandons), delete (popover.js:452-461 ✕ → store.apply('deleteNotePopover')), and per-note category (popover.js:322-324 dot painted with colorOf(category.paletteRef), dot.title = category.name). The clause "offers full note texts" fails visibly: app.css:917-920 gives .pop-row .txt `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` inside the 214 px .popover (app.css:899), no later rule or JS overrides it (grep of src/css, index.html, popover.js: only one .pop-row .txt rule; print.css:20 merely hides the popover on paper), and a standalone page built from those exact rules measures the .txt box at 147 px: a 78-character note needs 365 px (Ubuntu) / 392 px (system fallback), so it is clipped to under half its width with an ellipsis; even a 30-character note clips in the fallback font. The fallback case is the fresh-install case, because Ubuntu is not bundled (index.html:10 leaves it as a TODO). The full text is reachable only via the hover title (txt.title = n.text, popover.js:413) or by clicking into the edit input — the same hover mechanism the board already has (2.5), so the popover adds nothing for text beyond the board. The tier-2 rows the auditor cites (dom-rendering '2.4 · clicking the +n chip opens the popover with the FULL stack' at tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js:830-834; retrofit-probe2 Q4 rows) assert textContent and .dot count, never visible width, so they do not contradict this. Verdict PARTIAL is right; confidence should be raised to high since the pixel budget is now measured in WebKit rather than computed. No shell-level behaviour is involved, so Swift vs Tauri does not bear on this item.

defence.reason: The auditor is right and the clipping is now measured, not only computed. The popover's own header (src/js/popover.js:1-3) promises "full note texts", and the row does carry the full string (popover.js:335 rowText, :412 txt.title = n.text), but src/css/app.css:917-920 applies the board's nowrap/hidden/ellipsis rule to `.pop-row .txt` inside the fixed 214 px `.popover` (app.css:900), and nothing overrides it: no rule in src/css, index.html or family/sharing.js:SHARING_CSS (lines 485-547) touches `.pop-row .txt`, and popover.js sets no width or white-space (only :474 dot.style.width). Rendered in the WebKit browser pane with a verbatim copy of app.css:900-924 and an 80-character note, the text element measures clientWidth 165 / scrollWidth 367 (solo row, ↻ ✕) and 145 / 367 (family row with the share trigger) — clipped: true, ~36 / ~32 characters visible, ellipsis visible in the screenshot. The app uses `* { box-sizing: border-box }` (app.css:65) while the fixture was content-box, so the shipped text box is 18 px narrower still (~32 / ~28 characters). The full text is reachable only by hover title (same as the board, story 2.5) or by clicking into the single-line edit input (popover.js:636-660), neither of which is "offers full note texts". The other three clauses hold: in-place edit (popover.js:406-413 click → startEdit :636-660; tier-2 retrofit-probe2.dom.js rows Q4b/Q4c/Q4d at :247/:268/:281 assert the editor opens, commits, declines and abandons), delete (popover.js:452-461 store.apply('deleteNotePopover'); probe2 row 'Q4 popover ✕ deletes…' :222), category (popover.js:322-324 paintDot colours the dot and sets dot.title = category.name; dom-rendering.dom.js:818 row '2.4 · clicking the +n chip opens the popover with the FULL stack' counts `.pop-row .dot`). No tier-2 row measures visible width of `.pop-row .txt` (grep of tests/tier2 for scrollWidth/clientWidth/textOverflow against popover: none), so tier 2 neither contradicts nor covers the failing clause. PARTIAL is the right verdict, with "offers full note texts" as the failing clause; confidence can be raised to high because the clipping is measured in WebKit with the shipped CSS.

items.text: Overlapping bars render in parallel lanes within the day rows, so simultaneous things (project + vacation) stay readable.

items.evidence: tests/tier2/interaction.dom.js — row 'dragging upward normalises the range (3.5) rather than making it invalid' (drag from day 14 to day 4 → one bar, `startDate === to`, `endDate === from`, `startDate <= endDate`); src/js/interact.js:501 (`const [a, b] = drag.anchor <= date ? [drag.anchor, date] : [date, drag.anchor]; // 3.5`); resize clamp :525-526 and tests/tier2/coedit.dom.js — row '§4b …' comment '3.5 — dragging the start edge PAST the end clamps rather than inverting' (`after2.startDate <= after2.endDate`)
items.note: There is no error branch anywhere on the create path — the swap happens on every pointermove, so the preview and the ghost text already show the normalised range before release. The resize path clamps the dragged edge against the other one instead of inverting. Tier-1 layout.test.js '3.5 · normalization is a GESTURE concern' additionally pins that layout trusts the contract (and characterises that an inverted range from a hand-edited file renders degenerately rather than being repaired — not reachable from the UI).
items.text: Dragging upward (end before start) just normalizes — no error state for a natural gesture.

items.evidence: tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js — rows '3.6 · a bar running past the last column says so twice: on the stripe and under it' (`.bar-cont-down` textContent '↓' in the bar's colour, `.horizon-cue` textContent 'läuft weiter →', exactly one of each, pointer-events none), '3.6 · mirrored — a bar that began before the window gets a ↑ on the first column' (`.bar-cont-up`, no top grip, no footer), '3.6 · a bar that swallows the entire window is cued at both ends at once'; tests/tier1/layout.test.js — rows 'the cue rides with the window — the same bar loses it after paging' (after `pageYears:1` the same bar has `beyondStart` and no `horizon`), 'the horizon test is STRICT…'; src/js/board.js:1197-1214, :612-613; src/js/i18n.js:27 ('läuft weiter →') / :513 ('continues →')
items.note: The forward cue is literally 'continues →' in English and 'läuft weiter →' in German, plus a coloured ↓ glyph on the stripe; the mirror is a ↑ glyph on the first column (no footer at the near edge, by design — layout.test.js 'col.horizon reports the far end only'). 'Grows back into view as the board rolls' is a property of the view window: `beyondEnd/beyondStart` are recomputed by `buildBoard` from the current window, and rolling mode redraws on a month change (main.js:472-481), pinned for paging by the tier-1 row above.
items.text: A bar reaching past the visible horizon gets a "continues →" cue and grows back into view as the board rolls, so long projects are never clipped silently. Mirrored for bars starting before the view.

items.evidence: tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js — row '3.1/3.2 …' (`labels.length === 2`, 'the label repeats once per segment (3.7)'; `stripes[0].title` includes 'Umbau Küche' and `${from} – ${to}`), row '3.2 · a bar spanning three months …' (`labels.length === 3`), row '3.7 · each segment label sits on a row that carries no ink of its own'; tests/tier2/board-render.dom.js — row 'a bar renders one stripe plus one label per month segment' (`labels.length === 3`, each contains the label text); src/js/board.js:1152-1158 (`segTitle` = `${label} · ${start} – ${end}`), :1251 (`lab.title = segTitle(seg)`), :1185 (`bar.title = segTitle(seg)`); tests/tier1/layout.test.js rows '3.7 — one label row per MONTH SEGMENT…' and the six ink-avoidance rows
items.note: One 66 px chip (ellipsised, app.css:643-647) per month segment, placed on the first ink-free row within the first six rows of the segment; the full label plus the ISO date span is the hover `title` on both the chip and the stripe (the stripe's title is asserted in tier 2; the chip's is the same `segTitle` call at board.js:1251). On a family board with no free rows the chip retreats into the gutter (`.on-ink`) rather than covering entries — e8-density-legibility.dom.js §A3 rows '3.7/labels-land-on-empty-space'.
items.text: A bar's label renders once per month segment with full text on hover, so six-month stripes stay labeled without clutter.

items.evidence: src/js/layout.js:15 (`export const MAX_LANES = 3; // spec 3.8`), :617 (`if (lane >= MAX_LANES) overflowSegs.push(seg)`), :702 (`laneOverflow[d] += 1` per day); tests/tier1/layout.test.js — rows 'assignLanes itself is UNBOUNDED — the cap of 3 is applied later' (`L.MAX_LANES === 3`), '3.8 — the cap counts PER DAY: only the covered days carry the badge', '3.8 — two hidden bars on the same day make it "+2"'; tests/tier2/dom-rendering.dom.js — row '3.8 · the fourth overlapping bar becomes a +n, and only where three coincide' (3 `.bar` drawn, `.d-more` chip textContent '+1', `chip.title === '1 weitere Balken'`, no chip on an uncovered day); src/js/board.js:903-922 (`applyMore`: title `${laneOverflow} ${t('lanesFull')}`), i18n.js:461/:874 ('weitere Balken' / 'more bars'); tests/tier2/interaction.dom.js — row 'the +n chip opens the same popover'
items.note: Cap is 3 lanes, evaluated per day; overflow compresses into the same '+n' badge notes use, with a native tooltip naming it as bars ('n weitere Balken' / 'n more bars') and a click that opens the day popover listing every entry. One deliberate exception to lane stability: a bar hidden in one month is 'rescued' into a freed base lane in a later month (layout.test.js 'LANE RESCUE…' rows, DESIGN-DECISIONS §C) — visible beats stable, and the badge still counts it wherever it is not drawn. AUDIT.md F11 (a dropped foreign bar carried no 'neu' mark) is closed at layout.js:686-702.
items.text: Parallel lanes cap at 3 per day; further overlaps compress into a "+n" marker with tooltip, so extreme weeks stay legible.

items.evidence: src/js/interact.js:490-531 (`updateDrag` for 'create-bar' / 'move-bar' / 'resize' only mutates the local `drag` object and paints `.bar-preview` nodes via `paintRangePreview`, :653-674 — no `store.apply`, no `renderBoard`); :534-616 (`finishDrag` is the only place a bar op is committed, on pointerup); src/js/main.js:88-93 (`redraw()` runs only from `store.subscribe`), :472-481 (the 30 s clock redraws only when `todayISO()` changed); src/js/layout.js lane sweep is deterministic — tests/tier1/layout.test.js row 'the sweep order is start asc, then LONGER first, then id asc' (result independent of input order)
items.note: The gesture itself never writes to the store or re-lays the board before pointerup, so no lane is recomputed mid-gesture; other bars keep their stripes untouched and the moving/resizing bar is shown as a translucent preview at the column edge (`right: 2px`, not in a lane). No test asserts lane stability DURING a drag (family-density.dom.js §5 drives 200 pointermoves but measures frame time only; e1-incremental §I3 only checks a preview survives a patch render) — hence medium. Residual worth naming: in family mode nothing defers an incoming remote op while a drag is in flight (no guard in src/js/sync or store.js), so a peer's overlapping bar arriving mid-drag would redraw and could reshuffle lanes; that is not caused by the gesture, but the catalogue sentence does not carve it out.
items.text: While a bar is being dragged or resized, lane assignment stays stable — no mid-gesture reshuffling of other bars. *(src: v1 F3 notes)*

items.evidence: src/js/interact.js:460-465 (`beginDrag` creates a `.bar-preview` in the pressed column with the last-used category colour), :498-505 (`updateDrag` on every pointermove: normalise, `paintCreatePreview(a, b)`, ghost text `${short(a)} – ${short(b)} · N T`), :647-674 (`paintRangePreview` draws one stripe per month the range touches, `top/height` in row units), :535 (`clearPreviews()` on release); src/css/app.css:767-771 (`.bar-preview`: lane-width, opacity .55, z-index 5, pointer-events none), :777-782 (`.drag-ghost`)
items.note: During the create drag the user sees a translucent stripe of the future bar's colour spanning the current (already normalised) range — split per month exactly like the committed bar will be — plus a floating ghost reading e.g. '03.03. – 12.03. · 10 T'. Tests only pin the AFTER state (interaction.dom.js 'is-creating' cleared; retrofit-probe5.dom.js 'a preview stripe was left on screen' === 0; e1-incremental §I3 'after a drag preview was appended to a column'); no tier-2 row asserts `.bar-preview` is present mid-gesture. The code path is short and unambiguous, so high on the code, with that test gap noted.
trail: skeptic downgraded confidence → medium: The stripe preview is real (interact.js:498-505 updateDrag → paintCreatePreview → paintRangePreview :647-674 appends `.bar-preview` with top/height/right/background into the positioned `.rows`; app.css:767-771), so PASS stands. But the note's second half is false: the create-bar branch of beginDrag (interact.js:459-465) never calls makeGhost — the only `drag.ghost = makeGhost(...)` calls are :472 (move-note), :480 (move-bar), :486 (resize) — so the guarded `if (drag.ghost) drag.ghost.textContent = ...` at :503 never runs during creation and no '03.03. – 12.03. · 10 T' ghost exists. And no test observes the preview mid-gesture: coedit.dom.js `boardIsAlive()` (:154-162) and retrofit-probe5 T3 (:139) only count `.bar-preview` after release, and e1-incremental §I3 (:460-463) appends a `.bar-preview` by hand into a `.col`. A code-read whose stated behaviour is half wrong and wholly unobserved does not merit high.
items.text: Creating a bar shows a live preview of the range during the drag, before release. *(src: v1 §12 deliverable 5)*

Tier-2 pins (ran at HEAD per the brief; assertions opened and confirmed): dom-rendering.dom.js rows 3.1/3.2, 3.2 (three months), 3.7, 3.6 ×3, 3.8; interaction.dom.js rows 'a vertical drag…', 'dragging upward normalises…', 'the +n chip opens the same popover'; board-render.dom.js rows 'a bar renders one stripe plus one label…', 'a bar past the horizon…', 'a fourth overlapping bar…'; coedit.dom.js §4b/§4d. (2) Lane stability (3.A) has one designed exception after commit: the per-column lane rescue (DESIGN-DECISIONS §C, layout.test.js 'RESCUE — a rescued bar may sit in DIFFERENT lanes in different months', and its winner is store-order dependent, flagged there for LZP-402). (3) Tests I would want that do not exist: a tier-2 row asserting `.bar-preview` exists and tracks the pointer mid-create-drag (3.B), and a row asserting every other `.bar`'s `dataset.lane` and `style.right` are byte-identical across a 200-move drag (3.A); today both are code-read only. (4) Family-mode residual touching 3.A: no guard defers an incoming remote op during a drag (grep of src/js/sync, family, store.js, main.js finds none), so a peer's overlapping bar can redraw lanes under a gesture — not gesture-caused, but unpinned. Code: interact.js beginDrag/updateDrag/finishDrag (:452-616, `// 3.5` at :501, maxLength 40 at :863, makeEditor honours it at :723), pointerdown keys on `barNode.dataset.barId` from `.bar, .bar-label` on any segment (:351-361) which is what makes 'edit either part edits the whole' true; board.js buildStripe/buildLabel/segTitle (:1152-1252, `lab.title = segTitle(seg)` at :1251, grips only where !contTop/!contBot), applyMore title `${laneOverflow} ${t('lanesFull')}` (:903-922), horizon-cue (:612-613); layout.js MAX_LANES=3 (:15), `lane >= MAX_LANES → overflowSegs` (:617), per-day laneOverflow (:698-702), label passes A–D always yield a labelRow (:816-838); app.css `.rows{position:relative}` (:232), --lane-w 6px/--lane-gap 8px (:42-43), .bar-label 66px ellipsis (:643-647), .bar-preview (:767-771); main.js redraw only from subscribe (:88-93) and clock only on date change (:472-481); i18n :27/:513 'läuft weiter →'/'continues →', :461/:874 'weitere Balken'/'more bars'. Tests: every cited tier-2 row exists, is unskipped, and asserts its clause (interaction.dom.js :137, :152, :304; coedit :422, :453; dom-rendering :859, :921, :948, :967, :988, :1006, :1019; board-render :211; e8-density-legibility :579-585); the tier-2 drag() helpers dispatch real pointerdown/pointermove(+10/+12 px)/pointerup so the 4 px threshold is crossed. Tier 1: `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/layout.test.js` → `# tests 93 # pass 93 # fail 0 # skipped 0 # todo 0`; cited rows at :398, :411, :432, :454, :465, :520, :615, :626, :638, :651, :731, :758, :776, :787, :900 all present and assert what is claimed. 3.A upheld at medium: confirmed no gesture guard in src/js/sync/family.js (its `deferred` map is for uncurable ops) and store.emit('remote') (store.js:4367/:4953/:5400) reaches redraw() unfiltered, so the named family-mode residual is real; solo mode has no mid-drag redraw trigger (saveScroll is localStorage-only, the armFamilySeen scroll listener is disarmed by the pointerdown that starts the gesture). Minor inaccuracies not affecting verdicts: 3.8's cited '+n chip opens the same popover' row seeds 5 notes, not bars (the catalogue clause only requires marker + tooltip, which the 3.8 dom-rendering row asserts directly); 3.A's note says the move/resize preview sits 'not in a lane' but `right: 2px` is lane 0's offset. No shell-level behaviour in this section, so the Tauri/Swift distinction does not apply.

The 'brief flash' half is code-read only: tests/tier2/retrofit-probe.dom.js row 'P8 creating into a hidden category unhides + flashes' merely diag()s classList.contains('flash') without asserting it, so a regression that dropped the flash but kept the unhide would pass tier 2. prefers-reduced-motion disables the animation (app.css:1310) — deliberate. Never into the family space: src/js/core/ops.js:84 (categoryId 'never published, at any level'), :226-231 (no pub.categoryId), src/js/core/project.js:221 (CATEGORY_SPELLINGS barred from family patches); tests/tier1/core-ops.test.js — row 'A3 — categoryId has NO pub counterpart at ANY level, in ANY family kind' (ran: 70/70); tests/attack/redaction-invariants.test.js:442 WIRE.assertNeverTransmitted(SECRET.category) (ran: 49/49); tests/property/project-domains.test.js (ran: 13/13). But synced between own devices: src/js/core/ops.js:252 ('cat.set' space: 'personal'), :585-597 (spaceFor stamps the psp_ id), docs/v2/adr/001-*.md:535-536 (personal space = note/bar/cat/pad.set, replicated to my attested devices), src/js/sync/personal.js:1-8 ('MY TWO MACS, MY WHOLE PRIVATE BOARD').
items.clause: *Meine Kategorien* (personal, never synced) and *Familie*
items.note: What holds: the legend is two sections (categories + 'bearbeiten', then a divider, then member chips with per-member toggles), and categories are structurally unable to reach the family space — 'a private organizational system' is enforced by the absence of a field, not a filter. Two literal deviations: (1) neither section carries the named heading — the shipped row is 'Arbeit · Familie · Reisen · Deadlines · bearbeiten │ ⬤⬤⬤ · n', with no 'Meine Kategorien' or 'Familie' label; membersui.js:1088-1112 argues this away because v1 ships a default CATEGORY called 'Familie' and one 40 px row cannot carry that word twice with two meanings, and family-legend.dom.js pins 'no heading' as the intended state. (2) 'never synced' is false in the literal sense: cat.set is a personal-space op that replicates end-to-end encrypted to the user's own attested Macs (consistent with catalogue 19.4 'my entire board … syncs … between my devices only'); it is only 'never synced to the family'. A3's source text says 'personal, local … never synced' and predates F19, so the catalogue's own erratum rule ('the specs govern') likely resolves this as wording — but as written, the clause does not hold. Recommend an erratum re-wording 4.A to 'never shared with the family' and stating whether the section names are labels or just names.

defence.reason: The finding stands; I could not refute either deviating clause, and I sharpened both. (1) No section carries the name "Meine Kategorien" or "Familie" — not as visible text and not as an accessible name either. The family section is built at src/js/family/membersui.js:1080-1124 from exactly three children: a divider (`tb-sep legend-fam-rule`, :1086), the chip strip (:1121-1123) and the `· n` opener button (:1124, familyOpener :1134-1142). Neither the section (`sec`, :1080-1082) nor the categories half (src/js/legend.js) receives an aria-label, role, or title naming it; the only aria-labels are on the opener (:1139, "Familie im Kreis anzeigen" — a tooltip, per the code's own comment at :1119) and on per-member chips (:1172). The spec source A3 (docs/v2/traceability.json:977) literally names the sections "Meine Kategorien" and "Familie"; the shipped row shows neither word as a section identifier. The tier-2 row the auditor cites (tests/tier2/family-legend.dom.js:129-151) asserts the divider COUNT is 1 (:140) — it does not assert the absence of a heading; the absence rests on the code path above. (2) "never synced" is false in the literal sense, and I observed it rather than inferring it from the op-kind table: a scratchpad fleet run through the shipped engine (tests/helpers/fleet.js uses src/js/sync/personal.js createPersonalSync, real sealOp/openOp, real server handlers) added a category on Mac A and it arrived on Mac B after settle. Production wires that engine at src/js/family/engine.js:83. `cat.set` is classified space:'personal' at src/js/core/ops.js:252; store.outbox() (src/js/store.js:2433-2447) filters only by seq/park/device/space and therefore offers cat.set lines to the wire; ADR 001 §4.3 (docs/v2/adr/001-*.md:534-535) defines the personal space as note/bar/cat/pad.set replicated to my attested devices. This is consistent with catalogue 19.4 ("my entire board … syncs … between my devices only") and so the spec is internally in tension — A3 says "personal, local … never synced", 19.4 says the whole board syncs to my own Macs — but as the catalogue sentence is written, "never synced" does not hold. What DOES hold, and is verified: the legend is two sections in A3's order (family-legend.dom.js:137-149, tier-2 PASS); the family section has per-member visibility toggles (membersui.js:1167-1172); and categories are structurally unable to reach the family space — tests/tier1/core-ops.test.js row "A3 — categoryId has NO pub counterpart at ANY level, in ANY family kind" (ran: 70/70 pass), tests/attack/redaction-invariants.test.js (ran: 49/49), tests/property/project-domains.test.js (ran: 13/13), docs/v2/adr/004:37 (enforced by absence of a field). Verdict should remain PARTIAL: "two sections", "members", and "categories remain a private organizational system" hold; the section names and "never synced" do not. Recommend an erratum re-wording to "never shared with the family / never synced to the family" and stating that the two names are spec identifiers, not on-screen labels (the code's stated reason: v1 ships a default CATEGORY called "Familie", membersui.js:1088-1112).

defence.reason: The finding stands. I tried to refute both failing clauses and could not. (1) Section names: neither legend section carries a visible or machine-readable "Meine Kategorien" / "Familie" label in the shipped web layer (identical in both shells — the legend is DOM, not native). legend.js:paintCategoryHalf (201-209) inserts only category buttons, an overflow chip and the „bearbeiten" button; index.html:52 is a bare `<div class="legend">` with no aria-label; membersui.js:1079-1085 builds the family section as `<span class="legend-fam" id="legend-family">` with one `.tb-sep.legend-fam-rule` divider and no heading or aria-label (FAMILY_LEGEND_ID = 'legend-family', :1011); the only occurrence of the word "Familie" in that half is the opener's tooltip (:351 'Familie im Kreis anzeigen', :1138-1139), which is a tooltip, not a section name. membersui.js:1088-1112 documents dropping the label deliberately because v1 ships a default CATEGORY named „Familie". tests/tier2/family-legend.dom.js row 'A3 · the family half is drawn INSIDE the category rebuild, last, behind one divider' asserts at :140 `assert.equal($$('.legend-fam-rule', famSection()).length, 1, 'one divider, no heading')` — so "no heading" is the pinned, intended state, and it passed in tier 2 at HEAD. Two sections exist; they are not named on screen. (2) "never synced": literally false between the user's own Macs, and by design. ops.js:252 `'cat.set': { space: 'personal' }`; store.js:2433-2448 `outbox()` filters lines only by `op.space === this._personalSpaceId` — there is no kind filter, so cat.set lines are offered; sync/personal.js:811-822 seals every offered line (`sealLine(line.op)`) with no kind check (grep for `op.k` in personal.js finds none); main.js:163 arms this when `settings.syncEnabled && settings.personalSpaceId`. tests/attack/round3-seam.test.js:252-255 shows the app path `store.apply('addCategory', …)` appends a `cat.set` op (ran: 25/25 pass). tests/attack/e10-outbound-payload.test.js:154-158 builds a real `cat.set` op in the personal space, :190 seals it, and row '§1a · the personal push …' (:233-243) pushes it through `createBridgeTransport` to POST /api/v1/ops — asserting only that the PLAINTEXT does not cross, i.e. the encrypted category envelope does go over the wire (ran: 18/18 pass). The product's own settings copy says the same narrower promise: settings.js:664 "Private Einträge gehen nur zu deinen eigenen, gekoppelten Macs." The redaction-invariants WIRE assertion the auditor cites is family-tape-only (redaction-invariants.test.js:432-434 "this device's family ops are the only thing on this tape"), so it does not contradict this; it only proves the family half. What holds fully: categories are a private organizational system that can never reach the family space — ops.js:84 (`categoryId` "never published, at any level"), :226-231 (no `pub.` counterpart), project.js:221 CATEGORY_SPELLINGS barred from family patches, tests/tier1/core-ops.test.js row 'A3 — categoryId has NO pub counterpart at ANY level, in ANY family kind' (ran: 70/70 pass). Sharpening for the erratum: the catalogue is faithful to its source — traceability.json:977 (A3) itself says "(unchanged, personal, local) … Categories are never synced" — so this is not a catalogue-vs-spec conflict the header's "specs govern" rule resolves; it is a spec-internal tension between A3 and 19.4 ("my entire board … syncs … between my devices only", catalogue :216). 19.4 forces categories to replicate (a second Mac receiving note.set ops with categoryIds it lacks would render an unusable board), so the implementation followed 19.4. The erratum should re-word 4.A to "never shared with the family / never leaves my own paired Macs" and state that the two section names are names, not on-screen labels (the divider carries the split).

sections.skeptic_notes: All six F4 verdicts survive at HEAD ab00471. Every cited file:line exists and says what the auditor claims; no cited test is skipped/todo/only; the five tier-1 suites reproduce the cited counts (store-persistence 125/125, core-undo 97/97, core-ops 70/70, layout 93/93, palette 6/6, all via `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/<file>`). F4 is pure webview behaviour, so the Tauri-vs-Swift shell question does not arise. Two wording imprecisions in the evidence that do not change any verdict: (1) 4.1 cites retrofit-probe.dom.js P10 for rename, but P10 asserts only `depth()-before === 1`; the actual rename-through-the-sheet assertion lives in retrofit-probe3.dom.js R2 (`dc.name === 'Zuhause'`, undo restores 'Familie'/'Family'), which the auditor also cites. (2) 4.2 describes `categoryId: { t:'id' }` at ops.js:84/:95 as "required"; ops.js:386 only validates the value when present (non-empty string). The clause still holds because every create builder (ops.js:842-848, :886-892, :944-950) and every UI site (interact.js:542, :731→:799, popover.js:270) supplies it, migrate() repairs orphans (store.js:435-439), and store.category() falls back to the first category (store-persistence 1428-1432). Independently confirmed for 4.6 that the flash cannot be wiped by a late redraw: store.subscribe→redraw→renderLegend is synchronous inside apply() (main.js:88-93, :277-280), and the ResizeObserver path (legend.js:406-411) repaints only on a ≥0.5 px width change, so `flashCategory` after apply() lands on the freshly built node. Confirmed no tier-2 row clicks a `.swatches .sw` in the category sheet (grep over tests/tier2), matching the auditor's disclosure; recolor rests on legend.js:534-543 code-read plus core-undo 825/1054 at tier 1, which is thin but honest for the stated 'high' given the handler is a one-line apply().

sections.title: Move, resize, undo

items.evidence: tests/tier2/interaction.dom.js — rows '5.1 · dragging a note onto another day reschedules it, keeping everything else' (asserts n.date === to, text untouched, notes.length === 1, rendered on new day, gone from old) and '5.1 · a move is one undo step, and undo puts the note back'; code path src/js/interact.js:368-373 (pending note press) → :466-473 (beginDrag move-note) → :507-511 (target = day under pointer) → :567-586 (finishDrag commits 'moveNote' with the absolute date; repeat re-anchors via reanchorRepeat)

A repeating note keeps its series year and moves month/day (row '5.1/9.3'). The gesture on a foreign entry is refused at interact.js:457 (18.1), which is an authorisation rule, not a defect of this item.
items.text: I drag a note onto another day to reschedule it, so replanning is one motion instead of delete-and-retype.

items.text: I drag a bar as a whole to shift it while keeping its length, so sliding a vacation one week later is a single move.

items.clause: any pinned year, past or future, shows correct holidays

defence.reason: The auditor's residual is real and I could not refute it: it is reproduced by direct execution, it is pinned as characterized behaviour by a passing tier-1 row, and the single render path carries only one name per date. The catalogue's main clauses (rules not tables, Easter arithmetic, Buß-und-Bettag rule, no data horizon) hold fully; the "shows correct holidays" clause is broken only in the narrow, exactly-bounded case where Easter is 23 March and Christi Himmelfahrt (Easter+39) lands on 1 May. In those years the date is still marked as an own nationwide holiday but is labelled only "Tag der Arbeit" in both chip and tooltip, and the year's map has 18 entries instead of 19. Sharpening: (a) I verified this is the ONLY collision the rule set can ever produce — Easter+39 spans 30 Apr–3 Jun and 1 May is the sole fixed date in that window; every other Easter offset (-2, 0, +1, +49, +50, +60) and the Buß-und-Bettag window (16–22 Nov) never overlap any FIXED date — so the residual is precisely "Christi Himmelfahrt's name, in years with a 23 March Easter" and nothing else. (b) The affected years are 1636, 1704, 1788, 1845, 1856, 1913, 2008, 2160, 2228, 2380, 2532, 2600, 2752 (computed 1583–3000); the tier-1 constant EASTER_MAR_23_YEARS lists only four (omits 2380, which the auditor and tests/COVERAGE.md both include) — so the pin is narrower than the phenomenon, though the assertion is still correct for the years it names. (c) 2008 is reachable in the shipped UI: settings.js:212 offers 2024–2028 and main.js:421-425 page() decrements pageYears with no clamp (the only bound, entities.js:470 pinnedMonthsRenderable, guards hostile store data, not the pager). (d) find.js contains no holiday search at all, so "cannot find Himmelfahrt by name" is a visual/tooltip statement, not a search-feature statement. (e) The stable-count row at tests/tier1/dates-holidays.test.js:611-623 explicitly `continue`s past EASTER_MAR_23_YEARS, so the suite pins the loss rather than asserting correctness there. PARTIAL is the right verdict: primary clauses PASS, the "correct holidays" clause has a bounded, named-label residual.

defence.reason: The finding stands and is, if anything, understated. Clause "any pinned year, past or future, shows correct holidays" fails on two counts. (1) Collision drop, exactly as the auditor read it: src/js/holidays.js:119-126 `put()` returns early when `prev.own || !own`; FIXED (:58-71) is inserted before EASTER_BASED (:74-82) at :135-136, so when Easter is 23 March (1913, 2008, 2160, 2228, 2380) Christi Himmelfahrt (Easter+39 = 1 May) is discarded for every state including '' — the day stays a marked nationwide holiday under the single name 'Tag der Arbeit', and no render path can surface a second name (board.js:762-763, :776-778 read only d.holiday.name/short). The user can reach 2008: settings.js:212 offers only ±2 years, but the year pager (index.html:36-38, main.js:374-375, 421-425) is unbounded and layout.js:389/:562-565 derive `years` from the visible window. Tier-2 rows under 'holidays (F6 / 6.5)' (board-render.dom.js:110-171) never exercise a 23 March Easter year, so they do not refute. (2) Sharpening the auditor did not raise: the rule table encodes current law with no validity ranges, so pinned PAST years render anachronistic holidays — 2017 Reformationstag shown as 9-state regional (it was nationwide that year), 1994 Buß- und Bettag shown SN-only (nationwide until 1994), 2015 Berlin Frauentag shown as own (holiday only since 2019), 1985 shows Tag der Deutschen Einheit on 3 Oct and nothing on 17 June, 2020 Berlin 8 May absent. No doc in docs/v2 declares a historical scope. The rule-based / no-data-horizon half of the sentence holds (holidays.js:29-53; tier-1 far-future rows 2087/2100/3000). PARTIAL is the right verdict; the failing clause should be widened from 'one name missing in five collision years' to 'past years are computed under current law and the collision guard drops Christi Himmelfahrt on a 23 March Easter'.

The product does not merely carry placeholder data quietly — it declares it: the file header calls the dates "UNVERIFIED SAMPLE DATA", FERIEN_META.source reads 'KMK (Platzhalterdaten / placeholder data)', settings.js:189 renders a user-facing warning off verified===false, definition-of-done.md rule 7 says the flag "stays false until real KMK data lands", and tier-1 row '7.4 — FERIEN_META declares the data unverified' asserts deepEqual verified:false, so the test suite itself pins the placeholder state. items.note: Four distinct, monotonic values exist and are pinned; all are near-white (Ferien vs plain ≈ 1.05:1, weekend-in-Ferien vs white ≈ 1.3:1) so they stay quieter than any category ink or bar. Whether the faintest step (plain → Ferien, #FFFFFF → #FAF8FE) reads as distinguishable on a given display is a human-eye judgement; the product acknowledges this with the opt-in hatch second channel (settings.js:174-180, app.css:268-269, tier-2 row 'option 1k · the Ferien hatch is a second channel, off by default').
trail: skeptic downgraded confidence → low: What is pinned: the four token values exist and differ (app.css:26-28, :257-259; body paints --surface #FFFFFF at app.css:73 so a fill-less plain day is white), and tier-2 'challenge 4' asserts weekend ≠ Ferien ≠ weekend-in-Ferien with lum(weekendFerien) < lum(weekend) < lum(ferien). What is NOT pinned: no assertion anywhere compares the faintest pair, plain (#FFFFFF, SHADE.none in row 1.2) against Ferien (#FAF8FE, SHADE.ferien in row 7.2) — they are only asserted separately against their own constants; and no assertion touches 'quieter than any user content' at all (e8-density-legibility §A4 measures ink ON these backgrounds, not the backgrounds against content). The product's own design record concedes the operative clause is at threshold: DESIGN-DECISIONS.md:101-102 — 'four ambient states within a few percent of each other can die on a bad monitor' — and ships the 1k hatch (settings.js:174-180, app.css:268-269) precisely because value alone is not trusted. 'Visually distinguishable' and 'quieter than content' are therefore inferred from token arithmetic plus a design doc that admits the risk; that is low-confidence support for the sentence as worded. Not overturned: the concession is conditional ('can die on a bad monitor'), not a finding of indistinguishability, so there is no contrary evidence for PARTIAL.
items.text: The four ambient backgrounds — plain day, weekend, Ferien, weekend-within-Ferien — are all visually distinguishable while staying quieter than any user content. *(src: v1 F7 notes, §10)*

Vertical scrolling is a routine shipped state, not an edge case: .board-wrap has overflow-y:auto (app.css:210), a column is 26+31·rowH+14+62 = 31·rowH+102 px tall (app.css:45-46,786-787; board.js:601), row height is a persisted 18–32 px setting with no fit-to-window handler (layout.js:88,96; settings.js:271; no resize/clientHeight/innerHeight code in main.js/board.js/layout.js), and the shipped window is 1440×900 min 640 (tauri.conf.json:17-19; Swift main.swift:2052 identical) with 28 px titlebar + 40 px toolbar (app.css:88-89,111). Concrete failure: Komfort, default window, scrolled to the 31st (scrollTop≈76), press Heute on the 1st–2nd → the today row sits under the 26 px sticky .col-head (app.css:219) and stays there. defence.reason: The finding stands and the auditor's clause split is right. Three parts of the sentence hold on a straight code path in the SHIPPED shell: (1) the button exists and is wired (index.html:33 → main.js:367 → jumpToToday), (2) ⌘T is wired both in the web layer (main.js:516) and natively in the Tauri shell (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1452 MenuItem "today" CmdOrCtrl+T → lib.rs:1553-1562 on_menu_event emits "menu" → main.js:579 listen('menu') → actions.today main.js:563) — the Swift shell agrees (main.swift:2564), so no shell disagreement; (3) in pinned mode the year page is reset to the year holding today (main.js:429-443) and redraw() is synchronous (main.js:277 renderBoard → the today column exists before scrollToToday queries it at main.js:449). That state half is genuinely asserted in a real WKWebView (interaction.dom.js rows '8.3 · Today brings a paged-away pinned board back…' asserting pageYears→0, .is-today-month and .day.today present; and the rolling no-op row). What does NOT hold is the literal "from wherever I've scrolled" / "back to the current day": scrollToToday (main.js:447-453) issues wrapEl.scrollTo({ left }) with no `top`, so scrollTop is left where the user put it. Vertical scrolling of .board-wrap is a shipped, reachable state, not a hypothetical: app.css:210 gives it overflow-y:auto; the toolbar is 40 px (app.css:111), so a default 900 px window (tauri.conf.json:17) leaves ≈860 px for the board, while the offered Komfort preset (layout.js DENSITY.komfort.rowHeight 26) needs 31·26+26+62 = 894 px by the product's own formula (settings.js:308), the slider ceiling 32 needs 1080, and at minHeight 640 (tauri.conf.json:19) even Kompakt's 770 overflows. settings.js:313 tells the user those rows "have to be scrolled to". A user who scrolled down to the scratchpad or the last rows and presses Today when today is, say, the 2nd, gets the correct month column but the today row stays above the fold — the button does not bring the current day into view. Also worth recording: neither 8.3 tier-2 row asserts any scroll position (horizontal or vertical) — the GAP NOTE at interaction.dom.js:527-530 says so explicitly, and COVERAGE.md:121 records only the pageYears half — so the horizontal scroll clause is code-read, not test-read; the tier-2 harness viewport may show all 31 rows (dom-rendering.dom.js:433 guards its vertical test on scrollHeight > clientHeight+20). No tier-1/attack/property/fleet file touches DOM scrolling, so running them cannot settle this. Sharpening: severity is low — the vertical case only arises in a window the product already warns is too short, and find.js:381-392 shows the codebase already has a two-axis scroll-into-view idiom that Today could reuse (or `.day.today.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})`). Verdict: PARTIAL, with the failing clause narrowed to "back to the current day (vertically) from wherever I've scrolled"; the button, ⌘T in both shells, the horizontal jump to the today column, and the pinned year-page reset all hold.

items.clause: With macOS "Reduce Motion" enabled, the roll (and all other animations) become instant swaps

defence.reason: The finding stands; I could not refute it. The roll clause holds: main.js:293 adds `.roll-anim` and removes it by a 340 ms setTimeout (not animationend), and app.css:1308-1309 sets `.board.roll-anim { animation: none; }` under prefers-reduced-motion, so the roll is a genuine instant swap. But the "(and all other animations)" clause fails on one concrete path: legend.js:429 injects `.legend-more.flash { animation: unhide-flash .5s ease-out; }` into a <style> element (ensureFitCss, legend.js:435-441, called from moreChip at :251 and the disclosure list at :274 whenever the „+n" chip renders). The keyframes `unhide-flash` are defined unguarded at app.css:151-154. The reduced-motion block at app.css:1308-1312 neutralises only `.legend-item.flash` and zeroes `transition-duration` — it does not touch `animation-duration`, and no other rule in app.css or in any injected CSS (syncstatus.js:747, createjoin.js:2354, sharing.js:540, membersui.js:1294, pairingui.js:955 are all scoped to their own selectors) covers `.legend-more`. The path is reachable in production: interact.js:559, interact.js:809 and popover.js:289 call flashCategory(catId), and legend.js:453-462 puts `.flash` on `.legend-more` when the unhidden category is in overflowCats. So with Reduce Motion on, creating an entry whose category sits behind „+n" still plays a 500 ms background flash on the chip. This is a web-layer CSS issue, identical in both shells (neither main.swift nor lib.rs injects a motion flag; the page relies on WKWebView's prefers-reduced-motion mapping). Secondary, unverified: scrollToToday(true) at main.js:445 → main.js:452 uses `behavior: 'smooth'` with no matchMedia guard; whether WebKit makes programmatic smooth scroll instant under Reduce Motion cannot be verified from this repository, so it is not evidence either way. No test pins the media block: tests/COVERAGE.md:126 marks 8.6 T1/T2 as not automatable, and grep over tests/ finds no assertion on roll-anim or unhide-flash under reduced motion (the only reduced-motion assertions are sync-status.dom.js:422/973, sharing-control.dom.js:823, firstrun-unlock.dom.js:253 — family/unlock CSS, not the legend or the roll). Sharpening: the fix is one line — add `.legend-more.flash { animation: none; }` (or a global `* { animation-duration: 0s !important; }`) to the app.css:1308 block — after which the item would be PASS-by-code-read pending a human Reduce Motion check.
defence.evidence: Roll clause holds — src/js/main.js:289-295 (`boardEl.classList.add('roll-anim'); setTimeout(() => boardEl.classList.remove('roll-anim'), 340)`); src/css/app.css:1303 (`.board.roll-anim { animation: roll-slide 300ms ease-out; }`), :1308-1312 (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .board.roll-anim { animation: none; } .legend-item.flash { animation: none; } * { transition-duration: 0s !important; } }`). Failing clause — src/js/legend.js:429 `.legend-more.flash { animation: unhide-flash .5s ease-out; border-radius: 4px; }` inside LEGEND_FIT_CSS (legend.js:421-433), injected by ensureFitCss() legend.js:435-441, invoked at legend.js:251 (moreChip) and :274; keyframes unguarded at src/css/app.css:150-154; flash applied to `.legend-more` at src/js/legend.js:453-462 (`legendEl?.querySelector('.legend-more')` … `node.classList.add('flash')`), reached from src/js/interact.js:559, src/js/interact.js:809, src/js/popover.js:289. Smooth scroll (unverified secondary): src/js/main.js:445 `scrollToToday(true)`, :452 `wrapEl.scrollTo({ left: target, behavior: smooth ? 'smooth' : 'auto' })`, no matchMedia guard. No pinning test: tests/COVERAGE.md:126 ("8.6 roll animation, respects Reduce Motion | ❌ | ❌ | not automatable"); `grep -rn "unhide-flash\|roll-anim\|legend-more.*flash" tests/` returns nothing; reduced-motion assertions exist only in tests/tier2/sync-status.dom.js:422,973, tests/tier2/sharing-control.dom.js:823, tests/tier2/firstrun-unlock.dom.js:253 (family/unlock CSS). defence.reason: The finding stands; I could not refute it. The roll clause holds by code-read: the only roll animation (src/css/app.css:1303 `.board.roll-anim { animation: roll-slide 300ms }`) is switched off at app.css:1309 under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, and every CSS transition in the app (app.css:120, :1297 toast, and every JS-injected `transition:` in src/js/family/*) is zeroed by the universal `* { transition-duration: 0s !important }` at app.css:1311 — the `!important` wins over the non-important injected declarations regardless of origin order. But the "(and all other animations)" clause is not met: there is NO universal `animation: none` rule (the only `*`-scoped ones are `.unlock *` app.css:1290, `.pair *` pairingui.js:955, `.circle *` createjoin.js:2354), so each keyframe animation must be guarded individually — and one is not. src/js/legend.js:429 `.legend-more.flash { animation: unhide-flash .5s ease-out; }` is injected into the document by ensureFitCss() (legend.js:434-440) on the first legend fit, with no `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` block anywhere in LEGEND_FIT_CSS (legend.js:422-433). The +n chip is built as `el('button', 'legend-more', …)` (legend.js:252; src/js/ui.js:6-11 assigns className to exactly that string), so it never carries `legend-item` and the app.css:1310 guard `.legend-item.flash { animation: none }` does not match it. The animation is reachable in shipped code: flashCategory (legend.js:454-461) deliberately targets `.legend-more` when the unhidden category is in overflowCats, and is called from interact.js:559, interact.js:809 and popover.js:289 on every 4.6 auto-unhide. So with Reduce Motion on, creating an entry in a hidden category that sits behind the "+n" chip still plays a 500 ms flash. A second, unverifiable residual: scrollToToday's `behavior: 'smooth'` (src/js/main.js:447-452) has no app-level reduce-motion branch and is left to WebKit. Shell check: neither shell-macos/main.swift nor src-tauri/src/lib.rs / tauri.conf.json mention reduce motion (grep empty) — both rely on WKWebView's native media query, so the two shells do not disagree and the Tauri DMG behaves like the reference shell. No test asserts the app.css:1308 block: tests/COVERAGE.md:124 and :202 mark "8.6 roll animation + Reduce Motion" as not automatable; docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1189 lists 8.6 UNVERIFIABLE. The three tier-2 rows that mention reduced-motion (sharing-control.dom.js:822-825, firstrun-unlock.dom.js:245-255, sync-status.dom.js:413-422/973-980) assert only their own feature's stylesheet text or that no animation exists at all; none covers the board roll or the legend chip. Sharpening: the verdict should read PARTIAL with the roll clause marked holding (code-read, medium) and the failing clause narrowed to one concrete animation — the legend "+n" chip flash at legend.js:429 — plus the smooth scroll as unverified; the fix is one line (add `.legend-more.flash { animation: none; }` to the app.css:1308 block or a media block inside LEGEND_FIT_CSS).

sections.title: Yearly repeats

items.evidence: src/js/popover.js:427-444 (↻ toggle, title t('repeatsYearly') = 'Jährlich wiederholen' i18n.js:32, ONE txn sets {repeatsYearly:true, date}); src/js/core/entities.js:566-582 noteOccurrences expands a flagged note into every window year; ran `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/repeats-find-i18n.test.js` → '# tests 121 / # pass 121 / # fail 0', incl. rows 'a repeating note reappears in the next year after the window rolls past it (9.1)', 'a repeat anchored decades back still lands in the current window'; tests/tier2/retrofit-probe2.dom.js — row 'Q3 toggle-repeat ON anchors the series; OFF leaves date alone; undo restores' (clicks the real popover ↻); tests/fleet/long-offline.test.js — row 'a yearly repeat crosses the year boundary…' (ran: 12/12 pass)
items.note: Every clause holds functionally. Literal wording caveat: the control is a two-state ↻ toggle BUTTON (`el('button','act'+(on?' on':''),'↻')`, tooltip 'Jährlich wiederholen'), not an `<input type=checkbox>`; the catalogue's own 9.A calls it 'the repeat toggle', so I read 'checkbox' as the two-state control, not the widget type. It has no aria-pressed/role=checkbox — worth a follow-up if accessibility semantics matter.
trail: skeptic downgraded confidence → medium: The functional clauses (reappears same date every year; survives the roll) are fully pinned: tier-1 rows '(9.1)' and 'a repeat anchored decades back…' ran 121/121; tests/tier2/retrofit-probe2.dom.js — row 'Q3 toggle-repeat ON…' clicks the real popover .act and asserts repeatsYearly:true and date===occurrence. But the clause names 'A "repeats yearly" checkbox' and no such control exists: src/js/popover.js:427 renders an unlabelled ↻ <button class="act">; the text 'Jährlich wiederholen' is only a hover tooltip (:428, i18n.js:32), the ON state is conveyed solely by a colour shift ink-4→ink-1 (src/css/app.css:922-924) and there is no aria-pressed/role. A person verifying the sentence as worded would not find a labelled two-state checkbox; the auditor disclosed this but kept 'high'. Medium is what the wording deserves.
items.text: A "repeats yearly" checkbox on a note makes it reappear on the same date every year, so birthdays survive the roll into the next year.

defence.reason: The finding stands and I can sharpen it from "inferred from CSS" to "measured". The catalogue sentence has four clauses. defence.reason: The auditor's PARTIAL holds and I could not refute it. Two of the three clauses are verified: (a) the steady-state autosave is a real 700 ms debounce with no fake timers — tier-1 rows pass at HEAD on a fresh run; (b) there is no save button (i18n key `save` has no caller; Settings › Daten is Export/Import only). The failing clause is exactly the one the auditor named, and it fails in the SHIPPED shell specifically: in the Tauri build, ⌘Q / Dock › Beenden runs `PredefinedMenuItem::quit`, which muda implements as the native `terminate:` selector; tao 0.35.3 implements only `applicationWillTerminate:` (which calls `AppState::exit()`), never `applicationShouldTerminate:`; and `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` registers no `RunEvent::ExitRequested` handler (`.run(tauri::generate_context!())` with no callback) and never calls `window.__lzpFlush`. So no JavaScript runs between ⌘Q and process exit, and the page's pending 700 ms save timer is simply abandoned — an edit made within ~700 ms of ⌘Q is lost. The pagehide path cannot rescue it: even if WKWebView fired pagehide on process exit (it does not), `store.flushSync()` in the Tauri branch is an unawaited async `persistNow()` that first `await`s `rollSnapshot()` and then an IPC `save_board`, so it cannot complete synchronously. The project itself scopes this race under 11.1: the Swift reference shell's fix is captioned "11.1 — a quit must not race the 700 ms save debounce" (main.swift:2420-2421) and FINDINGS.md:4941's "⌘Q always flushed" is true only of that shell. The two shells disagree, and the shipped one (Tauri) is the one that loses the edit. Sharpening for the record: storage.js:189-191's comment that "in Tauri the debounced save plus the window-close hook already cover the same ground" is wrong for quit — the window-close hook is CloseRequested→prevent_close+hide (lib.rs:1564-1569), which flushes nothing (though it also kills nothing, so ⌘W/red-button is safe). The updater's restart path IS covered (main.js:266 wires `flush: () => store.persistNow()`, awaited at update-ui.js:299 before `update_restart`). The exposure is bounded — at most the edits of the last ~700 ms before a quit — so the item stays PARTIAL, not FAIL; the fix is a `RunEvent::ExitRequested` handler in lib.rs that `prevent`s, evals `window.__lzpFlush()` with a watchdog, then exits.

defence.reason: The finding stands and the auditor read the right file. At HEAD ab00471 the shipped Tauri shell's build_menu (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1377-1471) assembles exactly five submenus — LangzeitPlaner, Ablage, Bearbeiten, Darstellung, Fenster — and Menu::with_items at lib.rs:1471 lists those five and nothing else: there is no Hilfe submenu, and grep for "hilfe|help|set_as_help_menu|set_as_windows_menu" over lib.rs returns zero hits. The Fenster submenu (lib.rs:1462-1469) holds only minimize ("Im Dock ablegen") and fullscreen ("Vollbild"); it is never passed to Submenu::set_as_windows_menu_for_nsapp (an API that exists in the pinned tauri 2.11.5, ~/.cargo/registry/.../tauri-2.11.5/src/menu/submenu.rs:376), so the shipped build gets no system-managed window list, no Zoomen, no "Alle nach vorne bringen". The reference Swift shell (shell-macos/main.swift:2573-2586) does register NSApp.windowsMenu with Zoomen and Alle nach vorne bringen — the two shells disagree, and the shipped one is the weaker — but the Swift shell has no Hilfe menu either (its comment at main.swift:2573 even quotes "§9 — Fenster/Hilfe: standard" and then builds only Fenster). Nothing else refutes it: no tier-1/tier-2/attack/fleet test asserts menu-bar structure (grep of tests/ for Darstellung/Ablage/build_menu/buildMenu/helpMenu/windowsMenu finds only unrelated hits; tests/COVERAGE.md:182 records that the §9 keymap "is not enumerated"); the in-app "Hilfe" is a settings section (tests/tier2/feedback.dom.js row 'the ONLY way in is the Hilfe section of Einstellungen, and it is there', line 137), not a menu; the v1 §9 spec document itself is not in the repo (docs/ holds only v2), so the catalogue sentence is the only statement of the requirement. Every other clause of 13.K holds in the shipped shell: App (About lib.rs:1383, Einstellungen ⌘, :1397, Beenden ⌘Q :1400), Ablage (Exportieren ⇧⌘E, Importieren ⇧⌘I, Drucken ⌘P, Fenster schließen ⌘W, lib.rs:1417-1429), Bearbeiten (Widerrufen/Wiederholen, cut/copy/paste/select-all, Suchen ⌘F, lib.rs:1432-1446), Darstellung (Heute ⌘T, Feiertage ⌘1, Schulferien ⌘2, Modus rollierend/fixiert, lib.rs:1448-1460). Sharpening: the failing clause should be recorded as two defects — (a) Hilfe menu absent in BOTH shells, (b) Fenster non-standard in the SHIPPED Tauri shell only (not registered as the windows menu, missing Zoomen / Alle nach vorne bringen), while the Swift reference shell's Fenster is standard.

The four named menus (App, Ablage, Bearbeiten, Darstellung) match the catalogue entry-for-entry in the shipped Tauri shell — I re-read every MenuItem/PredefinedMenuItem in build_menu and the accelerators are exactly the catalogue's (⌘, / ⇧⌘E / ⇧⌘I / ⌘P / ⌘W / ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z / ⌘F / ⌘T / ⌘1 / ⌘2). No tier-2 row asserts anything about menu-bar structure (only shell-bridge/feedback rows touch the settings-side Hilfe section), so nothing in the verified test run contradicts the auditor. Verdict: PARTIAL — four of five menu groups hold exactly; Hilfe absent in both shells; Fenster non-standard in the shipped shell.

items.note: Every family-scope clause holds with high confidence: solo by default, no account, no family prompt, the features live only behind the settings section's two buttons and nothing family-shaped is evaluated, drawn or requested until a human presses one. The clause 'nothing has changed from v1 — … no network activity' is literally not true of a shipped solo Mac: after the welcome card is dismissed (which sets `disclosed`), the F22 launch/daily update check (catalogue 22.3) goes out from the Tauri updater plugin, and the PO-amended 21.5 (docs/v2/STATUS.md 'THE AMENDMENT', 2026-09-03) admits a human-pressed feedback request. Both are the catalogue's own v2 additions, not family traffic; the board's CSP keeps the WebView at zero. This is the same fact the prior audit recorded as 21.5 FAIL while passing 15.1 (docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1208, :149) — the catalogue contradicts itself between 15.1/N10/21.5 and 22.3, and the PO should resolve the wording. Minor wording note: the join button reads 'Einladungscode eingeben', not 'Familienkreis beitreten' — treated as a label choice, not a defect.

defence.reason: The finding stands: PARTIAL, failing on the literal clause "no network activity" (and by extension "nothing has changed from v1"). Every family-scope clause holds, but a shipped solo Tauri Mac does originate one unrequested HTTPS GET — the F22 update check — once the welcome card has been dismissed, and the repository asserts this fact against itself. What I add beyond the auditor: (1) the exact trigger chain on the shipped shell, including that the Rust prefs default `enabled: true` so dismissing the welcome card is the ONLY act between a fresh install and the first request, and the daily timer (30-min poll) makes that request in the SAME session, not merely on the next launch; (2) the fleet row the auditor cites as passing §15.1 counts relay-rig calls only and never models the updater, so it cannot rescue the clause; (3) the placeholder endpoint is substituted with the real repo slug at release time, so the shipped rc.3 binary has a live host, not a dead one; (4) the PO's amended 21.5 wording ("zero UNREQUESTED requests; the only one is a human press on Senden") does not cover the update check either, because launch/timer checks are not a human press — so the catalogue contradicts itself across 15.1 / N10 / 21.5(amended) vs 22.3, and the PO must resolve wording; the code is consistent and disclosed. Also confirming: the check is disclosed in copy on the welcome card, gated in both JS and Rust, off-switchable in settings, carries no identifiers, and the WebView/board itself stays at zero (CSP + network-scope gates). The auditor's family clauses I re-verified pass. A small precision note (attack P-3): pressing ⚙ on a solo Mac evaluates the crypto/sync/net.js modules in memory (no request, no keygen) — a wording matter for ADR 003 §7, not a defect against 15.1.
