items.clause: it prevents choosing a color already taken by another member
items.evidence: One screen + large paste field: tests/tier2/family-createjoin.dom.js — row '15.3 — code paste, name, colour, done…' asserts #circle-code-in ('the huge paste field') is taller than #circle-display; src/js/family/createjoin.js:2277-2281 .circle-paste {height:68px; font:600 26px mono; letter-spacing:3px}; :1855-1965 the whole join is one renderJoinForm. Colour prevention: src/js/family/createjoin.js:1596-1615 (docblock: 'A joiner is not yet a member, and GET /spaces/:id/members requires an active membership, so before redemption there is no way to learn the roster'), :1430 the join view starts with taken = new Set() (empty) and colorRef PALETTE[0], :1616-1640 colorPicker disables only tones in view.taken, :2036-2043 a relay 'color_taken' refusal adds the tone to view.taken, swaps to firstFreeColorRef and shows a notice; tests/tier2/family-createjoin.dom.js — row 'the join flow prevents a colour collision, and a collision reads as an offer not a failure' asserts the disabled state only AFTER the redemption round trip; server/core/handlers/invites.js:330 rolls the redemption back on a colour collision.
items.note: The join flow is one screen and the paste field is visibly the primary input (68 px, 26 px mono) — those clauses hold. The colour clause is met in outcome but not in the literal mechanism: because the joiner has no roster before redeeming (deliberately — an invite id must not be a roster oracle), every tone is selectable on first render; Mom can pick a taken tone, press 'Beitreten', and only then is it refused by the relay, swapped to a free tone, and disabled. No member can ever end up with a colour another holds (the server checks inside the transaction), and the retry is one click with the code intact. This is a documented, reasoned deviation from 'prevents choosing' (createjoin.js:1600-1610); the PO may accept it by amending the sentence to 'prevents ending up with…', or ask for taken colours to travel in the invitation text (invitationText at createjoin.js:1015 carries only the circle name, code and address today).

defence.reason: The auditor read the right file and the right shell layer (this is pure web-layer + relay behaviour; neither shell is involved). I looked for every way the join view could learn taken colours before redemption and found none: (1) the join view's `taken` set is initialised empty and is written exactly once, in the `color_taken` catch after a relay refusal; (2) `takenColorRefs` (createjoin.js:1048) and membersui's `freeMemberColorRef` are never called from the join view — createjoin.js does not import membersui.js at all, and the fleet row that mentions "the join flow's pre-selection" (e10-fleet-circle.test.js:242-248) only tests the pure function against a member list, it never opens the join screen; (3) the relay exposes no pre-membership roster: router.js:36-47 has only POST /invites, POST /invites/redeem, POST /invites/revoke, GET /invites/open, and both listMembers (members.js:203) and openInvites (invites.js:461) go through `requireActiveMember`; (4) the invitation text (createjoin.js:1015-1024) is name, code, origin only. The tier-2 row the auditor cites is decisive and I confirmed its assertions: a member holding `gruen` is seeded, the joiner CLICKS `#circle-color-gruen` successfully, presses join, and `disabled === true` is asserted only after `view.notice` arrives from the relay refusal. So "prevents choosing" is not met on first render; "no two members end up with the same colour" is met by the server transaction (invites.js:320-323 inside `ctx.store.tx`, rollback keeps the code valid). The one-screen and large-paste-field clauses hold and are tier-2 verified. PARTIAL is the right verdict; the auditor's clause attribution is exact. Sharpening: the deviation is deliberate and documented in code (createjoin.js:1600-1610) and was exercised against a real relay in E6-VERIFICATION.md §3.3, so the PO's choice is between amending the sentence ("prevents ending up with a colour another member holds — a collision costs one round trip and one click") or adding a design ticket to carry taken tones in the invitation text; the current product cannot pass the literal clause without one of those.
defence.evidence: HOLDING CLAUSES (one screen, large paste field): src/js/family/createjoin.js:1855 `function renderJoinForm()` — code, name and colour picker (:1955) on one screen; :2275-2280 `.circle-paste { height: 68px; font: 600 26px/1 var(--mono); letter-spacing: 3px }` with the comment "THE HUGE PASTE FIELD (15.3). Deliberately the largest input in the product."; tests/tier2/family-createjoin.dom.js — row '15.3 — code paste, name, colour, done: no email, no password, no registration form' asserts `paste.getBoundingClientRect().height > other.getBoundingClientRect().height` ('the paste field is not visibly the primary input') and zero password/email inputs (tier 2 PASS at HEAD, method test-read). FAILING CLAUSE ("prevents choosing a color already taken"): createjoin.js:1430 `taken: new Set(),` (join view starts with no knowledge); :1616-1640 `colorPicker` sets `b.disabled = isTaken` only for refs in that set; :2036-2043 the ONLY write to `view.taken` is `view.taken.add(view.colorRef)` inside the `e.code === 'color_taken'` catch after `redeemOnRelay` (:1249-1269, POST /api/v1/invites/redeem) is refused; grep shows no other caller of `takenColorRefs` and no import of membersui.js/`freeMemberColorRef` in createjoin.js. tests/tier2/family-createjoin.dom.js — row 'the join flow prevents a colour collision, and a collision reads as an offer not a failure' (:546-576): seeds a member with `colorRef: 'gruen'`, then `$c('#circle-color-gruen').click()` succeeds pre-redemption, `$c('#circle-join-go').click()`, `await waitFor(() => cj.circleScreenState()?.notice)`, and only then `assert.equal($c('#circle-color-gruen').disabled, true)`. Outcome guarantee: server/core/handlers/invites.js:320-323 `if (!(await tx.colorFree(spaceId, colorRef))) throw fail('bad_request', { field: 'colorRef', reason: 'taken' })` inside `ctx.store.tx` (:313), after `consumeInvite` so the rollback restores the code; createjoin.js:1319 maps that to `color_taken`. No pre-redemption roster: server/core/router.js:36-47 (routes: /spaces/:id/members, /invites, /invites/redeem, /invites/revoke, /invites/open — no invite-preview); server/core/handlers/members.js:203 and invites.js:461 both `requireActiveMember`. Invitation carries no colours: createjoin.js:1015-1024 `invitationText` = [line1(name), '', code, origin, '', line2]. Documented deviation: createjoin.js:1596-1615 docblock; real-relay run recorded in docs/v2/E6-VERIFICATION.md:165-172 (§3.3, Mama picks blau which Papa holds, relay refuses, notice offers Grün, one more click). tests/fleet/e10-fleet-circle.test.js:242-248 tests `takenColorRefs`/`freeMemberColorRef` on a fetched member list only, not the join screen.

defence.reason: Independent read of HEAD ab00471 confirms the auditor on all three clauses. Two hold: the join is one screen (src/js/family/createjoin.js:1855 renderJoinForm is the only join view; the sole other step is 'done', :2029/:1534) and the paste field is visibly the large primary input (.circle-paste at :2276-2280 is 68 px, 600 26px mono, letter-spacing 3px; tests/tier2/family-createjoin.dom.js row '15.3 — code paste, name, colour, done…' asserts #circle-code-in is taller than #circle-display and that no password/email input exists). The third clause — 'it prevents choosing a color already taken by another member' — is not met at the moment of choosing. view.taken is initialised empty at :1430 and is written in exactly one other place, :2040, inside the catch for a relay 'color_taken' refusal (:2036); colorPicker (:1616-1643) disables only refs in that set (:1621, :1631). No relay route hands a non-member the roster: router.js:36/:197 scopes listMembers to a space membership, and invites.js:320-323 does the colour check inside the redemption transaction, rolling consumption back on collision. The tier-2 collision row is itself the cleanest proof of the gap: with another member holding 'gruen', `$c('#circle-color-gruen').click()` succeeds before redemption and the redeem request goes out with gruen; only after the relay's refusal does the test assert `disabled === true` (row 'the join flow prevents a colour collision…', lines 546-575). So the outcome guarantee (no two members ever share a colour, retry is one click with the code intact) is real, but the literal mechanism 'prevents choosing' is a post-hoc disable, not a pre-choice one. Nothing in tier-1/attack/property/fleet bears on this UI clause, and it is not shell-level, so no lib.rs/main.swift divergence applies. Sharpening for the PO: invitationText (:1015-1024) deliberately carries only name, code and origin ('NO KEY MATERIAL … exactly what §7.1 permits'), so putting taken colours into the invitation would be a §7.1 design decision rather than a bug fix; the cheaper honest path is to amend the sentence to 'prevents ending up with a colour another member holds'. PARTIAL stands, with the colour clause as the failing half.
defence.evidence: src/js/family/createjoin.js:1430 `taken: new Set()` (join view initial state, empty); :2036-2044 the only other write to view.taken, inside `if (e && e.code === 'color_taken')` after the redeem round trip; :1616-1643 colorPicker — `const isTaken = taken.has(tone.ref)` (:1621), `b.disabled = isTaken` (:1631); :1596-1615 docblock stating a joiner cannot learn the roster before redemption; :1015-1024 invitationText carries only line1/code/origin/line2; :1855 renderJoinForm (single join view), :2029 `view.step = 'done'`; :2276-2280 `.circle-paste { height: 68px; font: 600 26px/1 var(--mono); letter-spacing: 3px }`. server/core/router.js:36 `GET /spaces/:id/members → listMembers, spaceParam: 'id'`, :197 `listMembers: 'param:id'`; server/core/handlers/invites.js:320-323 `if (!(await tx.colorFree(spaceId, colorRef))) throw fail('bad_request', { field: 'colorRef', reason: 'taken' })` inside `ctx.store.tx`. tests/tier2/family-createjoin.dom.js — row '15.3 — code paste, name, colour, done: no email, no password, no registration form' (lines 396-445: paste height > display height; no password/email inputs; one screen to 'done'); row 'the join flow prevents a colour collision, and a collision reads as an offer not a failure' (lines 546-575: seeded member holds 'gruen', `$c('#circle-color-gruen').click()` at line 556 succeeds pre-redemption, `assert.equal($c('#circle-color-gruen').disabled, true)` at line 567 only after `waitFor(... notice)`). Tier 2 ran PASS at HEAD in this session per the brief, so both rows are verified behaviour (method: test-read + code-read).

sections.section_notes:
Where F15 lives: src/js/family/createjoin.js (create/join screens, settings entry section, invite code derivation, paste parsing), src/js/family/membersui.js (member list, self-edit, colour rule, legend chips), src/js/family/adminpanel.js (invite list/expiry/revoke), src/js/family/mount.js (the ports and the solo/circle mount gates), src/js/main.js:120-227 (the single dynamic import() door), server/core/handlers/invites.js (TTL, single-use, revoke). Nothing in F15 is shell-level: neither shell-macos/main.swift nor src-tauri/src/lib.rs has a Familienkreis code path; the Tauri shell only matters here through the updater (15.1 caveat) and the sync_request transport.

Tests run at HEAD ab00471 in this session: tests/fleet/e10-fleet-circle.test.js (14/14 pass, ~1 s), tests/tier1/createjoin.test.js + tests/tier1/network-scope.test.js (52/52 pass). Tier-2 rows cited were opened and their assertions match the clauses; none of the three residual tier-2 FAIL rows (§A4/§E1/§E3) touch F15.

Cross-cutting: (1) 15.1's 'no network activity' is the same fact as 21.5/N10 vs 22.3 — the catalogue contradicts itself, and the prior audit (docs/v2/AUDIT.md:149, :1208) split it as 15.1 PASS / 21.5 FAIL; I have marked 15.1 PARTIAL on the literal clause so the PO sees the contradiction in this section too. The update check is consent-gated by a sentence on the v1 welcome card (main.js:624-645) whose dismissal counts as disclosure — worth a PO look at whether that is the 'told once' 22.3 intends. (2) Server authorisation for mint/revoke is any active member (requireActiveMember), tighter only in the UI — a note for F20 (admin verbs), not a defect in 15.5. (3) The AUDIT.md 'F15 · LOW' block (lines 1145-1170) is about the security audit's F15 finding (withoutForeignEntries), not this catalogue section; item 1 is closed by tests/tier1/spine-foreign-guard.test.js, items 2-7 are open docs/blast-radius notes. (4) Tests I would want that do not exist: a tier-2 row asserting the 'Einladung kopieren' button on the create-done screen writes invitationText to the clipboard (15.2's 'shareable' is code-read only); and a row pinning that the join screen's pre-redemption picker offers every tone (so a future 'taken colours in the invitation' change is visible).
sections.skeptic_notes: All five F15 verdicts (15.2, 15.3, 15.4, 15.5, 15.6) upheld at the stated confidence. Verified at HEAD ab00471: (a) every cited tier-2 row exists, is live (no skip/todo), and its assertions cover the catalogue clause as worded — family-createjoin.dom.js:294-343 (one screen: #circle-name, #circle-display, PALETTE swatches; code matches Crockford pattern; role === admin; relay saw exactly POST /spaces then POST /invites), :396-443 (zero password/email inputs, paste normalises and takes origin, redeem body keys exactly [colorRef, device, inviteId, member, proof], role member); family-members.dom.js:215-233, :254-274, :276-304; family-admin.dom.js:245-256, :306-318, :634-644; join-paste.dom.js:411+ control row. (b) I ran tests/fleet/e10-fleet-circle.test.js myself: 14 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped, including §15.2, §15.3, §15.4, §15.5a/b/c, §15.6; and tests/tier1/createjoin.test.js: 31 pass. (c) The fleet §15.6 helper (e10:120-122) calls the real store.apply('setMyProfile'), the same op the shipped port wires at src/js/family/mount.js:282-289 (core/ops.js:1149 registers it), so the tier-2 fake-port rows and the fleet propagation rows close the chain end to end. (d) Code paths confirmed: createjoin.js:1807-1836 done step renders #circle-code, TTL hint (INVITE_UI.ttlDays = 7 at :127, matching server INVITE_TTL_MS 604800000 at invites.js:52 and used at :192) and 'Einladung kopieren' via ports.clipboard(invitationText) with a fallback toast that the code is on screen — so 'shareable' does not depend on clipboard success; createjoin.js:1855-1955 renderJoinForm is one screen (paste, optional origin row from originField() at :1652, name, colour picker, submit); membersui.js:792 gates the member section only on a circle existing, not on role; chipNode (membersui.js) paints colorRef and initial; familysettings.js:175-177 mounts members section for everyone; mount.js is dynamically imported from main.js:133; invites.js:307 usedAt pre-check, :318 atomic consumeInvite, :308-309 revoked/expired → invite_invalid, :420-437 revokeInvite; adminpanel.js:869 buildInvites only for isAdmin, :1098 expiryLabel, :1104-1111 revoke button. (e) 15.6 'anytime': selfEditSupported (membersui.js:429) requires only a setProfile port, which the shipped mount always supplies when a circle exists — not gated on keysPending or sync state. All of F15's behaviour is web-layer, so no Swift/Tauri shell divergence applies. The auditor's scope note on 15.5 (relay authorises createInvite/revokeInvite on requireActiveMember at invites.js:182/:425; only the UI restricts to admin) is accurate and not contrary to the clause 'revocable by the admin'.

sections.title: Visibility (Privat / Belegt / Geteilt)

items.evidence: Ran: node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/fleet/e10-fleet-circle.test.js → 'ok 1 - §16.1 · private by default — an entry created with no level reaches nobody' (14/14 pass). The row (tests/fleet/e10-fleet-circle.test.js:417-447) creates a note with NO visibility argument, asserts visibility === 'privat', and asserts on both peers: seen()==null, registers().has(fk)===false, and the word never appears in the peer's register map; its second half asserts the pre-circle fixture note 'n-own' (tests/fleet/e6-attack-circle.js:65) is on no peer after the join. Code: src/js/core/visibility.js:139 DEFAULT_VISIBILITY='privat'; src/js/core/project.js:641 (absent register ⇒ privat); src/js/core/ops.js:1024 addCategory defaultVisibility='privat'; src/js/family/mount.js:44-51 (solo entries carry no visibility field; nothing re-levels on mount). tests/tier1/visibility.test.js 'P7d-c · 16.1 is structural — a Privat entry produces ZERO family ops' and 'C4-notLive · nothing here can re-publish an existing entry when a default changes' (ran: 28/28). tests/attack/e7-leak-routes.test.js ran 49/49.
items.note: Both clauses pinned: the default is privat (not a redacted op — zero family ops), and joining publishes nothing pre-existing. Solo/v1 entries have no visibility register at all, so a join cannot flip them.
items.text: Everything I create is private by default — joining a family changes nothing about existing or new entries until I explicitly share them — so oversharing is structurally impossible.

items.evidence: Ran fleet: 'ok 2 - §16.2 · the three levels, end to end, on somebody else's Mac' (tests/fleet/e10-fleet-circle.test.js:450-481): Privat ⇒ seen()==null on Mama; Belegt ⇒ redacted:true, level 'belegt', date visible, ownerId === Papa, Object.hasOwn(b,'text')===false, 'Therapie' absent from Mama's whole register map; Geteilt ⇒ redacted:false, text 'Omas Geburtstag'. Bars: fleet '§16.7' row asserts a Belegt bar carries startDate/endDate/ownerId and no label. Enum: src/js/core/ops.js:106 defaultVisibility enum V; tests/tier1/visibility.test.js 'X1 · the disclosure CLAIMS and the field ALLOWLISTS are the same table' (ran 28/28).
items.note: Applies to both notes (fnote) and bars (fbar); the redaction happens at the author (ADR 004) so 'no text' is absence on the wire, not an empty string.
items.text: Every note and bar has one of three visibility levels: Privat (only me), Belegt (others see that the range is taken, and by whom, but no text), Geteilt (others see everything) — so I can coordinate without disclosing.

items.clause: A personal category can set a default visibility for new entries in it

defence.reason: The finding stands, and is sharper than the auditor put it. Every clause of the catalogue sentence EXCEPT "can set" holds: the data model carries cat.defaultVisibility, all create paths read it exactly once via visibilityForNewEntry, changing it never re-levels existing entries, the category field never syncs, and the global default stays 'privat'. But the shipped product has no control anywhere that writes the field after creation, and its only UI create site omits the argument. I checked beyond the auditor's scope: (1) ops.js has no setter op at all — the category op family is toggleCategory / addCategory / renameCategory / recolorCategory / deleteCategory / deleteCategoryReassign, and only addCategory's build accepts defaultVisibility (defaulting 'privat'); (2) legend.js:482-489 is the only addCategory call site and passes id/name/nameEn/paletteRef only; (3) the category row (legend.js:505-575) has name input, ten swatches, count, delete — no level control; (4) family/familysettings.js lines 784/927 that reference a `level` are the moderation list of OTHER members' published entries, and that file contains no category reference; (5) settings.js has no category UI; (6) i18n.js has no string for a category default (only the generic level words geteilt/belegt/privat at :482/:890); (7) every test that sets the default bypasses the UI — tier-2 sharing-control.dom.js:835/851/856 use store.txn + tx.cat(catId).set({defaultVisibility}), fleet e10-fleet-circle.test.js:525-529 passes it as an addCategory argument; the fleet comment at :519-521 delegates "the WIRING of this rule into the create gesture" to tier 2, and tier 2 only drives the CREATE gesture, never a SET gesture. Decisive sharpening: docs/v2/adr/004-visibility-and-redaction.md:306-307 explicitly designs the control — "the legend's category editor states the default next to the swatch" — and legend.js catRow has no such element. So this is an ADR-specified control that was never built, not merely an unstated one. E7-VERIFICATION.md:67 (LZP-703 VERIFIED-HERE) and AUDIT.md:1209 (16.4 PASS) both rest on create-path evidence only. Shell is irrelevant here (pure web-layer UI; same in Swift and Tauri). PARTIAL is the right verdict: mechanism clauses hold, the user-facing "can set" clause fails.

defence.reason: The auditor is right and the finding stands as PARTIAL. The mechanism half of the sentence holds (a category's defaultVisibility is honoured by every create path, once, at creation; the global default stays privat), but the shipped product has no control by which a user can SET a category's default. I looked for every writer of cat.defaultVisibility in product code and found exactly one: the addCategory op's optional argument (src/js/core/ops.js:1024-1026), which the only UI caller (src/js/legend.js:482-488) never passes. No other op mutates the field (ops.js registered ops 1011-1074: toggleCategory/addCategory/renameCategory/recolorCategory/deleteCategory/deleteCategoryReassign — none carries defaultVisibility). The category manager row (legend.js:505-575) offers rename, ten swatches, a count and delete only; nothing in index.html or src/js/settings.js or src/js/family/* touches it; src/js/i18n.js has no string for it. Both tests that prove the mechanism seed the value from test code, not through a UI: tests/tier2/sharing-control.dom.js:835 uses tx.cat(catId).set({defaultVisibility:'belegt'}) and tests/fleet/e10-fleet-circle.test.js:525-527 passes defaultVisibility:'geteilt' directly to store.apply('addCategory'). Two sharpenings: (1) even the backup-import door cannot set it — src/js/core/replace.js:836-849 FORCES IMPORT_DEFAULTS.cat.defaultVisibility='privat' (replace.js:251) and merely records a "re-share" question, which src/js/sync/personal.js:409-414 only stores and no UI ever consumes (grep pendingReshares: only store.js and personal.js) — so a hand-edited file cannot do it either; (2) the product's own design promised at least a display: docs/v2/adr/004-visibility-and-redaction.md:306-307 says "the legend's category editor states the default next to the swatch", and legend.js catRow neither shows nor edits it. AUDIT.md:1209 and E7-VERIFICATION.md:67 marked 16.4 PASS/VERIFIED-HERE on mechanism evidence alone; traceability.json:2680-2688 already records the story as "fleet-partial" with an alsoNeeds that is still about the read side, not a setter. Suggested wording: PARTIAL — holds: "new entries in it take the category's default; the global default stays private (zero extra clicks once configured)"; fails: "a personal category can set a default visibility" — there is no user-reachable way to configure one, so "Familie ⇒ Geteilt" cannot happen in the shipped app.

Pinning suites that ran green on this machine at HEAD: tests/fleet/e10-fleet-circle.test.js (14/14), tests/fleet/e13-relaunch-sweep.test.js (13/13), tests/tier1/visibility.test.js (28/28), tests/tier1/unshare.test.js (26/26), tests/tier1/sync-family.test.js (27/27), tests/attack/e7-leak-{downgrade,observer,routes}.test.js (27/15/49), tests/attack/redaction-invariants.test.js (49/49); tier-2 rows cited from tests/tier2/sharing-control.dom.js, belegt-render.dom.js, density-808.dom.js, shell-offline-relaunch.dom.js (ran at HEAD per the brief; assertions opened and confirmed). Two findings the prior audits missed, both about reachability rather than mechanism: (1) 16.4 — no shipped UI writes a category's defaultVisibility (legend.js addCategory/catRow offer rename/recolour/delete only; no i18n string exists), so 'Familie ⇒ Geteilt' cannot be configured by a person; every test drives it through the op argument. (2) 16.3 — the three-state control exists only in the day popover; a selected entry on the board has no control, and the popover is reached by right-click or the '+n' chip, so the two-click budget holds only from an open popover. Stale documentation: docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1210 still says 16.6 FAIL (F4) although AUDIT.md:147 / FINDINGS.md:5108 record F4 CLOSED and FI-4a passes under relaunch; AUDIT.md:1209 marks 16.3 and 16.4 PASS without the selected-state or the UI check. Tests I would want that do not exist: a tier-2 row that builds a category with a non-default visibility THROUGH the legend's category manager (would fail today — no control), and a row that counts gestures from a selected board entry (not an open popover) to a changed level. Nothing in F16 is shell-level, so the Tauri/Swift split does not bear on these verdicts.

The failing part is the NAME: nothing in src/js ever calls popover.useMemberNames, so every surface reading memberNameOf (popover.js:340, find.js:246, print.js:199) shows the initial instead of 'Mama'. Every green row that shows 'von Mama' injects its own resolver (family-attribution.dom.js:51, fleet §17.6), so no test pins the shipped mount. defence.reason: The auditor is right, and every one of their citations checks out at HEAD ab00471. The display-name port exists (src/js/popover.js:80 useMemberNames / :93 memberNameOf) but nothing in the shipped code installs it: `grep -rn useMemberNames src shell-macos src-tauri/src` returns only the definition at popover.js:80. src/js/family/mount.js:52 imports `useSharing, memberNameOf` (not useMemberNames) and its only port calls are useSharing at :271 and installConflictNotice({nameOf: memberNameOf}) at :399 — passing the uninstalled resolver through. Neither production caller of openDayPopover passes opts.nameOf (src/js/interact.js:420 and :430 pass only {onChange}), so popover.js:169 falls through to memberNameOf, which returns null (popover.js:94 `if (!memberNames ...) return null`), and sharing.js:384-388 `who()` then falls back to entry.initial. The shipped row-title therefore reads "von M · geteilt · geändert So.", exactly the shape family-attribution.dom.js:170-172 pins as the UNINSTALLED case; that same row only reaches "von Mama" after calling popover.useMemberNames itself at :174, and the file's scaffolding installs its own resolver at :51. The fleet §17.6 row (tests/fleet/e10-fleet-board.test.js:353-363) builds nameOf by hand from readMembers and calls attributionLine directly — it never exercises the mount. I ran it (pass 12 / fail 0) and it is green precisely because it bypasses the missing wiring. A roster name lookup does exist (src/js/family/membersui.js:768 memberNameFor) but its only caller is familysettings.js:920 (the 18.3 moderation list), not any 17.6 surface. Board-level hover also carries no attribution: board.js:1126 sets a foreign note's title to [text, exposureTitle] and :1140-1143 redactedTitle is '<initial> · Belegt'. The project's own ledgers agree: FINDINGS.md §12e E8-6 (OPEN), E8-VERIFICATION.md:88 'OWED (hover, names)', STATUS.md:915-917. AUDIT.md:1211 marks 17.6 PASS, but that table cites fleet rows, which (per above) hand-build the resolver. What holds: the level word 'geteilt', the weekday 'geändert So.', the popover-row placement (popover.js:416 sets txt.title = attribution(n)), and 'never printed on the board' (family-attribution.dom.js:313 row). PARTIAL is the correct verdict; the failing clause is the NAME ('Mama' ships as 'M') and, secondarily, the board-hover half of 'Hover/popover'.

The shipped product has the plumbing for a display name but never connects it: src/js/popover.js:80 defines useMemberNames (the only installer of the `memberNames` resolver at :73) and a repo-wide grep for `useMemberNames` finds NO caller anywhere under src/ — src/js/family/mount.js:52 imports only `useSharing, memberNameOf`, and mount.js:271 installs `useSharing(circle ? sharing : null)` with no matching name install. (that exact shape is what sharing-control.dom.js:774-775 asserts as the roster-less case). The three readers of the port — popover.js:169/340 (row text title at :416 and the row line), find.js:246, print.js:199 — all inherit the initial. The web payload Tauri ships is a verbatim copy of src/ (scripts/build-frontend.mjs:40 SHIP=['index.html','src'], :63 cpSync), so this is shell-independent and applies to the released DMG. Every green test showing "von Mama" hand-installs its own resolver: tests/tier2/family-attribution.dom.js:51 (`popover.useMemberNames(...)` at module top, again at :174, :607, :642 — :167 even documents "without it, the initial"); tests/fleet/e10-fleet-board.test.js:359-362 builds `nameOf` from readMembers by hand and calls attributionLine directly, never through the mount (I ran it: pass 1, fail 0 — it proves the sentence-builder, not the shipped wiring). No tier-1/attack/property/fleet file references useMemberNames or memberNameOf at all, so nothing pins the mount. Second, independent gap on the "hover" half: board.js:1126 sets a foreign shared note's grid tooltip to [text, exposureTitle] — no "von", no level, no weekday — and board.js:1140-1143 redactedTitle for a Belegt block is "<initial> · Belegt", never a name and never a weekday. items.note: Upload-within-seconds, the ~30–60 s pull, and the no-button/no-refresh clauses all hold with tests that would regress. The literal clause 'on app focus' is not implemented: the only foreground trigger is document `visibilitychange`, which on macOS WKWebView fires on minimise/occlusion/⌘H, not on a plain ⌘-Tab back to a still-visible window (native edge inferred). In practice the 45–60 s tick bounds staleness to one minute, and main.js:486 already shows a `window.addEventListener('focus', …)` hook exists for the clock — wiring cadence.wake to it would close this. Prior docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1218 graded 19.2 PASS on the cadence alone.

defence.reason: The finding stands: three of the four clauses hold and the literal "on app focus" clause is not implemented in the shipped page, in either shell. I tried the refutation routes — a shell-forwarded focus event, a push path that also pulls, a real-time relay channel, a tier-2 row that dispatches focus and asserts a pull — and each closes. (1) Neither shell forwards window focus to the page: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1564-1570 `on_window_event` handles only `WindowEvent::CloseRequested`; the only other `emit` is the menu id at :1562; shell-macos/main.swift has no didBecomeActive/didBecomeKey hook (its evaluateJavaScript calls at :1538, :2463, :2469 are context-menu, menu id, beforeprint). Both shells agree, so this is a page-level gap, not a shell divergence. (2) The page's only foreground triggers are in src/js/family/engine.js:275-279 — `visibilitychange`, `online`, `pagehide`; `wake` is returned at :282 and no other module calls it (grep of src/js for `.wake`/`cadence` finds only comments). main.js:486 has a `window.addEventListener('focus', tick)` but that `tick` (:473-482) is the date-roll clock, not sync. (3) The blur-commit path (main.js:651) only arms the 2 s push — personal.js:1858-1861 store.subscribe → schedulePush → :1891 `pushNow()`, which is a push only; the pull-then-push pairing lives in `syncNow()` (:1730-1747) and is reached only from driveCadence. (4) The relay has no push channel: grep of server/ for event-stream/EventSource/WebSocket finds nothing, so nothing "arrives" between polls. (5) The one tier-2 row that dispatches `focus` (tests/tier2/network-audit.dom.js:155-157) asserts the OPPOSITE — that a solo session opens no socket — so it does not verify a family pull on focus. Sharpening the auditor's note: the design itself intends focus as a trigger. docs/v2/adr/003-sync-protocol.md:1249 (ADR 003 §8.2, the cadence table for "19.2 as amended in v2.1") lists "`focus`, `visibilitychange → visible`, `online` | pull all configured spaces immediately", and tests/attack/privacy-e5-metadata.test.js:312-313 pins that doc line — but the same test's code assertions at :305-309 check only the visibilitychange/online/pagehide listeners, so the spec-vs-code gap on `focus` is pinned by no test. The auditor's WKWebView claim (visibilitychange tracks occlusion, not key-window status, so a ⌘-Tab back to an unoccluded window fires nothing) is consistent with WebKit's page-visibility model but I could not verify it natively here (launching the app is forbidden); the 45–60 s tick bounds the staleness either way. The holding clauses are confirmed: personal.js:209 `pushDebounceMs: 2000` with the debounced-push row in tests/tier1/sync-personal.test.js; personal.js:210-212 and engine.js:253-256 give 45 s + [0,15 s) visible; ran `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/sync-protocol.test.js` → "ok 1 - visible is 45 s ± 15 s and hidden is a flat 10 min", "# pass 50 / # fail 0"; no-button rows in tests/tier2/sync-status.dom.js as the auditor cites. Verdict PARTIAL, failing clause "on app focus", with the added weight that ADR 003 §8.2 promises it.

defence.reason: The finding stands and is sharpened. The only foreground pull trigger is document `visibilitychange`; there is no `focus` listener anywhere that reaches the sync engine, in the web layer or in either shell. This is not an over-literal reading of the catalogue: the product's own ADR 003 §8.2 (docs/v2/adr/003-sync-protocol.md:1249) and the sync contract (docs/v2/contracts/sync.contract.js:185-186) list `focus` as a trigger DISTINCT from `visibilitychange → visible` and `online`; engine.js implements two of the three. The exported `cadence.wake` handle (engine.js:264-268, :284) has no caller anywhere in src/js. The one app-level focus hook (src/js/main.js:486) drives the clock tick only. Neither shell bridges activation to the page (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1564-1570 handles only CloseRequested; lib.rs:1546 set_focus is the tray click setting focus, not reacting to it; shell-macos/main.swift has no didBecomeActive/didBecomeKey hook), so the two shells agree and the gap is shared, not a shell divergence. No test asserts a focus-driven pull: the only test that dispatches `focus` is the solo zero-socket row in tests/tier2/network-audit.dom.js:157, which asserts the opposite direction. The other three clauses (2 s debounced upload, 45–60 s visible pull, no sync button/refresh anywhere) hold with pinned code and tests, so PARTIAL with failing clause "on app focus" is the right grade. The prior PASS at docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1218 cited only engine.js:244-277 for the cadence and never examined the focus clause. Practical impact is bounded to one 45–60 s tick after a ⌘-Tab that does not change occlusion; the WKWebView-visibility edge is inferred from WebKit behaviour, not run here (tier 2 forbidden this session).

FAILS: tests/tier1/sync-personal.test.js row 'OWED, and asserted so it cannot be forgotten: a Mac WITHOUT that board.json gets none of it' — passes at HEAD asserting `F.B.store.state.notes.length === 0` after the paired fresh Mac pulls (run output: 'ok 5 - OWED, and asserted…'). Code: src/js/store.js:2745 `_buildSpine(board, { restamp: !!binding })` with `binding` = family lineage only (store.js:1067), so a personal-only opt-in keeps every pre-opt-in entry at a GENESIS stamp; store.js:2444 `if (isGenesisStamp(op.ts)) continue;` excludes them from outbox(); src/js/family/pairflow.js and crypto/pairing.js carry recovery identity + key ring only (grep 'board' → nothing). Ledger: docs/v2/FINDINGS.md:1385 'E5-6 … HIGH · open', docs/v2/E5-VERIFICATION.md:551, docs/v2/STATUS.md:2020 'E5-6 is unchanged and is still what M1 does not deliver'.
items.note: Pairing works, delivers the full key ring (epoch 1 included), and everything authored after the personal space exists — private entries included — syncs end-to-end encrypted, personal scope disjoint from family. But a second Mac that does not already hold board.json receives NOTHING of the board planned before the opt-in (notes, bars, and the user's own categories — synced notes then get silently remapped to the receiving Mac's default categories, E5-VERIFICATION §E5-6). The product's own docs read 19.4 as 'my whole board from the moment the space exists', which is not the catalogue's wording. Workaround: restore a backup file on the new Mac first. Also: 19.4 has never been exercised in a shell (docs/v2/SHELL-VERIFICATION.md:453; AUDIT.md:1218 'relay store reads pairs 0'); all evidence is fleet/WKWebView with an in-process relay.

defence.reason: The auditor's failing clause holds up under independent verification at HEAD ab00471. The catalogue sentence (docs/v2/UX-AUDIT-CATALOGUE.md:216) promises my ENTIRE board syncs between my devices. What actually ships: (a) end-to-end encryption, private entries included, personal scope disjoint from family — HOLDS (tier-1 rows re-run, 75/75); (b) the key ring, epochs 1..e, is delivered by pairing — HOLDS (pairing.js assertContiguousFromOne + tier-2 row); (c) everything planned BEFORE the personal space existed never travels — a paired Mac that does not already hold board.json receives none of it, categories included. This is asserted by the product's own test row 'OWED … a Mac WITHOUT that board.json gets none of it', which passes asserting notes.length === 0 on the freshly paired Mac after a pull. Mechanism confirmed in code: migrateV1 stamps the spine at GENESIS (all-zeros device short); store.outbox() skips isGenesisStamp ops (store.js:2444); restamp only fires on a launch where the board carries a lineage AND the persisted log is absent/refused (the re-join path, store.js:2745/2776), so the normally adopted history keeps GENESIS stamps forever; the pairing payload (crypto/pairing.js buildPairingPayload) carries memberId, recovery keys and the key ring only; the new Mac's onPaired (family/mount.js:710-800) saves the ring, POSTs /devices/adopt, fetches the roster, writes settings and reloads — no board hand-over step exists, and the Tauri shell (src-tauri/src/lib.rs) has only load_board/save_board plus keychain re-pair, nothing pairing-related that moves a board. No refutation path exists: I searched src/js/sync, src/js/family, src/js/crypto for any snapshot/bootstrap/hand-over and found only the cursor/witness snapshots. Two sharpenings for the auditor: (1) their claim that `binding` is 'family lineage only' is slightly off — a lineage is minted for any durable log, personal included (store.js:5666) — but that changes nothing, because on a normal launch _adoptHistory keeps the persisted GENESIS-stamped spine and only the quarantine/re-join branch restamps; (2) the tier-2 row 'a full pairing in WKWebView ends with the second Mac reading the first Macs PRIVATE entries' is a KEY-level demonstration (decrypts one AES-GCM ciphertext sealed under epoch 1 with the restored ring, crypto-pairing.dom.js:220-250) — it never touches a store or a board, so it is evidence for key delivery, not for 'entire board' delivery. AUDIT.md:1218 marked 19.4 PASS but with the caveat that it has never run in a shell (relay reads 'pairs 0'), and SHELL-VERIFICATION.md:453 confirms no pairing was performed in a shell; E5-VERIFICATION §E5-6, FINDINGS.md:1389 and STATUS.md:2020 all carry it as HIGH/open. PARTIAL is the right verdict: two of three clauses hold (E2EE, my devices only / scope-disjoint), the 'entire board' clause fails for the case the story is written for — a second Mac that does not already have the file.
defence.evidence: RAN: `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/sync-personal.test.js` → `# pass 75 / # fail 0`, including `ok 5 - OWED, and asserted so it cannot be forgotten: a Mac WITHOUT that board.json gets none of it` and `ok 4 - …so the spine NEVER TRAVELS`. TEST-READ: tests/tier1/sync-personal.test.js:1580-1598 boots F.B with `{ board: null }` (bootMac at :248-252 seeds no board file), pairs it (peers=true, same F.spaceId), pulls from the relay seeded with A's push, then asserts `F.B.store.state.notes.length === 0` and that nothing was refused. tests/tier1/sync-personal.test.js:1551-1578 shows both Macs reproduce identical GENESIS-stamped ops and `outbox().length === 0` for the spine, 1 for a real edit. tests/tier2/crypto-pairing.dom.js:220-250 — row 'a full pairing in WKWebView ends with the second Mac reading the first Macs PRIVATE entries' decrypts a single ciphertext with `restored.personal.epochs.get(1)` and asserts epochs [1,2,3]; no store/board involved. CODE: src/js/store.js:2444 `if (isGenesisStamp(op.ts)) continue;` in outbox(); store.js:2626-2664 `_buildSpine` — migrateV1 ops appended unchanged unless `restamp`; store.js:2745 `_buildSpine(board, { restamp: !!binding })` with restamp consumed only on the `!hasLog` / refused-log branches (2747-2760), adopted history otherwise (`_adoptHistory`); store.js:1064-1074 `splitBoardEnvelope` (binding = board.json._v2 lineage); store.js:5666 lineage minted for any durable log. src/js/crypto/pairing.js:532-541 assertContiguousFromOne (ring must cover 1..e) and :578-600 buildPairingPayload doc listing memberId, RK_sig/RK_kex, personal+family epochs and nothing else; `grep -n -i board src/js/family/pairflow.js` → no hits. src/js/family/pairflow.js:238-283 finishAsNewDevice → onPaired with ring/epochs/identity only. src/js/family/mount.js:731-799 new-Mac onPaired: saveRingEpoch, POST /api/v1/devices/adopt, GET members roster, attestPeer, setSettings, persistNow, reload — no board transfer. src-tauri/src/lib.rs:80-86 load_board/save_board only; :281-293 keychain re-pair — no pairing hand-over. DOCS (verified independently): docs/v2/E5-VERIFICATION.md:551-577 §E5-6 ('pairing a Mac that does not already hold the board is not delivered', categories remap demonstration at :560-572); docs/v2/FINDINGS.md:1389 'E5-6 … HIGH · open'; docs/v2/STATUS.md:2020-2021; docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1218 '19.4 has never run in a shell — the relay store reads pairs 0'; docs/v2/SHELL-VERIFICATION.md:453 'no pairing was performed in a shell in this pass'.

defence.reason: The finding stands and the auditor's evidence reproduces exactly at HEAD ab00471. Three of the four clauses hold: (a) "end-to-end encrypted" — the relay stores only ciphertext (tests/tier1/sync-personal.test.js row 'THE RELAY IS BLIND', passes); (b) "between my devices only" — a family envelope replayed at the personal door never opens, personal and family scope disjoint (§6 rows, pass); (c) "including private entries" — a private entry authored after the personal space exists syncs (row 'a PRIVATE entry syncs too', pass), and the pairing payload delivers personal epochs 1..e so old ciphertext is readable (tests/tier2/crypto-pairing.dom.js row 'a full pairing in WKWebView ends with the second Mac reading the first Macs PRIVATE entries' — I opened it: it asserts decrypt under restored epoch 1 and epochs [1,2,3], but it decrypts a fresh ciphertext the test itself sealed; it never carries a board). The clause "my **entire** board" FAILS for the actual 19.4 scenario — a genuinely new second Mac: everything planned before the opt-in (notes, bars, and the user's own categories) is minted as a GENESIS-stamped spine from board.json (src/js/store.js:2745 `_buildSpine(board, { restamp: !!binding })`, with `binding` = family lineage only via splitBoardEnvelope store.js:1064-1067), and store.js:2444 `if (isGenesisStamp(op.ts)) continue;` keeps every one of those out of outbox(). Nothing else hands the board over: src/js/crypto/pairing.js:577-590 documents the pairing payload as memberId + recovery keys + key rings only; grep of src/js/family, src/js/crypto, src/js/sync finds no board.json/export/import transfer; src/js/family/pairingui.js's done screen (line 727-731) has no backup hint. The product's own tests pin the gap as a measurement: sync-personal 'OWED … a Mac WITHOUT that board.json gets none of it' (ran: ok 5, 75/75) asserts `F.B.store.state.notes.length === 0` after a paired fresh Mac pulls; tests/fleet/fleet-harness.test.js row 'THE COROLLARY, OWED' (ran: ok 2, 21/21) asserts `f.B.state.notes.length === 0` with seedAll:false. Worse, because default categories are spine ops too, synced notes arriving on the fresh Mac carry unknown categoryIds and store.js:434-438 silently remaps them to `categories[0]` (E5-VERIFICATION §E5-6 demonstration). The workaround (restore a §7.2 backup on the new Mac first, tests/fleet/e10-backup-restore.test.js §2) is out-of-band and not what the sentence says ("syncs"). Shell coverage: 19.4 has never been driven in either shell (AUDIT.md:1218 "relay store reads pairs 0", SHELL-VERIFICATION.md:453) and src-tauri/src/lib.rs has no pairing/board-transfer path of its own — all evidence is tier-1/fleet/WKWebView with an in-process relay. Ledger agrees: FINDINGS.md:1385 E5-6 HIGH open; STATUS.md:2020. PARTIAL is the right verdict, not FAIL: E2EE, device-only scope, and private-entry sync all hold; the missing piece is the pre-opt-in board on a Mac that does not already hold board.json.
defence.evidence: HOLDS — node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/sync-personal.test.js → "# tests 75 / # pass 75"; rows 'a PRIVATE entry syncs too — 19.4 is "my whole board"…' (line 363), 'THE RELAY IS BLIND…' (line 372), 'an empty key ring is a REFUSAL…' (line 403), §6 scope rows. tests/tier2/crypto-pairing.dom.js:220-250 row 'a full pairing in WKWebView ends with the second Mac reading the first Macs PRIVATE entries' — asserts decrypt with restored.personal.epochs.get(1) and `[...restored.personal.epochs.keys()] deepEqual [1,2,3]` (key ring only; no board bytes). src/js/crypto/pairing.js:577-590 payload = memberId, RK_sig/RK_kex, personal epochs, family epochs. FAILS — tests/tier1/sync-personal.test.js:1580-1595 row 'OWED, and asserted so it cannot be forgotten: a Mac WITHOUT that board.json gets none of it': `await bootMac(F.B, F, { board: null }); … eB.pullNow(); assert.equal(F.B.store.state.notes.length, 0, 'the pre-space board did NOT arrive over the wire — pairing owes the hand-over')` → run output "ok 5 - OWED…". tests/fleet/fleet-harness.test.js:433-449 row 'THE COROLLARY, OWED: a Mac that does NOT hold the board.json receives none of it': `createFleet({… seedAll: false}); assert.equal(f.B.state.notes.length, 0, 'B received NONE of it…')` → run "ok 2", 21/21. Code: src/js/store.js:2745 `const spine = this._buildSpine(board, { restamp: !!binding });` with binding from splitBoardEnvelope store.js:1064-1067 (family lineageId only); store.js:2444 `if (isGenesisStamp(op.ts)) continue;` in outbox(); store.js:434-438 `const fallback = s.categories[0].id; for (const n of s.notes) if (!ids.has(n.categoryId)) n.categoryId = fallback;` (silent category remap on the receiving Mac). src/js/family/pairingui.js:727-731 screenDone — no backup/restore hint. Shell: grep -n -i "pair|board.json|bootstrap|snapshot" src-tauri/src/lib.rs → only file I/O (lines 17-18, 90-96) and the LZP-1009 sync-off "one pair (method,path)" logic; no board hand-over. Ledger: docs/v2/FINDINGS.md:1385 "E5-6 — a paired Mac receives NONE of the pre-space board, categories included · HIGH · open"; docs/v2/E5-VERIFICATION.md:551-575 (category-id demonstration, "pairing a Mac that does not already hold the board is not delivered"); docs/v2/STATUS.md:2020; docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1218 "19.4 has never run in a shell — the relay store reads pairs 0"; docs/v2/SHELL-VERIFICATION.md:453 "no pairing was performed in a shell in this pass". Workaround only: tests/fleet/e10-backup-restore.test.js:533-545 (restore backup file, then sync continues).

items.text: I can pair my own second Mac: my entire board — including private entries — syncs end-to-end encrypted between my devices only.

items.clause: there are no passwords in this product
items.evidence: HOLDS: tests/tier1/crypto-pairing.test.js (ran, 57/57) rows 'a pairing code is 12 Crockford characters, uniform, and displayed XXXX-XXXX-XXXX', 'a full pairing over an honest relay ends with the new Mac reading my PRIVATE entries'; tests/tier2/pairing-flow.dom.js rows 'the code on screen is the code the session minted, formatted XXXX-XXXX-XXXX' (#pair-code matches Crockford, derives the rid that opens the published offer) and 'the Weiter button is dead until twelve characters are in the field'; src/js/family/pairflow.js:1-60 (rendezvous over the relay, no account, no reset); src/js/i18n.js:656-658 pairSectionHint 'No password: a code you read off one Mac and type into the other'; src/js/family/mount.js:361-365 mountSolo (the joiner needs no identity — a fresh install types the code). FAILS (literal): src/js/crypto/backup.js:347-349 `withPassword … label 'Backup mit Passwort sichern' / 'Protect the backup with a password'`, :354 'Nobody can reset the password'; src/js/settings.js:783-794 export sheet copy (PO decision D8).
items.note: Adding a device is exactly the described flow — a short code shown on the existing Mac, typed into the new one, key transfer, no password-reset. The one literal miss is that the product does contain a password: the optional passphrase on the backup file (D8's 'with password' export). It is not an account password and has no reset flow, so this may be an erratum for the catalogue rather than a product defect — flagged for the PO to decide. Residual touching this item: docs/v2/FINDINGS.md E5-5 (open) — the pairGet per-IP budget means a household pairing a third device within one hour sees a 429 that looks like a wrong code.

defence.reason: All three clauses hold on the shipped build. Pairing is a short code shown on one Mac and typed on the other with no reset flow (tier-1 crypto-pairing 57/57, crypto-guarantees 8/8 incl. the 19.5 MITM row; no 'passw' string in pairflow.js/pairingui.js/mount.js; tier-2 family-createjoin.dom.js:414 asserts zero input[type=password] on the circle screens in a real WKWebView). The auditor's literal miss rests on copy that never reaches a screen: the only <input type=password> in the codebase (familysettings.js:1121-1124) is drawn inside buildRecoverySection, which returns at :1100-1101 unless hooks.recoveryMaterial is a function, and the sole caller mount.js:191-193 passes only { onOptIn } — no file in src/, tests/, docs/ or dist/ supplies recoveryMaterial. So the 'Backup mit Passwort sichern' sheet (backup.js:347-354) is unreachable in v2.0.0-rc.3. Beyond that, the sentence's own source (V2-FINAL.md:884 / traceability.json:415) is defined by ADR 002:1290-1292: 'No passwords' forbids a registration-and-login system, not a passphrase on a key file the user chooses to carry. The only shipped residue is prose in the Datenschutz section (settings.js:780-794, rendered at :1020-1021) that describes an optional backup password — a description, not a password, and N1's concern rather than 19.5's. Sharpening for the PO: (1) footnote the catalogue clause to ADR 002 §7.2's definition so the item does not flip when the recovery sheet is wired; (2) separate defect outside 19.5 — familysettings.js:1085-1087 and STATUS.md:1995 claim P-4 (no entry point to the recovery file) is fixed via hooks.recoveryMaterial, but mount.js never passes it, so the passphrase-protected recovery export has no door in the shipped app; that belongs to the backup/recovery items (21.x, A2/D8). E5-5 (pairGet 429 on a third device within the hour) remains an open residual touching the pairing experience but not this clause.
defence.evidence: src/js/family/familysettings.js:1100-1101 (`if (!material) return;` gates the whole recovery sheet on hooks.recoveryMaterial); src/js/family/familysettings.js:1121-1124 (the only `pw.type = 'password'` in the codebase, inside that gated section); src/js/family/mount.js:191-193 (sole caller passes `{ onOptIn }` only); `grep -rn recoveryMaterial src/js tests docs dist` → only familysettings.js and its dist copy; docs/v2/adr/002-crypto.md:1290-1292 ("No passwords" forbids a registration and login system; does not forbid encrypting a key file); docs/v2/V2-FINAL.md:884 and docs/v2/traceability.json:415 (source of the catalogue sentence); tests/tier2/family-createjoin.dom.js:414 — row '15.3 — code paste, name, colour, done: no email, no password, no registration form' asserts `.circle input[type="password"]` count is 0; `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/crypto-pairing.test.js` → `# pass 57 # fail 0`; `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/crypto-guarantees.test.js` → `ok 6 - 19.5 — an active MITM relay that KNOWS the code still ends with both Macs refusing, and the attacker holding nothing`, `# pass 8`; tests/tier2/pairing-flow.dom.js rows 'the code on screen is the code the session minted, formatted XXXX-XXXX-XXXX' (:305), 'the Weiter button is dead until twelve characters are in the field' (:382), 'a full pairing: both screens show the SAME six digits, and the keys actually arrive' (:448); shipped prose residue: src/js/settings.js:780-794 (backupBody/lossBody mention 'Passwort'), rendered at settings.js:1020-1021; separate defect: familysettings.js:1085-1087 claims mount.js passes recoveryMaterial, docs/v2/STATUS.md:1995 and FINDINGS.md:142 record P-4 as fixed; docs/v2/FINDINGS.md:1373 E5-5 open.

defence.reason: The finding stands on the literal clause and cannot be refuted from the code: the shipped product does contain a password. src/js/family/familysettings.js:1121 creates an input with `pw.type = 'password'` (autocomplete 'new-password' at :1124) inside the export sheet that is built from EXPORT_SHEET_COPY, whose primary button is labelled 'Backup mit Passwort sichern' / 'Protect the backup with a password' (src/js/crypto/backup.js:349) and whose consequence line reads 'Nobody can reset the password' (:354). This is a real, reachable path — tests/fleet/e10-backup-restore.test.js (ran, 21/21) and tests/tier2/crypto-backup.dom.js row 'a wrong passphrase in WebKit gives the same one honest code, and writes nothing' exercise the passphrase-sealed export. So 'there are no passwords in this product' is false as stated. Everything else in the sentence holds and I re-verified it independently: the pairing flow has zero password/passphrase references (grep -c over src/js/family/pairflow.js = 0; src/js/family/pairingui.js no hits), tests/tier1/crypto-pairing.test.js re-ran 57/57, and tests/tier2/pairing-flow.dom.js row 'a full pairing: both screens show the SAME six digits, and the keys actually arrive' pins code-shown/code-typed key transfer with no reset flow. Sharpening for the PO: this is a catalogue-vs-source conflict, not a product defect, by the catalogue's own rule. docs/v2/PLAN.md:225 records PO decision D8 (dated 2026-08-25, the catalogue's own date) 'Export sheet gains one field and a two-button choice' in Delivery Plan v1.0 — a listed catalogue source whose 'fixed decisions' the header claims are 'already applied'; the catalogue header also says 'On any conflict between this catalogue and the spec documents, the specs govern and this catalogue receives an erratum'. DESIGN-DECISIONS.md:260-263 and docs/v2/adr/002-crypto.md:1290-1292 both read addendum §3's 'no passwords' as forbidding a registration/login system, and the sheet says so to the user (backup.js:415-420 'Das ist kein Konto-Passwort … geht nie an einen Server'). Verdict should stay PARTIAL until the PO issues the erratum (rewording 19.5 and N1 to 'no account passwords'), after which the item is PASS; N1 carries the identical clause and must receive the same erratum. The E5-5 residual (docs/v2/FINDINGS.md:1373, open, pairGet per-IP budget) touches 19.5's pairing UX but not this clause.

If it is gone, this backup is gone.'; `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/fleet/e10-backup-restore.test.js` → '# tests 21 / # pass 21 / # fail 0' (passphrase-sealed identity block is real); tests/tier2/crypto-backup.dom.js rows 'a wrong passphrase in WebKit gives the same one honest code, and writes nothing' and 'S7 in WebKit: the passphrase floor is the same floor…' (tier 2 PASS at HEAD). Delivery Plan v1.0, 'fixed decisions already applied', 'specs govern and this catalogue receives an erratum'); docs/v2/PLAN.md:216-225 (PO decisions dated 2026-08-25; D8 'Export sheet gains one field and a two-button choice'); DESIGN-DECISIONS.md:255-263 ('This does not contradict "no passwords" (addendum §3). That principle forbids a registration and login system'); docs/v2/adr/002-crypto.md:1290-1292 (same reading) and :1399-1400 (no PIN/re-auth because that WOULD contradict 'no passwords'); src/js/crypto/backup.js:414-420 notAnAccount copy shown on the sheet. items.text: Adding a device means entering a short pairing code shown on an existing device — not a password-reset flow; there are no passwords in this product.

items.evidence: Ran: node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/fleet/long-offline.test.js → '# tests 12 / # pass 12'. §1 'it opens, catches up, and the two boards are byte-identical' (laptop close()+offline(); 21 days advanced with one edit per day crossing 10 Dec → 31 Dec; laptop open()+catchUp(); all 21 notes present; boardsAgree byte-identical incl. register stamp+author); §1 'the month roll is not data: the two Macs' WINDOWS differ and their BOARDS do not' (a roll emits 0 ops, boards agree); §1 'a yearly repeat crosses the year boundary, and 9.4's Feb-29 rule holds on both Macs' (4 weeks over New Year, anchor '2024-02-29' unchanged on both, projectYearly 2027→02-28, 2028→02-29); §1 'the bar that spans the year boundary is one bar, and it survives the catch-up'; §2b 'the desktop compacts its log while the laptop is away, and the laptop still catches up'; §3 'the outbox drains in opsPerPush batches, however long the device was away' (260 ops → ≥2 batches, outbox 0). Also ran tests/fleet/attack-converge-outbox.test.js → 9/9.
items.note: The fleet harness is two real store.js module evaluations with real disks, the real sync/personal.js engine and the real server handlers (tests/helpers/fleet.js:14-33), driven by a simulated clock — the strongest evidence short of two physical Macs. Month rolls and yearly repeats are pure projections of the clock, so they cannot diverge by construction (ADR 003 §3.4), and the rows assert it.
items.text: After long offline periods everything merges cleanly on return — including month rolls and yearly repeats that occurred meanwhile — so a laptop opened after three weeks just catches up.

items.clause: with both-ends confirmation

defence.reason: The finding stands and the auditor's clause is the right one. Both ends have designed screens and the both-ends SAS confirmation is real and proven in a WKWebView — but only over an in-process relay. In the shipped Tauri shell (and identically in the Swift shell) the second, fresh Mac's very first request (anonymous GET /api/v1/pair/:rid) is routed through `sync_request`, which refuses everything except POST /api/v1/feedback while the shell pref `sync_enabled` is false; that pref defaults to false, and nothing in the pairing path (pairflow.js, pairingui.js, mount.js) ever arms it. `armShellSync()` fired on settings-open returns 'no-space' for a Mac with no space, and the only `optIn:true`/`armGate3()` callers are the Familienkreis create/join clicks (familysettings.js:480, createjoin.js:1761/2000), not pairing. So on the joiner the `guard` catches the NetError('blocked', sync_disabled) and sets errorCode; the SAS state is never entered on Mac 2, Mac 1 never receives an answer, and the both-ends confirmation cannot happen in the product as shipped. No tier-2 file that exercises `sync_request` touches pairing, and SHELL-VERIFICATION.md records no pairing was ever driven in a shell. Screens: PASS. Both-ends confirmation: mechanism proven in isolation, unreachable in the shipped shell → PARTIAL. Sharpening: the defect is the second (fresh) Mac only — the first Mac is armed by its own opt-in — and it is shell-independent (Tauri lib.rs:1077 and Swift main.swift:1199 gate identically), so this is a product-code gap (no arming at the pairing opt-in), not a shell divergence.

defence.reason: The finding stands; I could not refute it and the chain is tighter than the auditor stated. The "designed screens on both ends" clause holds (real screens, verified in a real WKWebView by tier 2). The "both-ends confirmation" clause holds for the UI and the crypto state machine but is UNREACHABLE in the shipped Tauri shell on a fresh second Mac: the joiner's first network act is an anonymous GET /api/v1/pair/:rid (pairflow.js:318 via :181), it travels through lazyAnon → chooseTransport({invoke}) → createBridgeTransport → invoke('sync_request'); the Tauri preflight refuses with SYNC_DISABLED whenever SyncPrefs.enabled is false (default) unless the request is exactly POST /api/v1/feedback (lib.rs:1012-1019, :1077-1078); the reply {error:'blocked', reason:'sync_disabled'} becomes a NetError and pairflow's guard turns it into errorCode 'blocked' before session.answerAsNew ever runs, so the joiner never reaches the SAS screen and Mac 1's offer expires unanswered. Nothing in the pairing path arms gate 3: armGate3 is called only from createjoin.js:1761/:2000 and familysettings.js:352, and armShellSync() without optIn returns 'no-space' on a Mac with no space (familysettings.js:342-349). The Swift shell has the identical gate (main.swift preflight line 1199-1200: `if !SyncPrefs.load().enabled && !syncSoloSendIsAllowed(url, method: method) { return .failure(.syncDisabled) }`), so both shells agree — this is not a shell mismatch, it is a product gap in both. Sharpenings: (1) the tier-2 rows the auditor cites do NOT exercise the shipped src/js/family/pairflow.js at all — pairing-flow.dom.js and pairing-sas.dom.js import pairingui.js + crypto/pairing.js and drive them with the test's own reference `makeFlow` (pairing-flow.dom.js:115) over `makeRelay()` (:76); pairflow.js is referenced only by static attack tests (privacy-e5-endpoint.test.js:319,:526; sync-domains.js:870). So "real UI + real crypto over an in-process relay" is right but "the shipped flow" is not covered by any tier-2 row. (2) The only end-to-end two-Mac pairing ever demonstrated (M1, docs/v2/E5-VERIFICATION.md:352-354) ran in Chrome on createFetchTransport before any shell implemented sync_request, so gate 3 did not apply to it. (3) Narrow escape that does not rescue the story: a second Mac whose gate 3 was already armed by a different opt-in (it created or joined a Familienkreis via createjoin.js) would pass the gate on the joiner path, but that Mac is then a different member, not the fresh own-device of 19.4/19.5. Verdict PARTIAL, failing clause "with both-ends confirmation" — more precisely: the joiner cannot reach the SAS/confirmation step in either shipped shell from a fresh install.

Suites run here at HEAD, all green: tier1 sync-queue 39/39, sync-personal 75/75, crypto-pairing 57/57, platform-net 21/21; fleet long-offline 12/12, e10-fleet-board 12/12, e10-fleet-circle 14/14, attack-converge-outbox 9/9. Disagreements with docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1218 (which graded all six PASS): 19.4 is PARTIAL because FINDINGS E5-6 is still open at HEAD and is pinned by a passing 'OWED' row asserting the gap (sync-personal.test.js ~:1553) — a freshly paired Mac gets none of the pre-opt-in board or the user's own categories; 19.2 is PARTIAL on the literal 'on app focus' (visibilitychange only); 19.5 is PARTIAL on the literal 'no passwords' (D8's optional backup password) — the last two are candidates for a catalogue erratum rather than product defects. Residuals touching this section: E5-6 (HIGH, open, owner WP-9: board.json hand-over at pairing), E5-5 (pairGet per-IP budget, third device within an hour), and 'no pairing has ever been performed in a shell' (SHELL-VERIFICATION.md:453, AUDIT.md 'relay store reads pairs 0'). Tests I would want that do not exist: (1) a cadence row asserting a pull on window `focus` (or a decision that visibilitychange is the intended trigger); (2) a shell-level two-instance pairing across sync_request (pair/offer + devices/adopt) in scripts/shell-family-e2e; (3) the inverse of the 'OWED' row once E5-6 closes — a fresh Mac receiving the whole pre-space board with its category ids intact; (4) an offline row exercising edit/move/undo (not only create) against the outbox, though the code path is the same store door.

items.note: All five verbs are wired end to end and pinned. Two honest caveats the code itself states: the `isAdmin` gate is presentational — the relay has no role column and any current member can call /members/remove and /spaces/:id/delete (adminpanel.js:69-84, server/core/handlers/lifecycle.js:33-46); what bounds that is the co-signature gate for removing the founder / any removal once the founder is gone / every delete of a real circle (lifecycle.js:458-470, 732-741) and the in-log authz that refuses rename/transfer from a non-admin. docs/v2/E6-VERIFICATION.md §3.6 measured rename propagation on two Macs and records E6-2 (transfer was a one-way demotion) as CLOSED; the tier-2 row was inverted accordingly.
items.text: As admin I can invite, revoke invites, remove members, rename the space, and transfer the admin role to another member.

items.note: 'Server data is purged' and 'fully intact' both hold (the relay cascades everything; nothing local is deleted anywhere). 'Every member reverts to a solo board' holds only for the admin who pressed delete. Every other member is left in a phantom circle: a permanent auth error in the sync status, foreign entries still projected (familySpaceId still armed), an admin panel whose only exit fails with not_a_member, and no way to create or join a new circle (20.6) — short of hand-editing prefs. No fleet or tier-2 row drives a remaining member's Mac after a delete; the earlier E6 pass (7d4aa91 §3.6) deleted a single-member circle on the admin's own Mac only. sections.section_notes:
Where F20 lives: src/js/family/adminpanel.js (the section and the relay port), src/js/family/leavedelete.js (LIFECYCLE_COPY, the four confirmations, the co-signature sheets), src/js/family/removal.js (rotation + `member.set{_alive:false}` after a removal), server/core/handlers/lifecycle.js (remove/leave/transfer/rename/delete), with the tier-2 pin in tests/tier2/family-admin.dom.js and the multi-Mac pins in tests/fleet/e6-removal, e6-attack-removed, e6-gate-removal. Everything here is web-layer; the Tauri shell (src-tauri/src/lib.rs) plays no role, so no shell divergence applies. The production relay's 20.4 purge rests on Prisma `onDelete: Cascade` (server/prisma/schema.prisma) — verified present on every Space relation.

Two defects found, both with the same shape (a Mac is never told it is out): (1) 20.3 — a voluntary leave authors no in-log op and triggers no rotation, so the leaver's shared entries remain on every remaining board that already folded them; SHELL-VERIFICATION.md F-SHELL-2 (STATUS.md:509, still open) is the same root cause seen from the co-signer count. (2) 20.4 — after a delete (and equally after a 20.2 removal), the non-admin members' Macs stay armed into the vanished circle: sync shows `syncErrAuth`, „Kreis verlassen" fails with 403 not_a_member before `forgetCircle` runs, and 20.6 blocks a new circle. A 403 not_a_member on /members/leave should be treated as 'already out'.

Residual ledgers touched: docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1220 marks 20.2 FAIL (F3); STATUS.md:159 says closed — confirmed by running tests/audit/compaction-sweep.test.js (§2b/§2c now assert refusal / no resurrection and pass). That suite's §0a/§0b fail at HEAD (expects 0 retained lines; `_persistOps` deliberately retains admin-chain lines) — stale expectations, not a 20.2 regression, but the suite is red and should be re-titled. tests/attack/ownership-authz-admin.test.js keeps 10 fold-layer rows OPEN (A2*, A3b/A3c, A3d, A4, A5*) — A3b (admin of an invented space evicts a member of yours) and A5 (removed member re-admits herself) touch 20.2 at the authz layer and are bounded only by relay revocation; FINDINGS.md G-1 (WP-9) open. The 'visibility' truth register is never reverted on leave — worth an explicit PO decision (revert on leave vs. keep the person's choice).

Tests I would want that do not exist: (a) fleet: member leaves → assert their Geteilt entries leave the remaining boards and an epoch rotation happens; (b) fleet/tier-2: admin deletes → a remaining member's Mac reverts to solo (or at least its leave succeeds); (c) leave, then join a fresh circle → a previously-shared entry is not republished on its next edit; (d) a tier-2 row that the removed/deleted member's phantom circle offers a working exit.

sections.title: Privacy and security, as experienced

items.evidence: tests/tier1/crypto-guarantees.test.js:167 row '21.1 — a sealed op's bytes contain NO plaintext field: the relay holds ciphertext and a routing header, and nothing else' (asserts no op.f value, entity key, kind, actor, deviceId or group id appears on the wire; wrap blob never contains the raw space key) — ran: `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/crypto-guarantees.test.js` → '# pass 8 / # fail 0'. server/prisma/schema.prisma:199-212 (Op.envelope, Op.chain, Op.witness are Bytes; KeyWrap.wrapped Bytes at :292-301 — the server holds only wrapped keys addressed to recipient devices). tests/attack/crypto-relay-read.test.js:37 'T1 holds the envelope and no key: there is no content in any of the nine wire fields' (12/12 pass). tests/fleet/e6-gate-privat.test.js:83 §1c 'purging the founder yields ciphertext and a member list, and nothing else' (7/7 pass).
items.note: All clauses hold end to end: shared and Belegt entries are sealed in the page (src/js/crypto/envelope.js), the relay's schema can only store Bytes for content columns, and keys reach the server only as per-device wraps (KeyWrap) — no plaintext key column exists. Honest limit, already disclosed in 21.3's copy: the relay sees the routing header (space id, epoch, deviceShort, padded size, arrival time), which is metadata, not content.
items.text: Shared and Belegt entries are end-to-end encrypted; only member devices hold keys — the server stores ciphertext it cannot read.

items.evidence: tests/tier1/crypto-guarantees.test.js:249 row '21.2 / 20.5 — the family key can NEVER decrypt a personal-space op, and no role in this layer can ask it to' (openOp with FSK on a personal envelope → 'aead'; relabelled envelope → 'P3'; personalRecipients throws on a family device list) and :498 row '19.4 — a private entry sealed on my first Mac opens on my second, end to end through pairing, with the relay holding nothing' — both pass (8/8). src/js/sync/personal.js:435-445 (`assertPersonalSpace` throws on any non-`psp_` id — 'A family space is not a fallback here (story 21.2)'). tests/fleet/e6-gate-privat.test.js:83 §1b: 'zero bytes of the Privat entry in the entire ciphertext stream' asserted over a raw GET /api/v1/ops of the whole family stream (7/7 pass). tests/tier1/crypto-spacekeys.test.js:154 '20.5: a family key applied to a personal envelope FAILS' and :561 'KeyRing: a key put under one space is NEVER returned for another' (44/44 pass).
items.note: Both clauses hold: private entries produce no family op at all (absence, not redaction — e6-gate-privat §1b reads the raw relay stream), and the personal-space engine structurally refuses a family space id. Also re-proved by tests/attack/redaction-invariants (49/49), e7-leak-* (91 rows) and privacy-e5-* (58 rows), all run at HEAD in this session.
items.text: Private entries never leave my machines except end-to-end encrypted to my *own* paired devices — no family key can ever decrypt them.

items.clause: no third-party services beyond the sync endpoint
items.note: 'No analytics, no tracking' holds by construction (one fetch site, CSP, no telemetry crate). But GitHub Releases is a second third-party service the shipped Tauri build talks to for the update manifest and the signed artefact — by design (22.3/22.8) and disclosed (settings.js updateBody 'bei GitHub … GitHub gehört zu Microsoft und steht nicht in der EU'; thirdBody 'Vercel, Prisma Postgres und GitHub sind alle Stellen, die es gibt'). The catalogue's 21.4 wording contradicts its own 22.3/22.8; prior AUDIT.md:1223 reached the same FAIL. Needs a catalogue erratum, not a code change.

defence.reason: The finding stands. The shipped Tauri build contacts a second remote host — GitHub Releases — for the update manifest and signed artefact, which contradicts the literal clause "no third-party services beyond the sync endpoint" (and N10's "no third-party calls beyond the single sync endpoint") while being required by 22.3/22.8 of the same catalogue. The tier-2 network-audit PASS rows cannot refute this: they watch the WKWebView resource timeline and page CSP, and the update GET is native Rust (tauri-plugin-updater/reqwest), invisible to them by construction. The product's own attack test already codifies TWO sanctioned hosts, not one. The first clause ("no analytics, no tracking") holds. Sharpening: the GitHub contact is consent-gated (disclosed defaults false, set only from screens showing the sentence), user-switchable, and disclosed in plain German on the Datenschutz screen — so PARTIAL (not FAIL), and the remedy is a catalogue erratum to 21.4/N10, not a code change.
defence.evidence: docs/v2/UX-AUDIT-CATALOGUE.md:236 (21.4 wording), :266 (N10 same clause), :245 (22.3), :250 (22.8). src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:63-66 plugins.updater.endpoints = "https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/releases/latest/download/latest.json"; .github/workflows/release.yml:143-153 substitutes OWNER/REPO with GITHUB_REPOSITORY; src-tauri/src/lib.rs:498-528 update_fetch_manifest → updater.check().await (native fetch). Consent gate: lib.rs:338-341 Default { enabled: true, disclosed: false }; lib.rs:502 and :557 refuse unless disclosed && enabled; src/js/update-ui.js:349-352 discloseUpdateCheck() is the only setter; lib.rs:398 update_set_enabled. Disclosure copy: src/js/settings.js:761-768 ("Die zweite Gegenstelle: die Update-Prüfung … bei GitHub … GitHub gehört zu Microsoft und steht nicht in der EU"), :798-800 ("Vercel, Prisma Postgres und GitHub sind alle Stellen, die es gibt"). Tests run from repo root: `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/attack/e10-network-scope.test.js` → "# pass 32 / # fail 0", where row '§1g · the WHOLE PRODUCT names exactly TWO remote hosts, and both are sanctioned' (tests/attack/e10-network-scope.test.js:210-240) asserts hosts.length === 2 and exactly one latest.json manifest URL; `node --test --import ./tests/helpers/dev-flag.mjs tests/tier1/network-scope.test.js` → "# pass 21 / # fail 0". tests/tier2/network-audit.dom.js rows at :71 ('§1 solo · the launch made no request off its own origin, and no API call'), :138, :181 observe page resources/CSP only — not the shell's reqwest. src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:28 CSP connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost binds the page only. Feedback uses the same relay origin: src/js/feedback/relay.js:147-163, admin.js:34 (no third host). `gh release view v2.0.0-rc.3 --json assets` → latest.json 2008 B, LangzeitPlaner-2.0.0-rc.3-universal.app.tar.gz 9068696 B, .sig 416 B. Prior audit docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1223 "21.4 FAIL — GitHub Releases is a third-party service beyond the sync endpoint".

defence.reason: The auditor's PARTIAL is correct and the evidence is accurate for the shipped Tauri shell. Two of three clauses hold by construction (no analytics, no tracking); the third — "no third-party services beyond the sync endpoint" — is contradicted by the product itself: both shells name GitHub as the update-manifest host, the released rc.3 artefact set includes the latest.json the updater fetches, and the product's own attack suite (e10 §1g) ASSERTS exactly two remote hosts, github.com and the Vercel relay. This is not a Swift-vs-Tauri divergence (the reference shell hard-codes the github.com URL literally at main.swift:236; Tauri gets it substituted at release time) and it is not a missed tier-2 row — network-audit.dom.js §1 only asserts the *launch* made no off-origin request, which is compatible with a consent-gated updater firing later. Sharpening the auditor's note: the GitHub contact is opt-in and off on a fresh install — UpdaterPrefs::default sets disclosed=false (lib.rs:340) and update_fetch_manifest returns {ok:false,error:"disabled"} before building the updater when !disclosed || !enabled (lib.rs:501-504) — so a user who never consents on first run experiences the sentence as written; a user who consents talks to a second, disclosed third party. That supports PARTIAL rather than FAIL, and it is a catalogue-wording problem (21.4/21.5/N10 say "one endpoint", 22.3/22.8 require GitHub), not a code defect. Prior AUDIT.md:1223 reached FAIL on the same clause.

items.note: As literally written the solo clause is false on the shipped build: once the welcome card is dismissed (every fresh install), the Tauri shell makes a daily HTTPS GET to github.com for latest.json with nobody pressing anything, and a solo Mac may also POST one feedback report on a human press. The page itself makes zero requests (network-audit §1/§2, CSP), and the sync half — exactly one pinned origin, /api/v1/ paths only, no redirects, no cookies — holds in both shells. The PO amended 21.5 to 'zero UNREQUESTED requests' (ADR 003 §7.5, D10, 2026-09-03) but the catalogue v1.0 (2026-08-25) still carries the old wording, and even the amended wording names only the feedback exception, not the update check (AUDIT.md D-F, still open as wording). Note the tests/attack/e10-network-scope §5a 'fresh install … ZERO requests' row is true only while `disclosed` is false, i.e. before the welcome card is dismissed.

Chain, verified at HEAD ab00471: lib.rs:338-341 Default { enabled: true, disclosed: false }; main.js:605/641-645 the welcome card (shown whenever seenFirstRun is unset, i.e. every fresh install, solo included) calls discloseUpdateCheck() on dismiss; update-ui.js:348-357 → shell.setDisclosed(true); main.js:110-111 runLaunchCheck(); startDailyTimer() on every boot; update-ui.js:249-256 bare setInterval over updater.checkDaily(); lib.rs:498-528 opens a real socket via tauri_plugin_updater once both flags are true, with no OWNER-placeholder runtime refusal in the Tauri shell (grep finds none; the Swift shell has one at main.swift:603) and release.yml:143-153 substitutes the real GITHUB_REPOSITORY into the endpoint at build time, so the released DMG GETs a real github.com URL. defence.reason: The catalogue sentence at docs/v2/UX-AUDIT-CATALOGUE.md:237 reads "In solo mode the app makes zero network requests; with a Familienkreis it talks to exactly one sync endpoint and nothing else." The second clause holds in the shipped Tauri shell; the first is false as written, and the auditor's chain is correct file-for-file. The one thing that could have made the solo clause vacuously true — the OWNER/REPO placeholder endpoint in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json — is rewritten at release time to the real repository (release.yml:143-153), rc.3 carries a latest.json asset, and src-tauri/src/lib.rs has no OWNER-PLACEHOLDER refusal at all (only shell-macos/main.swift:603 does). So on the shipped build a solo Mac whose welcome card was dismissed makes a real HTTPS GET to github.com roughly daily with nobody pressing anything, plus a human-pressed feedback POST that the shell deliberately lets through with sync off. The project's own records agree: DESIGN-DECISIONS.md:305-330 (D10) says "21.5's 'zero' was false from the commit that landed it", AUDIT.md:1224 rates 21.5 FAIL, and traceability.json's 21.5 text was re-stated to name both the disclosed update check and the feedback press — but the catalogue v1.0 line still carries the old wording, and that is the sentence being audited. items.note: The shipped build is notarized, so a stranger's Mac simply opens it (verified by the CI spctl gate).
