defence.reason: The finding stands; PARTIAL is the right verdict and the auditor picked the right failing clause. Clause 1 ("a signed and notarized build simply opens") HOLDS on the shipped Tauri artefact: the rc.3 CI run executed the signed branch and release.yml's hard spctl gate demands `accepted` plus `source=Notarized Developer ID` on both the .app and the DMG. Clause 2 ("in the unsigned fallback, a first-run screen walks through the Systemeinstellungen unlock in two illustrated steps") FAILS on the word "first-run screen": the auto-show path in src/js/firstrun.js can only fire when the native shell answers a `gatekeeper_status` invoke with supported:true and blocked:true, and that command exists in neither the shipped Tauri shell (src-tauri/src/lib.rs invoke_handler) nor the reference Swift shell — a grep of both shells and tauri.conf.json returns nothing. probeHost() therefore returns supported:false and shouldAutoShow() returns false on every launch, so the screen never appears unasked. This is not an auditor misreading: the source file's own header (firstrun.js:31-39) says the automatic path is "dark", scripts/build-unlock-page.sh:16 says the same, and the tier-2 row that ran green against the real shell asserts exactly p.supported===false. What DOES exist is the two-step illustrated walkthrough as content (tier-2 row asserts 2 .unlock-step and 2 SVG .unlock-fig), reachable on demand from Settings (tier-2 row 'Settings offers the walkthrough forever') and riding on the DMG as "Bitte zuerst lesen.html" (release.yml step 'Put the unlock page on the DMG' success, gated at release.yml:580-582). Both shells agree, so this is not a shell divergence — it is an unimplemented bridge on both. Sharpening the auditor's note: (a) the release-notes sentence "Beim ersten Start führt die App durch die Freigabe in den Systemeinstellungen" is emitted UNCONDITIONALLY at release.yml:817/820 on both the signed and ad-hoc branches, so the published rc.3 notes promise a first-run walkthrough that the notarized build does not need and the fallback build cannot deliver; (b) firstrun.js:13-18 concedes that while Gatekeeper is blocking the app, no in-app screen can be on screen at all, so even a fully implemented probe would only cover the "already running but quarantined / staged-quarantine" cases — the DMG read-me is the only surface that reaches a blocked reader. Six prior ledgers (E1-VERIFICATION §4, E10-VERIFICATION, AUDIT.md:1131, MOM-TEST.md, RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:362, SHIP.md:307, FINDINGS.md:4094, STATUS.md:653) record the same residual; I re-verified it independently by grep and code-read rather than trusting them.

defence.reason: The auditor read the right files and the right shell. The catalogue sentence has two clauses. Clause 1 ("a signed and notarized build simply opens") holds: release.yml:613-632 is a hard gate that fails the release unless `spctl --assess --type execute` on the .app AND `spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature` on the DMG both return accepted with `source=Notarized Developer ID`, and rc.3 was published through that gate. Clause 2 ("in the unsigned fallback, a first-run screen walks through the Systemeinstellungen unlock in two illustrated steps") does not hold as a first-run SCREEN: the only automatic path is src/js/main.js:103 `maybeShowUnlock()` → firstrun.js:471 `probeHost()` → firstrun.js:117 `invoke('gatekeeper_status')`. So probeHost returns `supported:false` (firstrun.js:125-129 catch → `off`) and shouldAutoShow (firstrun.js:138) returns false unconditionally; the screen never appears unasked. The module's own header (firstrun.js:36-39) states this: "the automatic path is dark until LZP-107/108 implement gatekeeper_status", and scripts/build-unlock-page.sh:16 and docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1129-1132 say the same. items.note: Hint lives in exactly two places (App menu, settings) plus the ⚙ dot; no modal, no toast, no dock badge (asserted). Medium because the Tauri App-menu item has never been seen by a human or a test — the menu rows run against the Swift shell. One edge to record: the plugin's macOS install falls back to an AppleScript 'with administrator privileges' password dialog if the bundle is not user-writable (updater.rs ~1318) — a native prompt mid-'quiet' download; not reached for a user-dragged copy in /Applications.
items.text: An available update announces itself only as a quiet "Update verfügbar" hint (app menu and settings), never a modal; one click restarts into the new version, and simply quitting applies it on next launch.

items.text: Every device — my two Macs and Mom's — follows the same single release channel and converges automatically.

items.evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:588-606 — `install(bytes)` is reachable only with the Vec<u8> returned by `update.download()`; tauri-plugin-updater-2.11.0/src/updater.rs:740 `verify_signature(&buffer, &self.signature, &self.context.config.pubkey)?` inside download; lib.rs:1478-1482 the plugin refuses to init without `plugins.updater.pubkey`; tauri.conf.json:67 pubkey decodes to minisign key 592231D8A449B6AB (key id bytes abb649a4d8312259) and equals shell-macos/main.swift:242 UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY_B64; the published rc.3 latest.json signature decodes to key id abb649a4d8312259 (same key); release.yml:104-116 refuses to build without TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY, :750-787 verifies the .sig against the embedded pubkey before publishing ('Generate and verify latest.json' success); .github/scripts/make-update-manifest.mjs:97-106 dies on a non-verifying signature. items.note: Authentic-or-nothing holds by construction in the shipped shell: the only route to the bundle swap passes through the plugin's minisign check against the key baked into the binary, the CI pipeline cannot publish an unsigned or mis-signed archive, and the key in the published manifest is the key in the app. Not observed at runtime on a device (no update has ever been delivered), but every link is code or a run that succeeded.
trail: skeptic downgraded confidence → medium: Every link is real (lib.rs:588-606 passes only download()'s Vec<u8> to install(); tauri-plugin-updater-2.11.0 src/updater.rs:740 verify_signature inside download(); Cargo.lock pins 2.11.0; tauri.conf.json pubkey decodes to minisign key id abb649a4d8312259 = the key id in the published rc.3 .sig; release.yml:104-116 and :750-787 gate CI; make-update-manifest.mjs:97-106 dies on a non-verifying signature). But 'high' overstates it: the shipped shell's verifier has NEVER executed — Tier 0 only compiles lib.rs, no Tauri updater run exists, and no update has ever been delivered to any device. The only runtime 22.6 rows are a fake-port JS row (tests/tier2/update-ui.dom.js:243 mount({downloadError:'signature'}) — it tests the UI's reaction, not verification) and a Swift-shell row (tests/tier2/shell-updater.dom.js '22.6 — with no updater key configured…' asserts error 'no-updater-key', i.e. the Swift shell's no-key state, not the Tauri verifier). The published rc.3 signature is prehashed 'ED' (sig alg ED), which the Swift reference shell refuses by design (make-update-manifest.mjs:109-121) — so the one shell that has been driven in a WKWebView cannot verify the artefact that shipped, and the shell that can has never been run. Authentic-or-nothing holds by construction from read-but-unexecuted code, which under these ground rules is medium, not high.
items.text: Updates are cryptographically signed and verified before installing — a device installs authentic builds or nothing.

items.text: Updates never touch user data; migrations run after the swap; if a server change ever requires a minimum client version, outdated clients say so in one plain sentence instead of failing quietly.

items.evidence: Desktop half: .github/workflows/release.yml:47-52 `on: push: tags` → build universal bundle, sign, notarize, DMG, latest.json + .sig → `gh release create` (release.yml:839-846); `gh run list --workflow release.yml` shows run 34643379564 for v2.0.0-rc.3 success and `gh release view v2.0.0-rc.3` lists dmg, app.tar.gz, .sig, latest.json, SHA256SUMS.txt. Server half: .github/workflows/server.yml:5-11 'WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO, ON PURPOSE: it does not deploy … Vercel's own GitHub integration is the deployer — push to `main` becomes the production deployment'; its triggers are push:main with server/** path filters and deployment_status — no `tags:`; docs/v2/RELEASE.md:66-67,430 say the same. Nothing in release.yml touches or waits on the server.
items.clause: one tag moves the entire product — server and every desktop — forward together
items.note: Releases do flow from GitHub and one tag does move every desktop (three real runs, assets published). The server moves on push to `main` via Vercel's integration, independently of the tag: a tag on a commit not yet on main, or a main push without a tag, moves one half only, and no gate ties the two. Whether the Vercel integration is even connected cannot be seen from this machine. Supersedes docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1227's 'UNVERIFIABLE' (release.yml has now executed).

defence.reason: The auditor's failing clause holds, and the GitHub record shows the two halves actually diverging at the very tags cited. Desktop half: .github/workflows/release.yml is tag-triggered (lines 47-52) and contains no reference to the server at all (grep -i 'server|vercel|deploy|api/v1' over release.yml returns nothing); its only dependency is `needs: suites` = ci.yml `suites`, which runs npm test / test:property / test:attack (ci.yml:58-62), not test:server and no deploy. Server half: server.yml triggers are push:main with path filters, pull_request, deployment_status, workflow_dispatch (server.yml:47-66) — no `tags:` — and its header says it does not deploy (lines 5-11); Vercel's integration deploys on branch pushes, and the GitHub deployments API shows 0 of the last 100 deployments with a tag ref. Concrete divergence: (1) v2.0.0-rc.1 (ceb223d) and v2.0.0-rc.2 (b8cb2d2) both have green release.yml runs (34634176652, 34638216920) and published assets, but the deployments API returns 0 deployments for either sha — the server did not move at all for those tags. (2) v2.0.0-rc.3 (ab00471): release.yml run 34643379564 succeeded and published, while Vercel deployment 6401009074 for the same sha is state=failure ('Deployment has failed — run npx vercel inspect dpl_6CJMNzkdT4N8AmYnBhaocuWzyY1b'); the deployment_status run 34643383791 was skipped (state != success, so the smoke job never ran) and nothing turned red on the release. The tag shipped green while the same commit's server deployment failed, and no gate connected them. Production is unaffected only by luck: server/ has not changed since the last successful deploy 9a18a85 on 2026-09-05 (git diff --stat 9a18a85 ab00471 -- server is empty), and curl https://langzeitplaner.vercel.app/api/v1/meta still answers 200 from fra1 at protocol 1..1. Sharpening of the auditor's note: the Vercel integration IS visibly connected from this machine — deployments are created by vercel[bot] and server.yml's smoke job ran to success on deployment_status events on 2026-09-05 (run 33975872986, job 'Smoke test the deployment': success). That resolves their uncertainty in the direction that makes the finding firmer: a connected integration failed on the tagged commit and the tag's release did not notice. The traceability text for 22.8 (docs/v2/traceability.json:670-676) carries the same 'one git tag, and the entire product, server and every desktop, moves forward together' wording, so the catalogue clause is not a paraphrase drift. Desktop clause PASS, server-together clause FAIL, so PARTIAL is the right verdict.

defence.reason: The finding stands and is, if anything, understated. I tried to refute it three ways and each closed. (1) Mechanism: release.yml triggers only on `push: tags` (release.yml:47-52) and ends at `gh release create` (release.yml:839); it contains no step that deploys, waits on, or checks the server (grep for server/vercel/deploy in release.yml hits only the LZP_MIN_CLIENT_VERSION variable at lines 747-770). server.yml triggers on `push: branches: [main]` with path filters and `deployment_status` (server.yml:46-67) — no `tags:`. Vercel's GitHub integration deploys on push to main; nothing in the repository ties the two, and no test does either (no test or check script mentions server.yml; the only vercel mentions in tests/tier1/release-gate.test.js:274-354 concern the retired placeholder hostname). The documented procedure itself is two separate pushes — `git push` then `git push origin v2.0.1` (docs/v2/RELEASE.md:224-226). (2) Live behaviour on the shipped tag: the GitHub Deployments API shows the Vercel production deployment for ab00471 — the exact commit v2.0.0-rc.3 points at — in state `failure` ("Deployment has failed", deployment 6401009074, 2026-09-11T20:17:00Z), as is the one for 0296638 (6400792505). The last successful production deployment is 9a18a85b from 2026-09-05. The rc.1 and rc.2 tag commits produced no Vercel deployment at all (correct ignoreCommand skip — they touch no server file). So across three real tags, the server moved with the tag zero times; the release workflow went green and published anyway. (3) The one witness that could have caught it is blind to this case: the smoke job's `if:` requires `deployment_status.state == 'success'` (server.yml:174), so a failed deploy yields a run whose every job is `skipped` (run 34643383791), not a red run. Mitigation, stated honestly: `git diff --stat 9a18a85b ab00471 -- server/` is empty, so the code Frankfurt is running is byte-identical to the tagged server tree and users see no divergence today; production answers 200 from fra1 at protocol 1..1. But the clause is about the mechanism ("one tag moves ... server ... forward together"), and that mechanism does not exist; the first tag that carries a server change alongside a client change will expose it. The traceability text (docs/v2/traceability.json:670-676) is weaker than the catalogue sentence — "the sync server deploys from the same repository to Vercel" — and that weaker clause does hold; the catalogue compresses it into "one git tag ... moves forward together", which does not. Auditor's supersession of AUDIT.md:1227 (UNVERIFIABLE) is correct: release.yml has now run five tagged/dispatched times with success.
defence.evidence: Desktop half (holds): .github/workflows/release.yml:47-52 `on: push: tags: 'v[0-9]+...'`; :839 `gh release create "$TAG"`; `gh run list --workflow release.yml` → run 34643379564 v2.0.0-rc.3 success; `gh release view v2.0.0-rc.3 --json assets` → dmg, app.tar.gz, .sig, latest.json, SHA256SUMS.txt; `git merge-base --is-ancestor v2.0.0-rc.3 origin/main` → tag is on main (commit ab00471). Server half (does not move with the tag): .github/workflows/server.yml:46-67 triggers `push: branches: [main]` + path filters + `deployment_status`, no `tags:`; server.yml:5-11 "it does not deploy ... Vercel's own GitHub integration is the deployer"; release.yml contains no server/vercel/deploy step (grep hits only lines 747-770, the min-client-version variable); docs/v2/RELEASE.md:224-226 procedure is `git push` then `git tag` then `git push origin v2.0.1` — two independent pushes. No coupling test: `grep -n -i "server.yml|vercel" tests/tier1/release-gate.test.js tests/tier1/release-staging.test.js tests/tier1/dmg-contents.test.js .github/scripts/check-release-config.mjs` → only the retired placeholder-hostname rows (release-gate.test.js:274-354). Live evidence the tag did NOT move the server: `gh api repos/manuelhein2016-hash/langzeitplaner/deployments?per_page=8` → deployment 6401009074 sha ab00471c (the v2.0.0-rc.3 commit) env Production, and `.../deployments/6401009074/statuses` → state "failure", description "Deployment has failed — run this Vercel CLI command: npx vercel inspect dpl_6CJMNzkdT4N8AmYnBhaocuWzyY1b --logs"; deployment 6400792505 (sha 02966388) likewise "failure"; last "success" is 6282815039 sha 9a18a85b at 2026-09-05T15:47:33Z. No deployment exists for the rc.1 (ceb223d) or rc.2 (b8cb2d2) tag commits. Smoke witness blind to failure: server.yml:174 `if: github.event_name == 'deployment_status' && github.event.deployment_status.state == 'success'`; `gh run view 34643383791 --json jobs` → all three jobs "skipped". Mitigation: `git diff --stat 9a18a85b ab00471 -- server/` → empty (server tree unchanged since last successful deploy); `curl -si https://langzeitplaner.vercel.app/api/v1/meta` → HTTP/2 200, x-vercel-id fra1::fra1, {"region":"fra1","minProto":1,"maxProto":1}. Catalogue vs traceability wording: docs/v2/UX-AUDIT-CATALOGUE.md:250 vs docs/v2/traceability.json:670-676 ("the sync server deploys from the same repository to Vercel — one git tag, and the entire product ... moves forward together"). Prior audit superseded: docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1227 "22.8 UNVERIFIABLE — release.yml has never executed".

sections.section_notes:
Where the section lives: src/js/platform/updater.js (decision logic, 33 tier-1 rows), src/js/update-ui.js (the hint, the settings section, the 22.7 bar), src-tauri/src/lib.rs:182-633 + :1378-1413 + :1475-1535 (the shipped Tauri port: nine update_* commands, App-menu item, plugin init), src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:62-68 (endpoint placeholder + pubkey), .github/workflows/release.yml + .github/scripts/make-update-manifest.mjs (tag → signed DMG + manifest), .github/workflows/server.yml (server guard rails; does not deploy), src/js/firstrun.js (unlock screen), docs/v2/email/* (deliverable 28).

Cross-cutting findings:
1. Stale 'UNVERIFIED — never compiled' headers in lib.rs (:186-199, :418-423, :1478) and Cargo.toml (:31, :37, :47): CI's 'Tier 0 — the shell PRODUCTION ships actually compiles' job and the release job both build this crate (run 34643379564 success). The comments now mislead an auditor; docs/v2/AUDIT.md:1225-1227 ('22.1 UNVERIFIABLE', '22.8 UNVERIFIABLE', 'release.yml has never executed') and the AU-14 residual are superseded by three real release runs.
2. Channel state: every release is a prerelease, so `releases/latest/download/latest.json` returns 404 (curl, 2026-09-11). No device has ever received an update through the pipeline; 22.3/22.5 are verified as mechanism only. The first non-prerelease tag is the event that lights the channel — RELEASE-CHECKLIST should name 'watch one rc device converge on it' as an explicit step.
3. `gatekeeper_status` is implemented in neither shell (scripts/build-unlock-page.sh:16; lib.rs invoke_handler). The in-app first-run unlock screen can therefore never auto-show; the DMG read-me and the Settings entry are the only routes. Either implement the command (xattr com.apple.quarantine on Bundle.main) or amend 22.2's wording.
4. Copy drift after the D1 reversal: the mail's step 3, unlockLead/unlockNote and 'Bitte zuerst lesen.html' describe an unsigned wall the notarized build never raises, and the release notes say the app walks the user through the unlock on first start (it cannot). SHIP.md:288-291 records keeping it; worth a PO decision.
5. Literal wording: both 'one plain sentence' strings are two sentences (i18n.js:305 and the 22.7 bar text). Recorded under 22.7, not failed.
6. Tests that do not exist and should: (a) a tier-2/e2e row driving the Tauri shell's update_* commands — every tier-2 updater row runs in the Swift shell, so update_menu_hint's menu rebuild and update_restart's app.restart() have only ever been compiled; (b) a row asserting the endpoint the BUILT binary carries (release-gate §6e checks the pre-flight predicate, and 'The published manifest resolves' is skipped on prereleases); (c) a self-test that verifies the published latest.json signature against tauri.conf.json's pubkey post-publish (today only the key ids were compared here: both abb649a4d8312259).
7. items.evidence: src/js/family/familysettings.js:1117-1125 (`pw.type = 'password'`, label EXPORT_SHEET_COPY.withPassword 'Backup mit Passwort sichern'); src/js/crypto/backup.js:347-356; docs/v2/adr/002-crypto.md:1284. items.clause: No … passwords exist anywhere in the product
items.note: Accounts and e-mail addresses are genuinely absent (no field, no flow, no server column; 15.3/19.5 join and pairing are code-only). But the product ships an optional password: the family backup export sheet (⚙ → 'Backup erstellen') has an <input type=password> and a primary button 'Backup mit Passwort sichern', designed in ADR 002 §7.2/D8. It is a local encryption passphrase, not an account credential, and the sheet itself says 'notAnAccount'. The catalogue's own 19.5 ('there are no passwords in this product') and 21.B ('Kein Passwort') contradict ADR 002 — an erratum is needed, but against the catalogue's literal wording the absence does not hold.
trail: both defenders refuted → ABSENT-CONFIRMED

defence.reason: The auditor's decisive evidence — the `<input type=password>` and the primary button "Backup mit Passwort sichern" in the family backup export sheet — is code that no user of the shipped build can reach. `buildRecoverySection` (src/js/family/familysettings.js:1096) returns before drawing anything unless `hooks.recoveryMaterial` is a function (lines 1100-1101: `const material = typeof hooks.recoveryMaterial === 'function' ? hooks.recoveryMaterial : null; if (!material) return;`). The ONLY production caller of `buildFamilySections` is src/js/family/mount.js:191, which passes `{ onOptIn: ... }` and nothing else; a repo-wide grep for `recoveryMaterial` (excluding node_modules/.git/dist) hits only familysettings.js lines 151, 153, 1088, 1094, 1100 — no caller, no test, no shell ever supplies it, and `git log -S recoveryMaterial -- src/js/family/mount.js` is empty (mount.js never passed it). So in the Tauri build (tauri.conf.json:7-10 builds `dist` from `index.html` + `src` via scripts/build-frontend.mjs, `dist` is not git-tracked) the ⚙ sheet never contains a password field, a password prompt, or a "Backup erstellen" section; the auditor's "⚙ → 'Backup erstellen'" path does not exist on screen. The other password-ish hits are not passwords in the product: `exportBackup`/`importBackup` have no callers outside crypto/backup.js (settings.js:602-604 are comments; the v1 ⌘⇧E/⌘⇧I path in src/js/backup.js has no identity/passphrase handling, so even a with-identity file is never asked for a passphrase); lib.rs:283/294/307 are the macOS Keychain API for the device key; lib.rs:906/969, main.swift:1038/1094, net.js:254, updater.js:288, createjoin.js:699 REJECT URL credentials. The auditor's concession on accounts and e-mails stands (only "kein Konto / kein Passwort" copy at i18n.js:400/822, settings.js:652/810; tier-2 family-createjoin.dom.js row '15.3 — code paste, name, colour, done: no email, no password, no registration form' asserts `document.querySelectorAll('.circle input[type="password"]').length === 0` at line 414). Observed as stated, the absence holds. Two sharpenings, neither of which changes N1 today: (a) the absence is accidental — ADR 002 §7.2/D8 and FINDINGS.md:1637 ("P-4 … fixed … backup.js wired from family/familysettings.js") describe a passphrase sheet that is actually a second orphan (the P-4 row in tests/attack/privacy-e5-silence.test.js only measures import reachability, 13/13 pass at HEAD); the moment mount.js passes `recoveryMaterial`, N1 flips to ABSENT-VIOLATED against the catalogue's literal wording, so the erratum the auditor asks for (catalogue 19.5/21.B vs ADR 002 "not an account password") is still needed — but as a spec/catalogue reconciliation, not as an N1 defect. (b) The rendered Datenschutz screen (settings.js:783-794 DE, 918-929 EN) refers to "eine Sicherung MIT Passwort" / "nur eine Sicherung mit Passwort erspart dir das", describing an export the product cannot produce — a copy-accuracy defect belonging to 21.3, not a password existing.

defence.reason: The auditor's sole evidence for a password is the export sheet in familysettings.js:1117-1125, but that sheet is dead code in the shipped product. It is built only by buildRecoverySection (familysettings.js:1096), which returns before drawing anything unless hooks.recoveryMaterial is a function (line 1100-1101: `const material = typeof hooks.recoveryMaterial === 'function' ? hooks.recoveryMaterial : null; if (!material) return;`). The only production caller of buildFamilySections is mount.js:191-193, whose hooks literal is exactly `{ onOptIn: (origin) => optIn(origin, hooks) }` — no recoveryMaterial. The identifier `recoveryMaterial` occurs in no file in src/, tests/, shell-macos/ or src-tauri/ other than familysettings.js itself (grep, whole repo), and the single commit that introduced it (git log -S recoveryMaterial → 23af664) touched only familysettings.js. So the `<input type=password>`, the 'Backup mit Passwort sichern' button and the whole 'Backup erstellen' section are never rendered on any Mac, solo or family. It is also the ONLY password-typed input in the codebase (grep over src/ and index.html: familysettings.js:1121/1124 alone). The v1 ⌘⇧E export (src/js/backup.js) has no passphrase. The shell hits are the Keychain generic-password API (lib.rs:283-307, main.swift:1569) and URL-credential rejection guards (lib.rs:906/969, main.swift:1038/1094) — not user-facing passwords. Accounts and e-mail: the auditor already found them absent, and the tier-2 row 'family-createjoin.dom.js — 15.3 — code paste, name, colour, done: no email, no password, no registration form' asserts `querySelectorAll('.circle input[type="password"]').length === 0` (line 414) in a real WKWebView. The catalogue's literal wording ('no passwords exist anywhere in the product') therefore holds for the product a user can reach; the auditor cited a code path, not product behaviour. SHARPENING (a different, real defect, not N1): ADR 002 §7 / D8's recovery export — the thing 21.B's honesty moment tells the user to 'exportiere jetzt eins' — is unreachable in the shipped build; the comment at familysettings.js:1088 claiming mount.js passes recoveryMaterial is false. The catalogue-vs-ADR-002 wording tension the auditor raises is a doc inconsistency to record as an erratum, but it does not make the shipped product violate N1 today; if the export is ever wired, N1 must be re-audited.

Two solo-mode request paths exist in the shipped Tauri shell, and the second is stronger than the auditor stated: (1) Rueckmeldung POST — lib.rs sync_preflight step 4 lets POST /api/v1/feedback through with the sync switch OFF (human press only; PO ruling 2026-09-03, ADR 003 §7.5, D10/D10 EXTENDED). UpdaterPrefs defaults to enabled:true, disclosed:false (lib.rs:340); the first-run card's "Fertig" flips disclosed (main.js:645 -> discloseUpdateCheck), after which main.js:110-111 runLaunchCheck()/startDailyTimer() fire on every solo launch and daily, reaching github.com. e10 §5d pins this as intended behaviour (six launches with disclosed+enabled -> exactly 1 request). defence.reason: The finding stands on the shipped Tauri shell. Clause "solo mode = zero network" is false by design in two independent ways. (1) Feedback POST: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1077 (`if !SyncPrefs::load(app).enabled && !sync_solo_send_is_allowed(&canonical, &m)`) lets POST /api/v1/feedback through with the sync switch off; lib.rs:1012-1019 defines the carve-out. It is reachable in production, not just permitted: the relay origin is compiled in (lib.rs:749 `SYNC_ORIGIN_BUILTIN = "https://langzeitplaner.vercel.app"`, lib.rs:836-838), `sync_status` reports `originConfigured: true` regardless of the switch (lib.rs:1258-1266) and its own message names the exception ("mit einer einzigen Ausnahme: eine Rückmeldung, die Sie selbst abschicken", lib.rs:1276-1282), so `bindSoloSender` binds (src/js/feedback/relay.js:186-209) via the dynamic door to platform/net.js (relay.js:225-233). (2) Updater: lib.rs:498-512 `update_fetch_manifest` opens a socket to github.com (tauri.conf.json:64-66, substituted at release.yml:150) once `p.disclosed && p.enabled`; the page-side gate (src/js/platform/updater.js:621-649) has no solo/family distinction and honours launch AND daily timer checks after opt-in (shouldCheck, updater.js:424-437), so an opted-in solo Mac makes unattended daily GETs — a network monitor would see them. Catalogue 22.3 itself mandates this for "every device", so N10's "zero network" was internally inconsistent with 22.3 on the catalogue's own date, independent of LZP-1009. The other clauses hold: no ads/analytics/tracking — CSP connect-src 'self' (tauri.conf.json:28), exactly one page-side network call site and exactly two sanctioned remote hosts (tests pass, see evidence); no cookies (privacy-e5-metadata.test.js:148-156). The product mitigates by warning in Settings ('px zu niedrig'), and the tier-2 suite documents the trade rather than forbidding it (density-808 §8 header quotes v1's 'never scrolls vertically'). 1.B's mechanism ('vertical fit … by row density') is a user setting, not automatic. defence.reason: The auditor's evidence is accurate and the finding survives; I could not find any code path, shell setting, or tier-2 row that prevents vertical scrolling of the board. The product's own source treats vertical scroll as a designed, warned-about state rather than an impossibility, and two facts sharpen the finding beyond what the auditor cited: (1) src/js/find.js:388-392 actively scrolls .board-wrap vertically (`wrap.scrollTop -= …` / `+= …`) with the comment "Dense settings can make the board taller than the window — track the hit vertically too", i.e. the Find feature is built on the assumption the board scrolls vertically; (2) both presets allow rowHeight up to 32 (layout.js:90 and :103 `maxRowHeight: 32`), and 31×32+88 = 1080 px exceeds the shipped default window height of 900 (tauri.conf.json:17), so even the default-size window scrolls vertically at the slider's own ceiling — no unusually small window is required. The two shells agree on the minimum window (Swift main.swift:2052 `minSize = NSSize(width: 900, height: 640)`; Tauri tauri.conf.json:19 `minHeight: 640`), so this is not a shell divergence; the shipped Tauri build is the one under judgement and it permits 640 px, below the 770 px that Kompakt at its default needs (settings.js:308 `need = 31*rowNow + 26 + 62`). The only clause that holds is the narrow one: at the shipped defaults (Kompakt 22 px, 1440×900 window) the board needs 770 px and fits, and density-808 §8 asserts exactly that default is not warned about (row 'v1§2/kompakt-at-its-default-is-not-warned-about-on-this-window'). But the catalogue sentence says "never", and the mitigations — a Settings warning ("px zu niedrig", settings.js:311-315), a hint that names the height budget (settings.js:293-295), and a prior audit (docs/v2/E9-VERIFICATION.md:398-402) conceding "v1 does not treat that one as a trade („the board never scrolls vertically")" — all document the violation rather than remove it. No tier-2 row asserts overflow-y is hidden or that scrollHeight <= clientHeight; dom-rendering.dom.js:432-446 asserts the opposite (header pins while the wrap scrolls vertically) whenever the viewport is short enough. Verdict remains ABSENT-VIOLATED; if the PO wants a defaults-only reading, the right shape is an erratum to 1.B/N16 ("does not scroll vertically at default density in a window ≥770 px tall"), not a pass.

defence.reason: The finding stands and I could not refute any part of it. N16 is absolute ("The board never scrolls vertically", docs/v2/UX-AUDIT-CATALOGUE.md:272, pointing at 1.B line 24 which promises fit "by row density, truncation, and popovers"). The shipped product (a) permits vertical scroll in CSS, (b) has no auto-fit mechanism — row height is a user preset (22/26 px) clamped only to a floor, never to the window; there is no ResizeObserver or resize handler on the board, and neither shell resizes the window to fit; (c) ships a minimum window height (640 px, identical in Tauri and Swift, so the shells do not disagree) that is 130+ px below what even Kompakt needs (31·22+88 = 770 px of board-wrap alone); and (d) its own tier-2 suite, which PASSED at HEAD in a real WKWebView, contains a row whose non-vacuity cell REQUIRES that at least one density configuration make need > have in that window (i.e. the board really does overflow vertically), and the product's response to that overflow is a warning paragraph in Settings, not prevention. The code comments in settings.js and density-808 explicitly name this as "the one v1 forbids". The auditor did not read the wrong shell (both shells set 900×640, both cited), did not misread a clause, and did not miss a contrary tier-2 row — no test asserts the absence of vertical scroll; dom-rendering's 1.4 row even asserts the header pin WHILE scrolling vertically. Sharpening: the violation is a deliberate, documented trade (warning text names it and tells the user to enlarge the window or pick Kompakt; headers stay pinned), so the fix path is either overflow-y:hidden + automatic density fit, or an erratum on 1.B/N16 restricting "never" to "at the default density in the default 1440×900 window" — as the auditor already suggested. On the default window at Kompakt 22 the board does fit (the §8 cell 'kompakt-at-its-default-is-not-warned-about-on-this-window' passed), so a narrowed sentence would be PASS; the sentence as written is ABSENT-VIOLATED.
defence.evidence: CSS permits it: src/css/app.css:209-212 `.board-wrap { flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-x:auto; overflow-y:auto; }` — only print.css:66 overrides (to `visible`), and only under @media print. No auto-fit: src/js/layout.js:85/93 `rowHeight: 22` / `26` are fixed presets; src/js/layout.js:551 `const rowH = Math.max(dp.minRowHeight, s.rowHeight || dp.rowHeight)` clamps to a FLOOR only; src/js/board.js:281 `setVar('--row-h', model.rowH)` and :601 `rows.style.height = 'calc(var(--row-h) * 31)'` derive the board height from that preset, never from the viewport. `grep -rn "ResizeObserver\|clientHeight\|innerHeight" src/js` → only legend.js:398 (legend width), settings.js:307 (the warning), popover.js:187 (popover placement); `grep -n resize src/js/main.js` → no matches. Shells: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:16-19 width 1440 / height 900 / minWidth 900 / minHeight 640; shell-macos/main.swift:2052 `window.minSize = NSSize(width: 900, height: 640)` — identical, and neither shell calls set_size/setContentSize (grep over lib.rs and main.swift: only setFrameUsingName at main.swift:2058). 640 < 770 (=31·22+88 needed at Kompakt, src/js/settings.js:308 `need = 31 * rowNow + 26 + 62`, with --head-h 26 / --pad-h 62 at src/css/app.css:45-46). Product's own admission: src/js/settings.js:294-301 comment "THE HALF OF THE TRADE 17.7 DOES NOT MENTION, AND THE ONE v1 FORBIDS … §1's design note is blunt: „The board never scrolls vertically."", followed by :309-316 which, when `need > have + 1`, appends a `.warn` paragraph "Dieses Fenster ist N px zu niedrig … müssen gescrollt werden" / "This window is N px too short … have to be scrolled to". No prior ledger covers it: `grep -rn "1\.B\|N16" docs/v2/*.md tests/COVERAGE.md` (excluding the catalogue) → no matches.

defence.reason: The clause the auditor failed is "no family, account, or network PROMPTS of any kind", and the auditor's own note concedes the only thing they found "informs, it does not prompt". A prompt asks the user to decide or enter something; the welcome card asks nothing about network. I opened the shipped code path: src/js/main.js:603-647 maybeFirstRun() builds exactly one .coach card containing an h3 (firstRunTitle "Willkommen"), a p (firstRunBody: click-and-type / drag a bar), an optional p (firstRunState: Bundesland missing), an optional p.hint (updateCheckHint) and two buttons — "Bundesland wählen" (opens settings) and "Fertig". There is no input, no toggle, no yes/no, no question attached to the update sentence; the sentence (i18n.js:165-166, en 617-618) is declarative: "Einmal täglich fragt die App, ob es eine neuere Version gibt. Dabei wird nichts über dich übertragen — dein Board bleibt offline." The user cannot accept or refuse anything on the card; the refusal control (update switch) and the request control ("Jetzt suchen") live in Settings → Updates, which is where 22.3/21.5 put them. So no network prompt exists on first run. Family and account: nothing on the card references either; the only family entry point is the settings-sheet button (i18n.js:334 circleCreateBtn 'Familienkreis erstellen'), and the pure-node guards prove first run reaches no family/crypto/net module and arms nothing — I ran them myself at HEAD (see evidence). Nothing on the wire before the user acts either: update-ui.js:229-240 runLaunchCheck → updater.js:626-628 returns {ran:false, reason:'not-disclosed'} before touching the port, and the shipped Tauri shell independently refuses at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:502 and :557 (`if !p.disclosed || !p.enabled` → "disabled", updater.check() never called; default disclosed:false at lib.rs:340). The Swift reference shell gates identically (shell-macos/main.swift:568, :653), so the tier-2 rows that passed in WKWebView describe the shipped behaviour too; and tauri.conf.json:26 `withGlobalTauri: true` means `window.__TAURI__.core.invoke` exists in the DMG, so the production card is the same card tier-2 saw (update-ui.dom.js:541-549), not a browser-preview variant. The auditor read the right files and misclassified a disclosure as a prompt. Sharpening for the ledger, not for N18: dismissing the card via EITHER button (main.js:639-645 dismiss() → discloseUpdateCheck()) flips the 21.5 flag, after which the 30-minute daily poll (main.js:111 startDailyTimer → update-ui.js:249-256 → updater.js dueForCheck with lastCheckAt 0) and every later launch will make the one update request in solo mode. That is solo-mode network ACTIVITY and belongs under 15.1 / 21.5 / N10 / 22.3 — where the catalogue is internally in tension (22.3 mandates the check, 21.5 says zero solo requests) — but it is not a prompt and does not fail N18. Also note the "Fertig" click is treated by the code as acknowledgement of the sentence (comment main.js:641-643), and E1-VERIFICATION.md:121 records that the card is deliberately the only surface a fresh install has for that disclosure; if the PO wants first run to carry no network-related text at all, that is a design change to request, not a catalogue violation. Verdict: PASS.

items.text: Sharing is never a side effect — no action other than the explicit visibility control (or a category default the user configured) ever exposes an entry. *(16.1, 16.4)*

All tier-1/attack files cited were run at HEAD ab00471: network trio 82/82, repeats+palette 127/127, visibility/unshare/authz/leak/silence 354/354.

Four catalogue errata are needed, because the catalogue (2026-08-25) predates PO rulings or contradicts the ADRs: (1) N10/21.5 — the PO reworded 21.5 on 2026-09-03 to 'zero UNREQUESTED network requests' (docs/v2/STATUS.md:366-374, AUDIT.md:619-650, LZP-1009 solo feedback POST at lib.rs:1012-1019) and 22.3's opt-in update check reaches a second host (github.com); N10 is violated only in wording. (2) N1/19.5/21.B — ADR 002 §7.2 designs an optional backup passphrase ('Backup mit Passwort sichern', familysettings.js:1117-1125); 'no passwords' is true of accounts, false of the export sheet. (3) N4 — three settings lines show hh:mm timestamps (settings.js:412, syncstatus.js:645/690, update-ui.js:524/544); 11.A says 'list of 7 dates'. (4) N16/1.B — .board-wrap is overflow-y:auto with fixed row heights (app.css:209-212), the shipped minHeight is 640 px (tauri.conf.json) against ~770 px needed at 22 px rows, and the product's own copy (settings.js:288-290) and tier-2 density-808 §8 treat vertical scroll as a warned trade, not an impossibility.

Residuals in prior ledgers this section touches: docs/v2/AUDIT.md D10/21.5 (CLOSED by ruling), privacy-e5-silence §4 'P-2' (documentation of the release host — now asserted present in server-metadata.md), e7-leak-downgrade FINDING E7L-2 (→Privat on a cursor-behind Mac emits no retraction; a 16.5 gap, adjacent to N8), crypto-relay-read length side-channel ≥140 bytes (16.7, adjacent to N12). Shipped-shell specifics: the Tauri shell (lib.rs) has no notification plugin, no dock badge API and no native dialog beyond file open/save (lib.rs:1305-1330); update_menu_hint (439-450) only rebuilds the App menu.

Tests I would want that do not exist: a tier-2 row asserting the board fits without vertical overflow at the shipped minimum window size (or a CSS rule making .board-wrap overflow-y:hidden with density auto-fit); a tier-2 row scanning board+toolbar text for hh:mm patterns; a tier-2 button scan (like sync-status.dom.js:104-117) that runs with the family settings sheet open, so N2 is asserted over the whole settings surface rather than prose rows.

1.1.text: When I open the app, I see the current month plus the next 11 as vertical day columns on one screen, so the whole planning horizon is visible without any clicks.

1.2.text: Each day is a slim row with date and weekday abbreviation (Mo–So) and weekends shaded, so the board reads like the printed Jahresplaner I'm used to.

1.3.text: I can switch from rolling mode to a pinned start month (e.g., always January), so I can also use it as a classic year calendar.

1.4.text: If the window is narrower than 12 columns (13" MacBook), the board scrolls horizontally with month headers pinned, so small screens degrade gracefully instead of shrinking to unreadable.

1.5.text: In pinned mode I can page year-back/year-forward, so retained history (8.4) is actually reachable, not just theoretically stored.

1.6.text: Rows align by day number (01 at top, like the PDF), so columns compare cleanly even though weekdays shift.

1.A.text: Month columns carry headers in the reference format (e.g., `August '26`); months shorter than 31 days leave their bottom rows empty. *(src: v1 §5)*

1.B.text: The board never scrolls vertically; vertical fit is achieved by row density, truncation, and popovers. *(src: v1 F1 notes)*

1.C.text: Rolling vs. pinned is a settings-level mode; year-paging controls are visible only in pinned mode. *(src: v1 F1 notes)*

1.D.text: First launch in solo mode opens directly onto the usable (empty) board — no wizard, no account prompt, no setup steps. *(src: Principle 7, A10)*

2.1.text: I click any day, type, and hit Enter to save — Escape cancels — so capturing a note takes seconds and never opens a dialog.

2.2.text: I click an existing note to select it, double-click it (or press Enter while selected) to edit it in place, and clear its text or hit ✕ to delete it, so maintenance is as fast as creation. *(click model fixed in v1 §15)*

2.3.text: A day can hold more than one note (with graceful truncation on narrow columns), so busy days don't force compromises.

2.4.text: A crowded day shows the first two notes plus "+n"; clicking expands a popover with the full stack, so narrow columns never silently hide entries.

2.5.text: Notes cap at ~80 characters, truncate with ellipsis, and show full text on hover — keeping rows thin is what keeps 12 months on one screen.

2.A.text: Notes render in their category's color on the board. *(src: v1 F2 notes)*

2.B.text: The day popover offers full note texts with in-place edit and delete, and shows each note's category. *(src: v1 F2 notes)*

2.C.text: In v2 the popover additionally contains the sharing cluster: the three-state visibility control, the co-edit flag, and the attribution line. *(src: A7)*

3.1.text: I press a start day and drag to an end day to lay down a colored bar, so vacations and project phases go on the board in one gesture.

3.2.text: A bar crossing a month boundary splits across the two columns but stays one entry (same color, label shown once per segment, edit either part edits the whole), so real ranges aren't broken by the layout.

3.3.text: I can give a bar a short label shown on or beside it, so every stripe is self-explaining.

3.4.text: Overlapping bars render in parallel lanes within the day rows, so simultaneous things (project + vacation) stay readable.

3.5.text: Dragging upward (end before start) just normalizes — no error state for a natural gesture.

3.6.text: A bar reaching past the visible horizon gets a "continues →" cue and grows back into view as the board rolls, so long projects are never clipped silently. Mirrored for bars starting before the view.

3.7.text: A bar's label renders once per month segment with full text on hover, so six-month stripes stay labeled without clutter.

3.8.text: Parallel lanes cap at 3 per day; further overlaps compress into a "+n" marker with tooltip, so extreme weeks stay legible.

3.A.text: While a bar is being dragged or resized, lane assignment stays stable — no mid-gesture reshuffling of other bars. *(src: v1 F3 notes)*

3.B.text: Creating a bar shows a live preview of the range during the drag, before release. *(src: v1 §12 deliverable 5)*

4.1.text: I manage a legend of categories (rename, recolor, add, remove) that starts with a sensible default set (Arbeit / Familie / Reisen / Deadlines), so it works out of the box but fits my life.

4.2.text: Every note and bar belongs to a category, defaulting to the last one I used, so entries come out colored without extra clicks.

4.3.text: I toggle a category's visibility in the legend, so I can isolate e.g. Work when planning around deadlines.

4.4.text: Deleting a category with entries prompts me to reassign them ("Move 23 entries to …?"), so nothing vanishes as a side effect.

4.5.text: Colors come from a fixed palette of ~10 distinguishable, print-safe tones instead of a free picker, so the legend stays readable on screen and paper.

4.6.text: Creating an entry whose category is currently hidden auto-unhides that category with a brief flash, so a new entry can never disappear the moment I make it.

4.A.text: In v2 the legend has two sections — *Meine Kategorien* (personal, never synced) and *Familie* (members) — and categories remain a private organizational system. *(src: A3)*

5.1.text: I drag a note onto another day to reschedule it, so replanning is one motion instead of delete-and-retype.

5.2.text: I drag a bar as a whole to shift it while keeping its length, so sliding a vacation one week later is a single move.

5.3.text: I grab a bar's start or end edge to stretch or shrink it, so adjusting durations is direct.

5.4.text: Z undoes / ⇧⌘Z redoes my recent changes (~50 steps), covering create, edit, move, resize, and delete — so no drag or delete is ever scary. Import is excluded; it has its own confirmation instead. In family mode, undo covers only my own actions (18.4).

5.5.text: Click selects a note or bar (Esc deselects, Delete removes); drags only start past a small pixel threshold (~4 px), so clicking to edit never turns into an accidental move.

5.6.text: Dragging near the board's edge auto-scrolls horizontally, so a note can be dragged from August into a month that's currently off-screen.

5.A.text: Entries expose the full state set: default, hover, selected, editing, dragging (ghost at origin + preview at target), and resize handles on selected bars. *(src: v1 §10)*

5.B.text: The cursor communicates the action: default / grab / grabbing / row-resize over bar edges. *(src: v1 F5 notes)*

5.C.text: There are no invalid drop targets — dropping is always allowed on any day. *(src: v1 F5 notes)*

6.1.text: German public holidays appear inline next to their date in a distinct style, so the board matches the paper original.

6.2.text: I pick my Bundesland once in settings, so regional holidays (Fronleichnam, Allerheiligen …) show correctly.

6.3.text: The holiday data is baked into the app for any year, so it works fully offline with zero sync.

6.4.text: I can toggle the layer off, so it never competes with my own entries when I don't need it.

6.5.text: Holidays are computed from rules (fixed dates + Easter arithmetic + Buß- und Bettag rule), not from a lookup table — so this layer literally never runs out of data, forever, offline: any pinned year, past or future, shows correct holidays.

6.6.text: A "show other Bundesländer dimmed" toggle reproduces the PDF's union view — my state's holidays strong, everyone else's muted (two distinct visual weights).

6.A.text: When user content covers a holiday's text, the user entry wins the space but the holiday stays discoverable (marked day + tooltip). *(src: v1 F6 notes)*

6.B.text: The Bundesland selector offers all 16 states plus "nur bundesweite Feiertage". *(src: v1 §13)*

7.1.text: Schulferien for my Bundesland appear as subtle background shading behind the day rows, so school-free periods are visible without stealing attention.

7.2.text: Hovering (or tapping) the shading reveals which break it is (Herbstferien, Osterferien …), so the shading is never cryptic.

7.3.text: The layer toggles independently of public holidays, so each layer can be on or off on its own.

7.4.text: Ferien are published only ~2–3 years ahead — the bundled dataset has a visible horizon ("Ferien-Daten bis Sommer 2028" in settings), beyond which shading is simply absent; the dataset refreshes through the normal app-update channel (F22), never a separate download. *(A11)*

7.5.text: With no Bundesland selected, the layer stays off, and toggling it prompts for the selection first.

7.A.text: The four ambient backgrounds — plain day, weekend, Ferien, weekend-within-Ferien — are all visually distinguishable while staying quieter than any user content. *(src: v1 F7 notes, §10)*

8.1.text: Today is unmistakably highlighted, so I can orient myself instantly.

8.2.text: In rolling mode the board advances by itself at the month change — oldest column out, new twelfth in — so I always face the next 12 months without maintenance.

8.3.text: A "Today" button jumps me back to the current day from wherever I've scrolled, so exploring next summer is never a one-way trip.

8.4.text: Entries that roll out of view are kept in storage, not deleted, so history survives and reappears if I pin an earlier start month; family entries remain part of that history only while I'm a member. *(A9)*

8.5.text: Date changes while the app is running — midnight passes, or the Mac wakes from sleep days later — update the today marker and trigger the month-roll live, no restart needed.

8.6.text: The roll itself is a brief, subtle slide animation (~300 ms), so the leftmost column leaving is comprehensible rather than a glitch.

8.A.text: The Today marker reads clearly against every other highlight (weekend, Ferien, selection) as the board's single permanent accent. *(src: v1 F8 notes, §10 hierarchy)*

8.B.text: With macOS "Reduce Motion" enabled, the roll (and all other animations) become instant swaps. *(src: v1 §15)*

9.1.text: A "repeats yearly" checkbox on a note makes it reappear on the same date every year, so birthdays survive the roll into the next year.

9.2.text: Repeating notes carry a small ↻ marker, so I can tell recurring from one-off at a glance.

9.3.text: Editing or deleting a repeating note applies to the whole series, so there's exactly one object to maintain — no exception logic.

9.4.text: A Feb-29 repeat shows on Feb 28 in non-leap years, so leap-day birthdays never skip a year.

9.5.text: A series exists from its first year onward — paging back before its creation year shows nothing, matching reality.

9.6.text: Repeats apply to notes only; bars stay one-off (annual events with movable dates would silently land wrong).

9.A.text: The repeat toggle lives in the note's edit state / popover, not on the board surface; the ↻ marker sits before the text so it survives truncation. *(src: v1 F9 notes)*

9.B.text: A repeating series can be shared; its visibility is series-level (the whole series is Privat/Belegt/Geteilt — no per-year exceptions), so Oma's birthday is entered once and visible to everyone, forever. *(src: A4)*

10.1.text: Each month column has a small free-text area beneath it, so undated thoughts ("book cabin?") live next to the month they belong to.

10.2.text: Scratchpad text persists and autosaves like everything else, so it's a real part of the board, not a sticky note that vanishes.

10.3.text: I can drag a scratchpad line onto a day to turn it into a dated note, so vague plans can graduate into real ones.

10.4.text: Pads belong to a *specific* month — Aug '26 and Aug '27 are different pads; new months arrive empty, old pads persist into history.

10.5.text: A pad grows to ~5 lines then scrolls; print includes only non-empty pads.

10.A.text: Pads read visually as margin, not day content, and support native text editing incl. its own text undo. *(src: v1 F10 notes)*

10.B.text: Scratchpads remain private in v2 — they never sync to the family. *(src: A5)*

11.1.text: Every change is saved locally within about a second, with no save button anywhere, so I never think about persistence.

11.2.text: One click exports my entire own state — private entries, my shared/Belegt entries with their flags, categories, settings, and my identity keys — as a single JSON; the file is the recovery artifact and says so in its header; other members' entries are never included. *(A2)*

11.3.text: Importing a JSON restores my data — and re-joins my Familienkreis when the keys are present — after an explicit "replace current board?" confirmation, so recovery is one action and never an accident. *(A2)*

11.4.text: Data lives as one human-readable JSON in Application Support, written atomically, so even a crash mid-save can't corrupt the board.

11.5.text: The app keeps the last 7 daily snapshots with one-click restore, so yesterday's bad idea is recoverable even after undo history is gone.

11.6.text: The data file carries a schema version and newer app versions migrate it automatically, so updating the app never strands data.

11.7.text: Export uses the native save dialog with a dated default name (`LangzeitPlaner-2026-08-01.json`).

11.A.text: Snapshot restore lives in settings as a list of 7 dates with a restore action behind a confirmation. *(src: v1 F11 notes)*

12.1.text: One click opens a clean A4/A3 landscape print view in the style of the schulferien poster, with my entries on it, so the plan can still end up on a wall.

12.2.text: The print view hides all UI (buttons, legend controls) and keeps entry colors, so the paper version looks designed, not screenshotted.

12.3.text: Printing respects the current layer, category, and (in v2) member toggles — what I see is what prints. *(A8)*

12.4.text: Printing goes through the macOS print dialog — "Als PDF sichern", paper size, and scale-to-fit come free and native.

12.A.text: The whole board prints on one landscape page; the Today highlight is excluded from print. *(src: v1 §15)*

12.B.text: Truncated content prints truncated (paper has no hover); only non-empty scratchpads print. *(src: v1 F12 notes, 10.5)*

13.1.text: A normal Dock app with a single window that remembers size, position, and scroll offset across launches.

13.2.text: A menu-bar icon focuses/opens the window with one click — a settings toggle, default on, with a monochrome template glyph.

13.3.text: A launch-at-login toggle in settings, so the board is just always there.

13.4.text: superseded by A1. Audit as 21.5: solo mode makes zero network requests; family mode talks to exactly one sync endpoint.

13.5.text: W hides the window while the app keeps running; ⌘Q quits; reopening from the Dock is instant with full state.

13.6.text: Every core action has a shortcut — audited item-by-item as 13.A–13.J below.

13.7.text: UI language is German by default, with an English toggle in settings; switching translates the full UI while German content terms (Feiertage names, Ferien names) remain German.

13.I.text: Enter / Esc — commit edit & step through find hits / cancel, deselect, close find or popover.

13.K.text: The macOS menu bar carries the standard structure with these entries: App (About, Einstellungen ⌘,, Beenden ⌘Q) · Ablage (Exportieren ⇧⌘E, Importieren ⇧⌘I, Drucken ⌘P, Fenster schließen ⌘W) · Bearbeiten (Widerrufen/Wiederholen, text editing, Suchen ⌘F) · Darstellung (Heute ⌘T, Feiertage ⌘1, Schulferien ⌘2, Modus Rollierend/Fixiert) · Fenster/Hilfe standard. *(src: v1 §9)*

13.L.text: Settings contains, findable in one surface: Bundesland selector (6.B) · layer defaults · rolling vs. pinned mode · language DE/EN · launch at login · menu-bar icon on/off · snapshot restore (11.A) · Ferien data horizon display (7.4) — plus, in v2: the *Familie* section (create/join, members, admin panel, sync detail, device pairing) and the *Datenschutz* section. *(src: v1 F13 notes, A10)*

14.1.text: F opens a slim search field; matching notes and bars light up while everything else dims (~30 %); Enter steps through hits, ⇧Enter backwards, with a "3/17" counter; Esc restores the board. Search covers note texts, bar labels, scratchpads — and, in v2, family entries (shared text, Belegt owner names). *(v1 §15, A6)*

14.2.text: Search also covers rolled-out history, listing off-screen hits as clickable results.

14.A.text: Find is an overlay state of the board, never a separate screen. *(src: v1 F14 notes)*

15.1.text: By default I'm in solo mode and nothing has changed from v1 — no account, no network activity, no prompts; the family features exist only behind an explicit "Familienkreis erstellen / beitreten" entry point in settings.

15.2.text: I create a Familienkreis with a name ("Familie Weber"), automatically become its admin, and receive a shareable invite code, so setup is one screen.

15.3.text: Mom joins by pasting the invite code into her app and choosing a display name and a personal color — no email, no password, no registration form — so a non-technical family member gets in within a minute.

15.4.text: All members see the member list (name, color, initial), so everyone knows who's in the circle.

15.5.text: Invite codes are single-use, expire after 7 days, and are revocable by the admin, so a leaked link can't haunt the family.

15.6.text: I can change my display name and color anytime and it propagates to everyone's boards, so identity stays current without admin involvement.

15.A.text: The join flow is one screen with a large paste field; it prevents choosing a color already taken by another member. *(src: v2 F15 notes)*

16.1.text: Everything I create is private by default — joining a family changes nothing about existing or new entries until I explicitly share them — so oversharing is structurally impossible.

16.2.text: Every note and bar has one of three visibility levels: Privat (only me), Belegt (others see that the range is taken, and by whom, but no text), Geteilt (others see everything) — so I can coordinate without disclosing.

16.3.text: I change an entry's visibility with a three-state control in its selected state and popover, two clicks maximum, so privacy management never feels like administration.

16.4.text: A personal category can set a default visibility for *new* entries in it (e.g., category "Familie" ⇒ Geteilt), so routine sharing costs zero extra clicks while the global default stays private.

16.5.text: I can change visibility at any time; a downgrade removes the entry (or its details) from other members' boards at the next sync, so nothing shared is shared forever.

16.6.text: My shared and busy entries carry a small badge on my own board, so I always see my exposure at a glance and never have to wonder what Mom can see.

16.7.text: A Belegt entry appears on others' boards as a neutral block with my color/initial and the word "Belegt" — duration and owner are deliberately visible, the content deliberately not — so "I'm away, don't plan with me" works without explanation.

17.1.text: Shared and Belegt entries from other members appear on my board automatically in their date rows, so family plans live exactly where my plans live.

17.2.text: Color logic: my entries always render in my category colors; others' entries render in the member's personal color with an initial chip ("M") — so "whose is this?" is answered before "what is it?".

17.3.text: The legend's member section lets me toggle each member's visibility, so I can hide Papa's entries the same way I hide a category.

17.4.text: Family entries obey all v1 density rules — lanes cap, "+n" overflow, truncation — so a busy family can never break the board's legibility.

17.5.text: Entries added or changed by others since my last session carry a quiet "neu" dot that fades once I've seen them — no popups, no counters, no push — so I notice change the way I'd notice new ink on a wall calendar.

17.6.text: Hover/popover shows attribution: "von Mama · geteilt · geändert So.", so provenance is one glance away but never printed on the board.

17.7.text: A per-device density setting (Kompakt / Komfort) slightly increases row height and font size on that machine only, accepting horizontal scroll as the trade.

18.1.text: By default only the owner can edit or delete an entry; other members view — so nobody's plans can be rewritten behind their back.

18.2.text: An entry-level flag "Familie darf bearbeiten" opts one entry into co-editing, so collaboration exists exactly where invited and nowhere else.

18.3.text: As admin I can *unshare* any entry from the family space — it reverts to owner-private, it is never deleted — so moderation is non-destructive, and I still can't read what was never shared.

18.4.text: My ⌘Z undoes only my own actions; other members' changes never appear in my undo stack.

18.5.text: If two people edit the same co-editable entry near-simultaneously, the later change wins per field, attribution updates, and only the person whose in-flight edit lost sees a quiet one-line inline notice that dismisses itself.

18.6.text: Deletions propagate to all boards; my undo of my own deletion restores the entry as a new shared operation.

18.A.text: The co-edit flag sits next to the visibility control in the popover as one "sharing" cluster. *(src: v2 F18 notes)*

19.1.text: The app is fully functional offline — create, edit, move, everything — and queues changes locally; sync happens when connectivity returns, so a train ride never interrupts planning.

19.2.text: My changes upload within seconds of saving; others' changes arrive automatically — on app focus and every ~30–60 s while the app is open. There is no sync button and no manual refresh anywhere.

19.3.text: Sync status is silent when healthy; only pending-offline or a real error produces a small, unobtrusive indicator.

19.4.text: I can pair my own second Mac: my entire board — including private entries — syncs end-to-end encrypted between my devices only.

19.5.text: Adding a device means entering a short pairing code shown on an existing device — not a password-reset flow; there are no passwords in this product.

19.6.text: After long offline periods everything merges cleanly on return — including month rolls and yearly repeats that occurred meanwhile — so a laptop opened after three weeks just catches up.

19.A.text: Pairing has designed screens on both ends (show code / enter code) with both-ends confirmation. *(src: v2 F19 notes, deliverable 21)*

20.1.text: As admin I can invite, revoke invites, remove members, rename the space, and transfer the admin role to another member.

20.2.text: Removing a member deletes their shared/Belegt entries from all family boards and their access — their private data on their own machine is untouched.

20.3.text: Leaving voluntarily has the same effect, self-initiated; other members' shared entries disappear from my board, my own entries all revert to private and stay with me — nobody ever loses their *own* data by leaving.

20.4.text: As admin I can delete the entire Familienkreis: server data is purged, every member reverts to a fully intact solo board.

20.5.text: Even as admin, I structurally cannot see other members' private entries or the contents of their Belegt entries — enforced by encryption, not by policy.

20.6.text: Each user belongs to at most one Familienkreis, so the mental model stays as simple as the family it serves.

20.A.text: The admin panel is a section inside settings, not a separate console; removal/leave/delete confirmations state their consequences in one plain sentence. *(src: v2 F20 notes)*

21.1.text: Shared and Belegt entries are end-to-end encrypted; only member devices hold keys — the server stores ciphertext it cannot read.

21.2.text: Private entries never leave my machines except end-to-end encrypted to my *own* paired devices — no family key can ever decrypt them.

21.3.text: The app documents plainly what the server side *can* see — pseudonymous IDs, timestamps, IP addresses in transit, encrypted blob sizes — and names the processors (Vercel, Prisma Postgres; EU/Frankfurt region), so trust is informed, not marketed.

21.4.text: Still no analytics, no tracking, no third-party services beyond the sync endpoint.

21.5.text: In solo mode the app makes zero network requests; with a Familienkreis it talks to exactly one sync endpoint and nothing else. *(supersedes 13.4)*

21.A.text: A "Datenschutz" section in settings carries this in human German, not legalese. *(src: v2 F21 notes)*

21.B.text: Family onboarding contains the honesty moment: "Kein Passwort. Dein Backup ist dein Schlüssel — exportiere jetzt eins," making key-loss consequences plain and prompting an immediate backup export. *(src: v2 §3, deliverable 24)*

22.1.text: The app ships as a single DMG small enough to attach to a normal email; installing is open → drag to *Programme* → launch; the same email carries the download link as fallback.

22.2.text: First launch handles macOS quarantine gracefully: a signed and notarized build simply opens; in the unsigned fallback, a first-run screen walks through the Systemeinstellungen unlock in two illustrated steps.

22.3.text: The app checks for updates on launch and roughly daily, downloads quietly in the background, and applies on the next start — after the first email, nobody ever downloads anything manually again.

22.4.text: An available update announces itself only as a quiet "Update verfügbar" hint (app menu and settings), never a modal; one click restarts into the new version, and simply quitting applies it on next launch.

22.5.text: Every device — my two Macs and Mom's — follows the same single release channel and converges automatically.

22.6.text: Updates are cryptographically signed and verified before installing — a device installs authentic builds or nothing.

22.7.text: Updates never touch user data; migrations run after the swap; if a server change ever requires a minimum client version, outdated clients say so in one plain sentence instead of failing quietly.

22.8.text: Releases flow from GitHub: one tag moves the entire product — server and every desktop — forward together.

22.A.text: The update hint is a dot in the quiet-signal family, not a badge count. *(src: v2 F22 notes)*

22.B.text: The invitation email is itself part of the experience: subject, three install steps with a screenshot, the invite code, the fallback link. *(src: deliverable 28)*

N1.text: No accounts, emails, or passwords exist anywhere in the product. *(15.3, 19.5, v2 §3)*

N2.text: No save button, no sync button, no manual refresh, anywhere. *(11.1, 19.2)*

N3.text: No dialogs for creating or editing entries — dialogs appear only for destructive or rare actions (delete category, import, restore, leave/remove/delete space). *(v1 Principle 2)*

N4.text: No times of day anywhere — dates only; consequently no timezone or DST behavior exists to audit. *(v1 §13, v2 §8)*

N5.text: No reminders, notifications, or push of any kind. *(anti-goals; v2 §11)*

N6.text: No popups, badge counts, or attention-demanding signals for family changes or available updates — only quiet dots. *(17.5, 22.4, 22.A)*

N7.text: No read receipts, no presence indicators, no "seen" states — in either direction. *(Principle 9)*

N8.text: No notification or trace when someone changes an entry's visibility — downgraded entries are simply no longer there ("no snitch mechanics"). *(v2 §6)*

N9.text: No comments, reactions, or chat on entries — the board is not a messenger. *(v2 §6)*

N10.text: No ads, analytics, tracking, or third-party calls beyond the single sync endpoint; solo mode = zero network, verifiable with a network monitor. *(21.4, 21.5)*

N11.text: No spinners or loading states on the board itself. *(v2 F19 notes)*

N12.text: No role — including admin — can access another member's private entries or Belegt contents. *(20.5)*

N13.text: No per-year exceptions on repeat series, and no recurrence beyond yearly notes (no weekly/monthly, no repeating bars). *(9.3, 9.6)*

N14.text: No free color picker — only the fixed palette. *(4.5)*

N15.text: Nothing is ever deleted by the passage of time — rolling removes from view, never from storage. *(8.4)*

N17.text: No UI copy ever promises "live" sync. *(v2 §3)*

N18.text: Solo first-run contains no family, account, or network prompts of any kind. *(15.1, Principle 7)*

N19.text: Sharing is never a side effect — no action other than the explicit visibility control (or a category default the user configured) ever exposes an entry. *(16.1, 16.4)*

N20.text: No per-member visibility ("share with Mom but not Papa") — the circle is the unit of trust. *(v2 §8)*
